# Owned-client activation and reload feasibility R6

**One PID-specific AppleScript activation and an original/full-work/original reload sequence passed actual focused capture guards.** No shader performance claim.

Human authorized AppleScript for the owned Minecraft client and requested retained scripts. The System Events activation attempt in R5 timed out; its outcome remains unverified and was not retried. The retained wrapper now uses direct AppKit `NSRunningApplication` PID lookup and one `activateWithOptions:0` request. It checks session ownership, exact PID/birth/argv, sole Minecraft process, readiness and one attempt per session; nil/terminated/prohibited applications fail closed. No activation-policy, permission or system-preference changes are made.

Retained helpers: [Python wrapper](../../scripts/dev_client_ui.py), [direct activation](../../scripts/dev_client_focus.applescript), [optional Iris UI actions](../../scripts/dev_client_ui.applescript). Example: `python3 scripts/dev_client_ui.py --session /absolute/owned/session focus`. Keep these files for reuse. The helper does not retry or continuously steal focus.

R6's actual owned process53692 accepted the one activation request. After warmup, actual named receipts independently recorded focused/fullscreen native1920×1200, no Iris fallback, empty option queue, main present, helper false and expected core/native maps in all three arms: original398/coreOff →full-work400/coreOn →original398/coreOff. [Feasibility receipt](../../dev/logs/cross-shader-performance-r3/unbound-cloud-shadow-persistent-r6/feasibility.json).

Pack transitions used a parent-backed-up PRIVATE iris.properties selection followed by existing normal Apply Off→On→Off. Pinned Iris reload initializes and loads disk config. This is an existing control/reload path, not an Iris UI operation. Actual resulting loaded archive/options/core were checked after each transition. Parent restored the exact original private Iris config backup for return. External config edits are not owned by the mod transaction and remain the parent's recovery responsibility. No unrelated configuration, worlds, licenses or scripts were deleted.

The client was stopped exactly and no owned clients remained before the next sequence. Focus in other workloads, future OS behavior, arbitrary private→private transitions, full lifecycle restoration, quality and speed remain unverified. R7 adds the same one-time activation before each fresh client's existing capture; all original acceptance gates remain unchanged.

## Historical local campaign snapshot — retained evidence only

The following describes the completed November 1–2 campaigns. Its CLOSED/BLOCKED/EXCLUDED labels apply to those finite searches, not the current 16-candidate audit. Do not use it to exclude C02 or stop the current task.

**The resumed shortlist search has reached its stopping condition: ten goals closed and G02 blocked.** Fresh independent Astra/medium reviews support the finite pinned local searches. G02’s viable routes are complete; the remaining Reimagined and Unbound originals cannot start natively on the current runtime, including with ShaderLOD absent. C02 is excluded. No candidate is newly qualified for default enablement.

**Scheduling:** sustained optimization and review requested on 2026-11-01 for G01–G10 and C01 is finished, with the scoped G02 blocker retained. C02 is excluded. The shortlist contains twelve entries total, eleven after that exclusion. Final evidence: `dev/experiments/shortlist-closure-20261101/checkpoint.json`. Historical quick-test pause is superseded by this request.

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`--gl-context native` preserves Minecraft's normal context request. For explicit
desktop API coverage, maintained comparisons also accept `3.2`, `4.3`, `4.5` and
`4.6`. These request real GLFW contexts; they do not override reported versions
or capabilities. Explicit requests disable NeoForge's reusable early window in
the owned profile, with the normal configuration backup/CAS/restoration contract.
The returned desktop version must meet the requested minimum and is recorded in
`summary.json.gl_context`. A driver returning4.6 for a4.5 request is labeled4.6;
it does not supply an independent4.5 result. Keep actual context/configuration
cohorts and their native baselines separate. Frozen Bliss qualification retains
its existing native-context protocol and refuses an explicit context override.
`--expected-renderer 'RTX 5080'` additionally refuses a ready client on a different
GPU, including a hardware integrated GPU. It validates the observed renderer
before scoring; it does not select the GPU or change personal driver settings.

`--performance-stack optimized` selects the exact pinned ModernFix, FerriteCore
and ImmediatelyFast tuple for G03 and its matched original-only startup/baselines or byte-identical native controls.
Default remains `minimal`. Other private/frozen protocols reject this override.
Preflight verifies every optional JAR, launch uses the maintained stack selector,
and runtime readiness checks the actual loaded module versions before scoring.
Optional artifacts are frozen operation inputs. Keep stack cohorts separate;
selecting the tuple is not proof that G03 compiled, executed, or helped.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

Windows ownership JSON reads and atomic publication retry transient sharing errors
for at most three seconds, including CRT EACCES/EPERM errors that lack a Windows
error number; persistent denial still fails the operation. Normal
configuration restoration includes the five numbered FML backups for each
ShaderLOD client config. For an older interrupted report that omitted these
paths, `recover --output REPORT --preserve-generated-backups` retains newly
created known backups in that report before checking the complete original
profile map. Existing backups and unknown files retain normal ownership checks;
recovery never replays measurements.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

C02 is an explicitly labeled 2×2 bloom quality tradeoff, with Master-On native
controls; its scoped exception is documented in the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md#c02-experimental-bloom-shading-rate).

## Choose the check for the question

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |
| Does this change activate and recover? | `check` | Performance or visual equivalence |
| Is the idea worth more investigation? | `test`, then `report` | Broad workload/machine qualification |
| What does native do without ShaderLOD? | `baseline` | Installed-Off overhead by itself |
| Does it preserve motion or work across packs/hardware? | Candidate-specific protocols in the reference | Coverage of untested scenes, transitions or machines |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep
workload performance, compatibility breadth, quality, or a quick screen. Reuse
the supported commands above. Put the chosen claim, comparator, coverage, useful
metrics, controls and budget in the existing experiment record. Record exclusions
and fallback separately; do not impose a universal repetition count or payback
horizon. Performance requires actual-window execution and valid output evidence,
not merely enabling a setting. Source changes do not inherit earlier timings.

## Records and milestone cleanup

Keep current work in STATUS, durable attempts/decisions in EXPERIMENTS, supported
procedures here and specialized routes in BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES. Extend the existing
candidate entry when adding a route; retire superseded wrappers only after checking
imports, tests and historical reproduction dependencies. Keep active experiments in
`dev/experiments`, reusable inputs/clients in `dependencies` and `run-workloads`,
and retained historical evidence in `experiment-evidence`. Do not move a pinned
active path just to satisfy this layout.

After an investigation, preserve compact raw measurements, configuration/source
identity, conclusions and any images/motion needed to support the claim. Remove
owned disposable intermediates once dependencies and restoration are checked;
there is no background cleanup requirement. For old camera sequences, put a
nonempty `.storage-retire` file beside the frames only after recording the reason
and retained evidence location. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py prune-captures`
previews exact eligible files; `--apply` uses the existing ownership/restoration
checks. Age alone is not permission to discard motion evidence. `.storage-keep`
on an ancestor protects a subtree. Unknown or still-needed evidence stays intact.


## Cost-map diagnostic checkpoint

Offline commands never launch a client; live diagnostics stay outside scored A/B:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py profile-plan --fps 60 --seconds 20 --windows 3 --processes 2 --cadence 4 --scope-sets 7
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py profile --input /absolute/path/capture.json --output /absolute/path/new-report
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py profile-report --input /absolute/path/capture.json --output /absolute/path/new-report
```

`profile --input` imports an existing schema-1 canonical cohort.
`profile --live --profile MANAGED_CLIENT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --seconds 8 --output FRESH`
launches an owned native 2560×1600 Asahi client in the prepared authored save,
captures CPU/GPU records, exercises an Iris reload, exports each cohort and restores
configuration and the whole save. Capture duration is bounded to 1–30 seconds;
startup/world loading are separate bounded phases. `--dh` enables pinned owned JAR
staging; `--dh-transition-check` explicitly tests rendering off/on with API override
restoration. Generation/radius/mode/distance remain the existing effective inputs unless the
explicit steady workload request described below owns generation=false.
The report is diagnostic, not an A/B performance or readiness qualification.
`profile-report` regenerates offline exports. Output must
be a new directory; existing finalized output is never overwritten. Legacy
unversioned `report.json` is read and labeled duration-only without inventing
endpoints. `profile-plan` estimates regularly active observations per scope set
using `floor(fps * seconds * windows * processes / cadence / scope_sets)` and exits
1 below `--minimum` (default 100). It does not inspect a live slot or qualify overhead.

CSV/JSON/HTML and separate CPU/GPU trace exports preserve missing values. Elapsed
GPU data has no timeline positions; uncorrelated GPU timestamps never share a CPU
trace. Cost labels and inclusive hierarchy are nonadditive. See
[COST_MAP_IMPLEMENTATION](COST_MAP_IMPLEMENTATION.md) for exact implemented scope,
test evidence and remaining stage 2–4 work. No four-pack capture study is implied.


Cost-map live coverage additions (2026-11-08): `--scene horizon` and `--scene water`
select saved poses 12/13 in the same authored world and retain a separate native
screenshot before timers start. `--workload steady` explicitly owns a temporary
DH generation=false API override and restores the prior API value (including
absence); it does not guarantee queues have drained. `--workload streaming`
labels the request without clearing caches, moving the camera or enabling generation.
The default `observed` preserves the generation policy. Reports distinguish the
request from actual task/queue evidence; loading during a steady request stays
visible. Generation-disabled rendering cannot establish generation cost.

`task-costs.csv` reports CPU wall/thread task distributions; `dh-tasks.csv` retains
individual intervals, thread identities, failures and requested upload bytes.
Tasks are window-owned and nonadditive with render-frame scopes. Readiness uses
fresh world-list uploaded VBO containers wholly beyond the vanilla distance square,
not submissions alone. It establishes residency, not visible pixels or complete
horizon coverage. Four-pack mixed labels and limits: [DH catalog](COST_MAP_DH_CATALOG.md).

# Agent operations

## Choose and bound the operation

[STATUS](STATUS.md) alone owns current scope, authorization, allocation and last
observed state. Use `python3 scripts/project_checkpoint.py show docs/STATUS.md`;
read linked goal sections relevant to the task. Maintenance does not resume a
paused or unobserved runtime campaign.

For an existing-concept port, name the working implementation, missing joins and
actual selected public consumer. Prepare the changed consumer and authentic
caller inputs together, then bind the integrated artifact. For an optimization,
identify active native work and take an early matched original/control/enabled/
return cost and quality observation. An inactive effect is coverage, not a gain.
Use [EVALUATION](EVALUATION.md) for the claim; a manual preview or control increment
does not require every historical performance protocol first.

Put the relevant assignment details in the worker message or existing attempt;
no new form or launch gate is required:

- **Outcome:** family/version/loader/dimension, preset, selected consumer and next
  user-visible result; for work reduction, native → selected active work.
- **Reuse:** working implementation, pinned inputs and valid unchanged evidence.
- **Ownership:** exact files/worktree, dependencies, exclusive resource owner,
  allowed actions and report destination.
- **Acceptance:** authentic input and real entry point, checks and evidence limits.
- **Budget and handback:** review/stopping boundary covering setup, workers,
  repairs and handoffs; changes, actual checks, evidence and exact owned processes.

Rank hypotheses by active removable work, likely total benefit, uncertainty,
effort and visual risk. Batch cheap independent defects with saved inputs and
[preflight](EXPERIMENT_PREFLIGHT.md); stop diagnostic work when the actual consumer
answers the question. The parent targets the next useful result and explains the
main delay across preparation, rendering and evaluation. Repeated same-cause
failure or an overrun of the roughly 15-minute auxiliary review budget calls for
a simplify/justify-extension/switch decision. If uncertainty remains, use one
bounded independent proceed/change/park review, with no execution or allocation
authority; do not add a standing supervisor. Preserve healthy allocated work and
closed negative trials.

## Assignments and integration

Partition by remaining dependencies, not automatically one worker per shader.
Shared API/resource repairs have one owner and one integration. Keep authentic
caller preparation with consumer ownership through handback; do not accumulate
patches awaiting unassigned caller work. Parent accepts actual artifacts/checks,
with selective independent review when a consequential uncertainty remains.

Repository role briefs under `.codex/agents/` describe domain responsibilities;
use [the runtime adapter](T3_AGENT_RUNTIME.md) for actual availability, dispatch,
review rounds, worktree setup and cancellation. A child handback does not finish
the parent outcome or transfer a client lane.

## Client, build and GPU ownership

Astra/medium leads decisions, delegation and acceptance. A named Sol/high executor
owns each authorized machine operation end to end: operational planning,
implementation, tests, diagnosis,
routine repairs, restoration, verification and cleanup. Keep one owner per shared
runtime machine through that entire operation, including quiet measurements. The
lead hands over the authorized resource and outcome once, then accepts evidence
or resolves a change of scope, budget or risk; it need not execute each test or
repair. This supports a single Sol executor running operations sequentially as
well as independent executors on different machines. A role assignment does not
transfer an existing live lane: arrange an explicit handoff after its current
owner verifies release. Historical root-only allocations remain history, not a
permanent root-only testing policy.

Choose storage admission for the actual operation before preparing inputs.
General world/profile copies retain their 32 GiB floor; a finite recipe with an
explicit smaller report/copy allowance propagates that allowance through the
common storage helper. Read-only analysis, small source checks and cleanup do not
inherit an unrelated game-launch reserve. Routine in-scope repair stays with the
machine owner; retain useful recovery inputs and report a genuine change of
scope or an unrecoverable resource conflict to the lead.

Before launch, reconcile actual availability with the last observation. Record
hardware, component pins, scene, command, session, PID/birth/argv, finite deadline
and exact stop procedure. Use existing `scripts/dev_client.py` supervision and
exact-client stop APIs where supported; never kill by broad process name.
Remote hosts and allowed actions come from current STATUS authority.

Mac development launches default to hidden background windows so they do not
interrupt the user. Do not automatically focus, show, maximize or enter fullscreen.
The launcher disables the early splash before startup and retains configuration
backups. Hidden/background rendering is diagnostic evidence, not qualified
foreground performance evidence; the existing timing checks stay strict.

Quiet measurements exclude source edits, builds, tests, encoders and unrelated
CPU work unless the protocol permits them. An untimed control operation can
release independent source preparation when its owner permits it. Do not change
a live freeze or reinterpret its quiet contract. Verify exact termination and
save/lock release before reporting the lane free. Analysis follows the operation's
executable restore/verify/release path without consuming its recovery allowance.

Build success, startup, in-world rendering, DH terrain, active feature consumption,
quality and speed remain separate evidence. Record hardware/OS; one platform does
not qualify another. Use [benchmark storage](BENCHMARK_STORAGE.md) for capacity/
retention and the [finite speed caller](RENDERER_BRACKET_CONSUMER.md) for supported
tuples. Adoption uses the actual normal producer, compiled resource and caller,
with the current receipt rather than an old staged patch. Keep final freeze/
preflight/deadline stamping/launch in one local operation once callers are ready.
Version-specific builds use their documented executables.

For maintained non-Photon adapters, use the builder's `--sync-resources` preview
and explicit `--apply`; do not hand-copy recipes into ten builds. See
[verified commands and limits](DEVELOPMENT_THROUGHPUT_REVIEW_20261012.md).

## Checkpoints, reports and handoff

Update managed STATUS at meaningful milestones with actual evidence, next action,
owners/jobs and unchanged allocation/authorization. Use
`python3 scripts/project_checkpoint.py` show/lint/update with the observed prior
SHA; inspect `--help` for update arguments. Preserve the typed schema and exact
history; do not append a competing current block or refresh time as progress.
Record an outcome once and link its evidence; active lesson summaries link the
preserved historical episodes.

Before handoff record exact owned jobs, stop path and next executable action.
After resume verify actual workers/jobs/artifacts before acting. Keep one stdout
reader per operation. Distinguish an attempt closing from Full completion using
actual terminal metadata. For elapsed-time reports distinguish preparation,
active render/evaluation time and waiting, and name the main delay; do not present
process health as a measured result. Runtime continuation semantics live in
[the adapter](T3_AGENT_RUNTIME.md).

# Benchmark window observations

`WorkloadSession` now adds `window_state` to its report. The read-only tracker
samples once per existing workload tick during warmup and capture: three GLFW
window attributes (`FOCUSED`, `ICONIFIED`, `VISIBLE`) plus cached Minecraft window
dimensions, framebuffer dimensions and pacing options. It does not query GL,
read pixels, pump events, invoke host commands, or alter focus, visibility,
resolution, pacing or shader settings. No new render/pass hook is added.

This can distinguish observed focus/visibility/size changes from apparently
matched endpoints. It does not establish a cause for frame-rate differences.
GLFW visibility does not prove that another window is not covering the game,
and these observations do not measure host clock frequencies, thermal state,
GPU utilization or window-server scheduling.

## Report schema

`window_state.schema` is `1`; `source` and `note` describe the observation method
and limits. `warmup` and `capture` each contain:

- `observations`, `available_observations`, `unavailable_observations`.
- `start` and `end`: first/last observed boundary, containing
  `elapsed_workload_seconds`, `frame_id` and `state`. No observations leaves these
  null/absent; a missing phase is not a confirmed stable window.
- `focused`, `iconified`, `visible`: each has `true_observations`,
  `false_observations`, `unknown_observations`. Unknown is separate from false.
- `window_size_counts` and `framebuffer_size_counts`: maps of `WIDTHxHEIGHT` to
  observation counts; nonpositive cached dimensions use `unknown_or_nonpositive`.
- `transition_counts`: counts by changed field, independently of the detail cap.
- `transitions`: up to 128 chronological changes, each with
  `elapsed_workload_seconds`, `frame_id`, `changed_fields`, `from`, `to`.
  Further detail events increment `dropped_transitions`; aggregate counts remain.
- `unavailable_reasons` and `max_observation_gap_seconds`.

Boundary and transition `state` fields:

```json
{
  "availability": "available",
  "focused": "true",
  "iconified": "false",
  "visible": "true",
  "window_width": 1280,
  "window_height": 720,
  "framebuffer_width": 2560,
  "framebuffer_height": 1440,
  "pacing": {
    "pause_on_lost_focus": false,
    "fullscreen": false,
    "configured_framerate_limit": 260,
    "vsync": false
  },
  "note": "GLFW attributes and cached Minecraft sizes"
}
```

Flags are strings `true`, `false`, or `unknown`. A missing handle or unavailable
GLFW call reports `availability: unavailable`, explicit unknown flags and a
reason; it does not manufacture an unfocused/hidden state. Cached dimensions and
options can still be present when native attributes are unavailable. Fullscreen
is Minecraft's window flag; the frame-rate value is the configured option, not
the actual rate or proof that an OS limiter is inactive. The tracker does not
read GLFW's error queue or infer success from timing counters.

At the warmup→capture tick, the same single window read becomes the capture start
sample. It is not counted twice. First and last samples bracket observed ticks,
not every rendered frame. Times are relative to workload construction and use
the existing workload monotonic timestamp; no extra CPU/GL timing queries are
introduced. Normal sampling is roughly the existing client tick rate. A brief
focus/size change between ticks can be missed; a pause can leave a sampling gap.
Counts are observation counts, not elapsed-time fractions. A stationary cached
framebuffer size while iconified is not proof of active rendering.

The report addition is telemetry only. It does not introduce benchmark rejection
rules or retroactively classify older reports without `window_state`. The
benchmark assessment worker and coordinator own exclusion/interpretation policy.

## Checks and runtime evidence

`WindowStateTrackerTest` uses pure synthetic observations; it never calls GLFW
or creates a window. It checks separate warmup/capture counts, known/unknown
flags, logical versus framebuffer dimensions, pacing and size transitions,
phase boundaries, observation gaps, immutable snapshots, backward-clock rejection
and the 128-detail cap while retaining all transition counts.

The tracker and fixture compile/run independently against the pinned LWJGL Java
classpath. The coordinator owns the full development build and subsequent
runtime verification. Successful fixture checks do not establish actual GLFW
state sampling or overhead in a running game; record those separately once a
completed workload report contains the new field.

# ShaderLOD-next: agent-first porting plan

Status: implementation of packages A–D and lightweight agent development exercises authorized by Philip on 10 November 2026. Benchmark redesign (E), optimization research/workflow proof (F), and high-level skills/shared agent operations (G) remain deferred. Live work requires a currently available compatible machine; an unavailable allocation is a partial state, never a synthetic substitute. Current implementation and verification status is maintained below.

## 1. Outcome and settled constraints

The goal is a short, reliable development loop: inspect measured expensive work, state a plausible mechanism, implement one optimization through a supported extension, verify activation and correctness, measure through the maintained harness, iterate, then close with scoped evidence. More checks, instructions, or generated code are not success by themselves.

Philip's latest decisions govern this plan:

- Preserve `/home/philip/ShaderLOD` and the lowercase historical checkout. Leave historical evidence there. Refactor selected behavior into next; do not transplant its candidate graph or clean up the old repositories.
- Next may be substantially rebuilt, but remains local-only with no remote/push. Keep small reversible commits and preserve unrelated edits.
- Start with Complementary Reimagined and DH on a compatible first machine. Add shaders and hardware gradually. DH absence must still be safe; enabled-DH behavior is part of the first intended product.
- Include native shader selection, config, Apply/Off/Cancel/recovery, and the basic machinery for developing and loading NEW optimizations. All old candidates remain parked. Do not port auto-tuning, unrelated loader/version targets, or old campaign launchers.
- Preserve original archives, effective native settings, resolution and AA. Unsupported combinations must remain explicit; do not silently lower settings to obtain a pass.
- Ban comments/docstrings in owned code. Refactor unclear code into understandable types, names, and responsibilities. Do not merely move excuse-laden comments into decisions. Preserve required attribution through narrow exceptions; shader directives are executable syntax, not comments.
- Root-only instructions; `CLAUDE.md` references `AGENTS.md`. No arbitrary instruction byte cap. One findings index if it remains useful, with accepted results showcased in README and other findings separately accessible.
- Agents work autonomously within the authorized task. Routine tests, check repairs, bounded recovery, and safe resource reclamation do not require repeated approval. New goals, destructive operations, unsupported scope changes, and weakened acceptance semantics do.
- No hosted CI/PR/review bureaucracy is required. Local verification must stand on its own. Actual benchmark methodology remains a later design task; this plan specifies interfaces and integrity requirements only.

The hierarchy for every recurring problem is: eliminate the bad state through architecture; encode the invariant in types/API behavior; verify it with tests/static checks; use a tool or skill for operational procedure; use instructions for the remaining judgment. A new rule must explain the failure it prevents and the legitimate path it leaves available.

1. A typed optimization module contract, generated registration, activation witnesses, and add/remove extension tests.
2. Explicit owners for configuration transactions, runtime lifecycle, artifact publication, and disposable workspaces; recovery is part of their APIs.
3. One versioned wire contract with Java/Python conformance fixtures and closed decoding at boundaries.
4. A fast CPU feedback lane and a complete closure lane; trustworthy incremental reuse and actionable diagnostics.
5. A bounded runtime execution interface shared by verification, profiling, and later benchmarks; structured status, cancellation, recovery, and resource accounting.
6. Managed storage classification and safe reclamation before resource failure becomes a blocker.
7. One current plan, one findings index, immutable evidence references, and generated/validated accepted-result presentation.
8. An explicit optimization workflow tying candidate selection to observed cost and scope; end-to-end rehearsal before claiming agent readiness.

### Remove

1. Text/filename bans that infer raw output, plans, GPU allocation, or architectural ownership from common words.
2. The hard instruction-size cap, seven-finding limit, and exact global test-name list.
3. Mandatory hosted CI/CODEOWNERS artifacts and personal review of every test/check edit as completion requirements.
4. Stage-number literals in runtime refusal logic; missing capabilities should be reported by capability, not migration numbering.

6. Stale MakeUp-first/four-shader-first instructions and per-piece approval stops.
7. Rejected candidate source, hooks, registrations, and fixtures that no longer protect shared behavior from the active tree after closure and preservation.

1. Keep a comment ban, but distinguish comments from shader preprocessor syntax, licenses, string data, and digest-pinned third-party inputs.
2. Keep one owner per durable value; do not turn the result publisher into the only package allowed to perform any I/O.
3. Keep required-test/no-skip guarantees; make suite obligations and behavior IDs stable while normal test discovery grows.
4. Keep self-tests, but rerun expensive tool specimens when their inputs change and at explicit clean verification, not blindly on every edit.

8. Keep source parity and CPU-before-live gates, but make them executable progress gates within authorized work rather than requests for Philip's attention.

## 4. Product boundaries and source refactor

Remain in one Gradle project unless a demonstrated classpath/packaging problem requires a later change. Keep the number of concepts small. Names below are responsibilities, not a mandate for a class per noun.

| Boundary | Owns | Must not own |
|---|---|---|
| Pure domain/contracts | Pack/candidate identities, settings, supported/unsupported decisions, immutable operation values | Game classes, filesystem, GL, process launch |
| Pack provider | Exact source identity, semantic binding, capability requirements, supported extension sites | Other pack providers or runtime execution |
| Optimization module | One mechanism, applicable capability/pack constraints, changed resources, activation evidence requirements | Shared engine dispatch, direct settings writes, evidence verdicts |
| Application transaction | Prepare/apply/observe/commit/restore state transitions and one current selection | Pack-specific algorithm branches |
| Iris/DH/NeoForge adapters | Pinned hook seams, actual runtime observations, necessary thread-affine mutations | Statistical conclusions or fallback fabrication |
| Development instrumentation | Bounded collectors, missingness/health, runtime control and profiling export | Shipping product activation policy |
| Host runner | Process/profile ownership, storage preparation, ordered requests, cancellation, recovery | Pack algorithms, direct construction of positive verdicts |
| Evidence publisher/analyzer boundary | Validated finalized records and derived reports respectively | Rewriting raw observations or mutating live settings |

Classify compiled outputs and use package visibility and narrow interfaces to prevent accidental access. Architecture tests cover all classes, forbidden edges, cycles, and forbidden concrete adapters. Explicitly mark intentionally empty components during the skeleton stage; require nonempty coverage when the corresponding slice lands. Standard ArchUnit checks are preferable to accumulating custom regex approximations.

### Optimization extension contract

Each candidate lives in one module directory with a stable ID, supported input identities/capabilities, parameter schema, targeted measured work, transformation or runtime behavior, and test fixtures. Generated registration drives selection/config/UI and development discovery. Unsupported input is a typed refusal with a reason; recognition is not qualification.

Start with the smallest transformation path that pinned Iris can actually support. Spike and verify the integration seam before freezing its API. Do not promise in-memory GLSL rewriting without proving the seam. A derived archive is acceptable if originals remain immutable, generated identity is distinct, and apply/recovery is transactional. New mechanisms may legitimately require a reviewed engine capability; “no common-engine edits” applies to another candidate using an existing capability, not every imaginable optimization.

Separate requested, prepared, linked, observed-active, and restored state. UI toggles or successfully written bytes cannot establish execution. Record the loaded artifact, graph generation, effective settings, and mechanism-specific witness. Reload/dimension/DH transitions invalidate stale prepared state. Configuration persists IDs/parameters rather than a growing candidate enum.

The seam spike chooses a generated index or an established registration mechanism such as ServiceLoader. In either case, the packaged registration must match the declared module directories and require no manual common-code edit. First prove discovery and removal with a non-shipping identity/no-op test provider. It demonstrates plumbing, never a speedup. After the profiler and redesigned benchmark exist, demonstrate one authorized real candidate through the same API. It may be rejected; a trustworthy negative closure is successful infrastructure validation.

Candidate composition starts conservative: independent candidates are not automatically safe together. Declare overlapping resources/conflicts and reject combinations without an explicit composition rule. No automatic tuner or additive-speedup claims.

### Port behavior, not accidental structure

Characterize selected old contracts on an external copy before refactoring. Port native pack identity and archive safety, option snapshots/queues, Apply/Off/Cancel and failed-reload behavior, reload/world/dimension invalidation, optional DH loading, and relevant profiler event ownership. Retain useful rejection/recovery fixtures. Maintain a selected-source disposition for every removed override, config key and hook: irrelevant feature, equivalent native behavior demonstrated, or required behavior reimplemented. Trace consumers and failure paths; misleading historical names do not establish deadness. Separate structural parity from intentional behavior changes, and keep shared correctness guards in treatment and control. A known native defect must be characterized and explicitly retained as a limitation or corrected under a new shared identity, never silently treated as comparison purity. Do not import the old root initializer, central candidate enums, `CompileOptionControl`, pack recipes, or campaign scripts wholesale and strip them afterwards.

Before package B, lock the complete runtime set: Minecraft and NeoForge, exact Iris, Sodium and DH builds, Reimagined archive/member digests, settings preset, and required transitive integration dependencies. Reuse verified identities from history only after checking the actual acquired bytes and compatibility; the foundation's build pins alone are insufficient. Acquisition uses package A's staged verification. CPU parity receipts name the behavior, old/new source identities, intentional correction, assertions, and evidence level. Known bugs are negative fixtures, not behavior to preserve. The packaged JAR is checked for dev instrumentation, parked implementations, accidental mixins, and undeclared resources; source scans alone are insufficient.

## 5. Scope without making every iteration a compatibility campaign

Use one primary development cohort: pinned Reimagined, a declared settings preset/dimension, enabled DH, and an available machine that can render the original combination correctly. Choose it from current availability during execution; native Windows RTX 5080 is a candidate because the old project measured Reimagined there, but that does not prove this exact enabled-DH stack works or renew its allocation. Old RTX allocation is not standing access. Preserve absent/disabled DH behavior and native fallback as correctness cases without pretending they are the same performance cohort.

Distinguish four claims: recognized input, supported integration, observed working behavior, and performance-qualified optimization. A shared pack family or an adapter implementing an interface grants none of the later claims automatically.

Development iterations exercise the candidate's declared affected scope on the primary target. Changes to shared lifecycle, config, or discovery run the broader CPU contract suite. Compatibility expansion is a deliberate milestone: add a second structurally different provider through the existing seam and run the applicable live checks. Do not choose the second pack solely because it resembles Reimagined; choose the smallest useful test of the abstraction when expansion is authorized. Additional versions, GPUs, settings and PBR enter explicit scope cells later.

An extension exercise must show that adding a provider requires its implementation, descriptors and tests, not engine branching. It need not literally be one file. If a second provider exposes a flawed abstraction, improve the shared interface instead of adding special-case paths.

The old Asahi sampler-limit result remains scoped historical evidence. Static capabilities can reject known impossible cases early, but cannot universally predict shader-link success. First-machine admission needs an actual native link/render verification before optimization work. No silent sampler reduction. README claims remain scoped until broader evidence exists; “proven generally positive” is not rewritten as four packs times two machines.

## 6. Checks that are useful and fast

Retain `./check` as the complete CPU closure entry. Add an explicitly labeled fast invocation using the same rule implementations for edit feedback. A fast pass must never be presented as full completion. Pre-commit may use the fast lane; coherent milestones and handoff require the full relevant check and applicable runtime verification.

- Run cheap repository/schema checks before expensive setup where possible. Report rule ID, file/site, observed problem, expected owner, and the supported fix.
- Declare Gradle task inputs/outputs. Cache deterministic CPU results against source, checks, fixtures, dependency/tool identity and relevant environment. Changed checks invalidate their own proof. Prefer Gradle's native incremental machinery, including tool-specimen tasks, over a second custom cache. A stale report directory is not a current pass.
- Reuse compiler/build caches; parallelize independent CPU lanes. Keep heavy CPU work and housekeeping off the measurement host during scored GPU work when they could contaminate the workload.
- Run expensive bad/control tool specimens on checker/tool changes and in a clean verification mode. Full closure includes valid proof for the current identity; cached proof is labeled as reused. Test discovery and no-skip/no-zero assertions still execute for the required suites.
- Replace global name equality with test-engine discovery plus mandatory suite/contract coverage. A newly added ordinary test should not require an administrative registry edit. Required integration cases must not disappear silently.
- Check mutations of the safeguards themselves: remove a required task, change a package role, introduce an invalid provider, alter a fixture, stale a report, and rename a production package. Assertions must fail for the intended reason.
- Keep narrow policy exceptions with rationale and regression evidence. Normal tests and stricter checks are autonomous. A replacement or relaxation must carry a negative specimen showing the original defect is still rejected and a legitimate control showing the corrected path works. That is sufficient for routine implementation changes without personal approval. Changes to evidence levels, verdict promotion, restoration guarantees, or native-quality semantics require Philip's decision; a passing specimen cannot authorize a changed requirement. Independent review is useful for a specific unresolved semantic question, not a mandatory loop.
- Separate structural syntax allowances (shebangs) from temporary behavioral exceptions. Do not make a stable shebang expire with wall-clock time. Time-sensitive policy tests use an explicit test clock.
- Audit file categories by owned roots and artifact types. Allow legitimate assets and small declared fixtures. Do not reject `world`, `region`, `frames`, or ordinary plan prose globally. Unknown executable source types must enter the checker coverage map.

Derive small oracle expectations independently of production code: manually worked transaction/state cases, known historical counterexamples, and independently computed identity vectors across producer/consumer boundaries. Two agents or two generated consumers agreeing with the same incorrect schema is not independent proof. Exercise unknown versions and deliberately disagreeing consumers. Required runtime safety must use explicit validation/errors, not assertions that optimized Python or disabled Java assertions can erase; otherwise refuse that execution mode. CPU fakes qualify their named logic only, not native GL synchronization or a real renderer.

Measure cold setup, warm no-change checks, one-file edit checks, changed-check self-tests, and failure-to-diagnostic delay during implementation. Optimize the largest repeated cost first. No numerical latency promise is justified by this audit. Do not trade away scientific validity to hit a timer.

## 7. Benchmark and profiler interface only

Benchmark redesign is a separate work package. This document does NOT choose scenes, repetitions, warmup, sample counts, statistical procedures, confidence levels, numerical thresholds, stop rules, quality tolerances, or the generality matrix. Old proposed numbers are not inherited defaults.

Expose one maintained development runner with discover/plan, verify, profile, compare, status, cancel, recover, and report operations, implemented as modes of the same lifecycle rather than independent launch scripts. Exact CLI spelling can follow the existing maintained entry. Pure report/analysis work never launches a client. Missing methodology reports unavailable; a synthetic stand-in cannot return a live verdict.

Name the supported schema versions and readers for requests, control messages, captures and terminal results. Unknown versions or producer/consumer disagreement refuse before mutation or qualification. Intentional migration creates a new artifact with source lineage and preserves the original; no automatic broad legacy support or schema-registry service.

The boundary carries:

- A versioned request: purpose, source/artifact identity, candidate/parameters, native baseline identity, pack/settings/world/dimension/DH identity, requested machine capabilities, methodology ID, and authorized resource bounds.
- Observed runtime state separate from requested state: actual loaded artifacts, renderer, linked graph/settings, activation, readiness, and measurement mode.
- Progress and terminal states: admitted or refused, preparing, running, restoring, complete, failed, cancelled, recovery-required. Completion is not synonymous with valid evidence.
- Immutable result references with execution status, validity/reasons, correctness, measured/missing data, health, coverage, restoration state, and applicable scope. Retention/default enablement remain distinct decisions.
- An analyzer result that can be positive, negative, inconclusive or not measured, with uncertainty and limitations supplied by the later methodology. Invalid results cannot be promoted by a force flag.

Authority, readiness, evidence validity, selection and scientific usefulness are independent facts. Authorization cannot validate stale/corrupt evidence; green evidence cannot grant execution authority. Editable approval fields and content hashes establish neither permission nor trust. Selection may reference an older valid result rather than the latest attempt.

Admission and terminal reports expose the same facts in bounded machine-readable and plain-language forms: the goal, actual mechanism activation (or not yet observed), starting source/runtime state, limiting risk, resource budget, stop action and evidence scope. Distinguish operational progress, scientific validity/usefulness and progress toward the objective. Label causes confirmed, supported hypothesis or unknown. A running renderer with insufficient observations is not a successful experiment; a scoped gain is not general qualification.

Profile and scored comparison are distinct modes. Requests declare instrumentation, observations attest to the actual enabled collectors, and the analyzer rejects contaminated timing or mismatched instrumentation. Intrusive scope queries, screenshots, graph dumps and diagnostic exports do not run in scored windows. Numerical overhead budgets and any justified timing instrumentation belong to package E.

Profile output identifies expensive named work with units, coverage and missingness. It must distinguish CPU wall work, GPU intervals, overlap and waits; do not sum overlapping intervals into a frame total. An optimization brief links the measured opportunity, mechanism, affected boundary, and disconfirming observation. Lack of useful profile evidence triggers diagnosis or a bounded exploratory hypothesis, not a fabricated ranking.

Fast development comes from cached builds, reusable prepared slots, offline analysis, and avoiding unnecessary startup/copy/export work. The interface may support multiple isolated requests per client only after reset/identity/contamination tests pass. Whether reuse is scientifically appropriate is decided by benchmark design, not assumed here. Likewise, streaming progress and cancellation do not authorize statistically invalid early stopping.

Content-addressed artifacts may deduplicate bytes and memoize deterministic analysis of frozen input. They must NOT memoize physical performance: identical declared inputs do not imply identical thermal state, scheduler behavior, or future measurements. Historical evidence can inform planning but is not a fresh run.

## 8. Runtime ownership, recovery and storage

Use one bounded owner of the complete runtime operation. It prepares a slot, journals intended mutation and preimages, launches the exact client, verifies actual state, restores, and finalizes. No alternative launch wrappers. The initial supported host implementations are Linux and native Windows; qualify the actually used platform and keep the other explicitly unverified until its tests run. Process identity, fail-fast exclusion, path safety and atomic publication must have real platform implementations, not a POSIX-only shell recipe. Transfer the built JAR, dependency/input manifest and request to an authorized target host with identity verification; return compact and raw evidence to the configured canonical evidence root. Use configured Tailscale aliases with LAN fallback where transfer is needed, retain host-key verification, and create no Git remote. Installation/build tools on the target are pinned as well. Each attempt binds an immutable source snapshot including dirty tracked content, untracked/generated executable inputs, the built JAR and actual loaded relevant libraries/dependencies, not HEAD alone. Source or loaded-input drift starts a new attempt and invalidates relevant qualification; no silent reuse. Occasional concurrent implementation uses separate worktrees and serial integration checks. Worktrees do not isolate devices, ports, environments, caches or artifact roots.

The execution owner enforces supplied wall-time/resource bounds, stop action, retry count and cumulative failed-attempt cost without relying on an agent or notification channel. Persist accounting across restart; missing or duplicate wakeups cannot extend authority or restart indefinitely. Choose explicit bounded operational defaults within the authorized task if needed, without inventing scientific stopping rules. Test lost notifications, exhausted retries and owner disappearance.

Control requests for stop/cancel/retry bind to the current operation, attempt and owner. Reject foreign/stale/replayed requests, including delayed cancellation after restart. Use existing harness/local access controls; if a network control endpoint is introduced, explicitly authenticate access and restrict scope. Do not invent a credential service. Authenticated access is not Philip's policy authorization, and shared credentials do not establish tenant isolation. A client crash and a runner crash both enter the same recoverable protocol. Recovery runs before another operation can mutate an unresolved profile.

Keep result publication separate from a state journal and disposable scratch writes. Validate/serialize a result before publication; commit a complete record atomically on the same filesystem, refuse replacement, and distinguish interruption from a finalized result. Durability requirements include flush/fsync and directory behavior on supported platforms. Readers only accept completed records. Failed recovery must preserve diagnostic inputs rather than publish success.

The state journal must allow idempotent recovery from every externally visible mutation boundary. Compare current bytes/identity against the operation's last owned version before restoring; preserve unrelated user edits. Use one parameterized fault harness across the actual mutations: Iris selection properties, effective/queued shader options, DH settings, generated packs and prepared-slot/save state. Test abrupt termination, disk-full writes, partial downloads, failed reload, duplicate requests, stale responses and recovery failure. A process termination releases process resources; it does not restore settings by itself. Process-kill tests establish process-crash behavior, not power-loss durability. Document filesystem assumptions and require separate evidence before claiming power-loss guarantees.

**GPU policy tradeoff:** the current global ban on GPU locks is too broad to distinguish a scheduler service from a minimal ownership primitive, and process scanning has a launch race. Do not build a lease server or agent-managed lock protocol. Recommended adaptation: one executor with a non-blocking OS exclusion primitive held for its lifetime, automatic release on owner death, and a busy refusal for a concurrent request. Choose a primitive whose behavior is tested on Linux and Windows. No queue, waiting protocol, lease, timeout-based ownership, or persistent scheduling service is needed. This is a proposed narrow change to the approved no-lock policy, not permission to implement a hidden lock system. If that adaptation is declined, runtime launch must be restricted to one external owner and concurrent submission stays unsupported; a process scan alone cannot claim concurrency safety.

The independent reviewer considers this merely implementing the already-allowed refusal correctly; this plan conservatively records it as a narrow policy adaptation because Philip explicitly accepted the previous no-lock wording. It can be approved with this plan, without revisiting each runtime launch.

Any cooperating GPU projects must use the same host/device ownership namespace or an existing external owner; a checkout-local lock cannot exclude another project. Advisory exclusion only covers participants. Detect ambient/uncooperative occupancy and refuse or report uncertainty rather than promise global exclusivity. External exclusive-window authorization may supply ownership where a repo prohibits reservation machinery. This alignment defines exclusion semantics, not a universal lock implementation or service. Rechecking disk headroom does not reserve capacity against unrelated writers.

No “world is stopped” claim based only on a stale PID. Bind host/boot and process-birth identity, owned profile, operation generation and recovery records. Do not terminate unrelated clients. Do not introduce a job queue or keep an executor running without a task need. CPU work may proceed elsewhere while the GPU owner works; measurement-host contamination is checked separately.

### Resource reclamation without micromanagement

Port the useful capacity/copy/slot protections from `run_storage`; do not copy its arbitrary historical reserve/retention numbers as universal policy. Size admission includes incoming data, peak staging, recovery preimages, expected output and a configured reserve. Disk pressure is an operational state with an automated remedy, not an immediate handoff.

Classify managed artifacts as reproducible cache, disposable workspace, active input, recovery input, canonical world, or retained evidence. Only explicitly disposable/reproducible inactive entries may be reclaimed automatically, under configured roots and ownership checks. Plan and apply reclamation within one owned operation; revalidate identity and active references immediately before each removal. Journal each deletion's path, classification, size, identity and reconstruction recipe. Refuse symlinks/path escape. Shared tool caches such as `~/.gradle` are outside this port's reclaim roots; any future cleanup uses the owning tool's supported mechanism. Old-repo trees are never reclaim roots. Age or an ignored filename alone is never sufficient.

The normal path is inspect capacity → reclaim eligible artifacts → recheck capacity → admit work. Bound retries and preserve useful caches where rebuilding costs more than their space benefit. If insufficient reclaimable space remains, continue independent work and report the exact additional need or preservation decision. Do not delete old-repo evidence to avoid asking a necessary question.

A shared disk-reclaim skill is useful as a thin interface to deterministic tooling. A global helper/subagent may invoke it for other projects, but each project supplies its classification/roots and holds its preservation policy. The agent cannot expand deletion authority. This plan does not install a global skill, spawn a permanent helper, or edit personal configuration. Validate the project mechanism first, then extract a shared capability under separate implementation scope.

## 9. Plans, findings, evidence and pruning

Keep this one current plan in Git. README/root instructions point to it; execution updates its compact stage state and unresolved decisions in place. Do not append daily narratives. When superseded, retain durable decisions and references, remove the obsolete active document, and let Git preserve history. Retire `remaining-stages.md` and contradictory decisions during the authorized infrastructure update, preserving the user's existing edit first. This audit does not delete them.

Scratch is external, task-owned and explicitly non-authoritative. Each active task has one workspace and an ownership/retention record. Before closing, promote reusable source, decisions, tests and compact findings into Git; delete disposable scratch after checking ownership. Preserve valuable unknown material pending classification. Default context/search entry points cover current source and current docs, not an archive of every old plan. No stale plan can silently regain authority because an agent found it through a broad search.

Use one structured findings index with stable IDs, question/mechanism, scope, disposition, revision/artifact references, evidence level, limits and reopen conditions. README's accepted table and the negative view are mechanically validated against the index; negative/inconclusive records have a separate view of the same index. Two evidence pools are useful presentation/retention categories, not two independent sources of truth. Preserve F1–F7 as historical, not newly verified, and add compact indexed references to relevant prior Reimagined/DH mechanisms so agents can avoid repeating known failures without loading old plans. The accepted table starts empty and remains so until eligible new evidence exists. All relevant attempts remain visible within a finding; showcasing a positive result must not hide its applicable regressions or unsupported scope.

Accepted evidence needs reproducible source/artifact identity, exact supported scope, correctness/performance receipts and limitations. Negative evidence needs enough mechanism/context to explain why it failed and when revisiting is justified. Preserve crash/recovery artifacts until resolved. Future retention policies may prune raw data explicitly, but the record must then state that full reproduction evidence is no longer available. A hash alone is not a backup.

On rejection, remove the candidate from the working tree, generated registrations, packaged resources, UI and config defaults. # Explicit LOD adapter contract

The dependency-free `com.pp.shaderlod.lod.adapter` API declares adapter capabilities
and negotiates work caps using the existing [effect policy](EFFECT_POLICY_API.md).
It is usable independently of NeoForge, Iris, pack files and a graphics context.
It does not discover, rewrite, select or load shaders. A descriptor declares
support; registration and an accepted cap prove no shader compilation,
consumption, quality, physical work avoidance or performance improvement.

## Declaration and extension

| Type | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `AdapterIdentity` | Namespaced adapter id and exact revision string. Runtime/source bindings must separately verify source pins; a revision label is not a hash check. |
| `ProtocolRequirement` | Namespaced protocol id with an explicit set of accepted positive integer versions. Missing, unknown and newer versions are not implicitly compatible. |
| `WorkKey` | Existing `Effect`, namespaced adapter operation and `WorkKind`. An effect category alone never grants support for a suboperation. |
| `WorkKind` | COUNT (`count`) or RATE (`rate`). Stable string keys, never enum ordinals. Exact mathematical reuse is outside this cap API. |
| `WorkCapability` | A matching `CountFloor` or `DiscreteRates` legal domain. |
| `AdapterDescriptor` | Exact identity, required protocols and supported work capabilities. Empty or conflicting declarations are rejected. |
| `AdapterRegistry` | Immutable snapshot. `register` returns a new registry and rejects duplicate exact identities; different revisions can coexist. |

IDs use lower-case `namespace:path` syntax. Collections are defensively copied.
Conflicting duplicate protocol ids or work keys in one descriptor are errors;
registration never replaces an existing identity. There are no built-in pack
descriptors, names, source algorithms or defaults in this package. New adapters
register explicit declarations without modifying the registry. New operations
can use namespaced keys under the existing effect categories; adding a new effect
category still requires the existing policy/transport contract to be extended.

Required protocol ids belong to the declaration, rather than being inferred from
the registry's schema. A binding can explicitly require `shaderlod:core` version
2 and `shaderlod:effects` version 2, for example. Accepted version 1 of a group's
fields must be declared deliberately. Additional input protocols are ignored;
each declared requirement must match. This API does not resolve transport modes:
the binding must resolve INHERIT/FULL/ADAPTIVE before constructing `EffectPolicy`.
An unavailable or unresolved transport must retain the original path.

## Work negotiation

`WorkRequest` snapshots the exact adapter identity, protocol versions, work key,
resolved immutable policy, global enable, camera-relative Euclidean distance in
blocks, actual upstream count, and caller's legal floor. Null runtime policy/key,
invalid distance/count/floor, absent identity and missing versions fail open with
an explicit reason. A null request object is a programming error because it has
no upstream count to preserve. Declaration constructors reject malformed schema.

```java
var operation = new WorkKey(Effect.VOLUMETRICS,
        "example:integration", WorkKind.COUNT);
var descriptor = new AdapterDescriptor(
        new AdapterIdentity("example:adapter", "exact-source-revision"),
        List.of(new ProtocolRequirement("shaderlod:core", Set.of(2)),
                new ProtocolRequirement("shaderlod:effects", Set.of(2))),
        List.of(new WorkCapability(operation, new WorkCapability.CountFloor(1))));
var registry = new AdapterRegistry().register(descriptor);
var result = registry.negotiate(new WorkRequest(descriptor.identity(),
        Map.of("shaderlod:core", 2, "shaderlod:effects", 2), operation,
        resolvedPolicy, globalEnabled, distanceBlocks, actualUpstreamCount,
        pathSpecificMinimum));
int acceptedWorkCap = result.negotiatedWorkLimit();
```

This is an API example, not a supported adapter or quality recommendation.
Caller paths must retain the original operation for every rejected negotiation.
`WorkNegotiation.requestedBudget` preserves the numerical `WorkBudget` with its
continuous requested ratio and integer requested cap. `negotiatedWorkLimit` is
the cap accepted by the descriptor. Unsupported requests may therefore show a
smaller requested budget while the negotiated limit remains full upstream work.
`reductionRequested` and `reductionNegotiated` describe those two states only;
neither reports actual executed work. Runtime readbacks and operation counters
must be recorded separately. There is deliberately no physical-realization field.

COUNT delegates to `EffectPolicy.decide`: smoothstep distance transitions,
`ceil(upstream * ratio)`, clamping to upstream, and a legal floor. The effective
floor is `max(caller floor, declared floor)`. Zero explicitly permits skipping.
Zero upstream work stays zero. A positive upstream count below the declared floor
is unsupported and retains its original count. Large counts, including
`Integer.MAX_VALUE`, use the existing bounded numerical semantics.

RATE declares exact retained evaluation ratios, including 1 for full work. Both
the continuous requested ratio and the integer cap divided by upstream count
must be declared legal rates. Zero upstream work uses a full quantized ratio
because no evaluations exist. Unsupported intermediate rates or rounded counts
retain full work with `UNSUPPORTED_RATE`; the API does not silently snap rates.
For example, a declaration `{1, 0.25}` accepts one of four evaluations at 0.25,
but rejects a 0.5 transition or three of nine evaluations after upward rounding.
A zero rate must be explicitly declared. These exact-double membership checks
are Java contract checks, not promises of bit-exact GLSL float execution.

Global disable, effect disable, lighting protection and invalid numerical inputs
take precedence over descriptor checks and retain original work with the same
reason as the existing policy. Eligible requests then check exact registration,
each required protocol, effect, work key and legal domain, in that order. Thus a
disabled request reports disable even if the adapter is absent. Unsupported
effect, operation/kind, upstream domain or protocol never becomes a partial cap.
Shadow filtering and ambient occlusion stay protected when
`preserveSalientLighting` is true. Registration cannot bypass that policy.

# Development loaded artifact evidence

`LoadedArtifactEvidence` is a standalone development utility for the pinned
Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.253 runtime. It imports only JDK APIs, Gson and
NeoForge's `ModList`; it has no dependency on ShaderLOD production classes. This
allows the original Photon `runClientLodOff` control to collect the same artifact
evidence as a mod-present control. The actual client call sites remain parent-owned.

Artifact identities describe bytes reachable through the loaded ModList roots
at capture time. They do **not** prove loaded or transformed class bytes, active
shader execution, driver compilation, rendered quality or performance. There is
no atomic filesystem freeze; the external run protocol must prohibit artifact
changes and capture outside measured intervals.

## Entry points and snapshot schema

| API | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `capture()` | Reads the real loaded registry and every ModList artifact root; returns valid or failed evidence with errors retained. |
| `observe(Path, JsonObject mods)` | Independently computes one root's raw locator and content identity; does not consult a legacy path map. |
| `snapshot(JsonObject expectedMods, List<JsonObject> observations)` | Validates and coalesces detached observations; useful for isolated checks. |
| `requireValid(JsonObject snapshot)` | Throws for failed captured evidence. Attach/write the snapshot before calling so errors survive. |
| `fileSha256(Path)` | Streams a regular file's SHA-256. |
| `directoryIdentity(Path)` | Uses the exact existing BenchmarkSession directory schema, bounds and ordering. |

Schema 1 returns `loaded_mods`, `loaded_artifact_inventory`,
`complete_mod_coverage`, `complete_identities`, `valid`, `errors` and a `limits`
statement. Each inventory item contains:

- `mods`: loaded mod ID to exact version string.
- `path`: raw `Path.toAbsolutePath().toString()`, including legitimate empty
  paths for virtual roots.
- `filesystem_provider`: raw filesystem provider scheme.
- `uri`: raw `Path.toUri().toString()`, preserving Java encoding and mount IDs.
- `identity`: file SHA-256 string, bounded directory object, or unknown/null.
- `locator_error` / `identity_error`: retained when an observation fails.

The utility never normalizes a virtual mount ID or URI, chooses an alternate
nested dependency or accepts a receipt. Those are separate independently pinned
comparison decisions. Distinct physical URIs retain separate records even if
their raw paths are both empty and their hashes match.

Only equal provider + URI, raw path and **complete** content identity can coalesce,
and their mod IDs must be disjoint. Duplicate mod IDs, conflicting identities or
paths, unknown locators, malformed identities and incomplete directory trees
fail `valid`. Conflicting/unknown records remain in the inventory. Exact coverage
checks every registry mod ID **and version**; counts alone cannot pass. A duplicate
mod also prevents `complete_mod_coverage`, even when a path-keyed object would
otherwise collapse it.

Unknown JSON values are represented by `JsonNull` in memory. A caller's default
Gson serializer may omit these properties; omitted and JSON-null locator/identity
must both remain unknown and invalid. Error strings and invalid root records
survive either serialization. The isolated result uses `serializeNulls()` to make
the null examples explicit; legacy caller serialization need not change.

## Exact directory identity

The directory object uses kind
`development directory; regular files only, symlinks excluded`. It walks without
following symlinks, filters `isRegularFile(NOFOLLOW_LINKS)`, and uses natural Path
sorting exactly as the existing BenchmarkSession implementation. Each digest
entry is UTF-8:

```text
relative/path + NUL + file_sha256 + LF
```

A complete object has `complete: true`, `files`, `bytes` and `tree_sha256`.
Exceeding 5000 files or 32 MiB returns `complete: false` and the existing exact
limit string `5000 files / 32 MiB; no partial tree hash advertised`; it contains
no partial tree hash, file count or byte count. The file SHA-256 streaming method
produces the same digest as the prior full-byte-array hash.

   and Delta=2ray_step*extent, define:

   ```text
   H = project(M,P)
   dH = vec4(M[0].x,M[1].y,M[2].zw) * Delta.xyzz
   w_min = abs(H.w) − abs(dH.w)
   D = abs(H.w) * w_min
   ```

   entire remaining segment and every component is monotone. Its maximum absolute

   displacement over the entire segment. It is the same conservative coordinate
   envelope that frozen max(abs(endpoint−center)) constructs, without three
   homogeneous vector divisions. In exact arithmetic this is sound for Photon's
   actual project helper, including whichever DH/combined inverse matrix the
   original code passes. It is not a claim about arbitrary new projection code.

   The z/W cheap precheck needs scalar `H.z/H.w` numerators and homogeneous changes
   only: H.z=M[2].z*P.z+M[3].z, H.w=M[2].w*P.z+M[3].w,
   dH.z=M[2].z*Delta.z, dH.w=M[2].w*Delta.z. No inverse division or x/y work is
   needed on z rejection. Computing N.z with the same multiply/subtract expression
   is preferred initially; an algebraic determinant cancellation shortcut needs
   its own floating-error fixtures before adoption.

   Successful full checks need one project plus one homogeneous delta rather than
   three project calls, no homogeneous divide and one reused extent. The reduction
   is in source math, not proven GPU cost. Existing 1mm margin is not a general
   IEEE error proof: test high-depth amplification, cancellation, W-near-zero,
   large/small coordinates, all signs, actual matrices and conversion rounding
   before making any safety-equivalence assertion.

4. At60–81, consider restoring literal original coarse texelFetch and saving only
   the successful hit's key/depth for first refinement. No-hit rays then avoid K
   cache branches/state updates, and distinct-key coarse hits avoid useless checks.
   This removes rare exact coarse duplicate-key reuse but changes no sample
   positions/depth results. Allocate/query cache dimensions only after a hit, or
   query once when actually validating that hit. This is a separate measured
   implementation choice, not automatic authorization to modify frozen source.
   Keep invalid/out-of-bounds behavior unmodified and never reuse undefined depth.

A once-only expensive eligibility attempt can be a conservative additional cost
policy, but should not be the first repair: pixel span becomes smaller on subsequent
updates, so first failure does not imply future failure. An m>=2 gate plus necessary
bounds and closed-form world test attacks work without throwing away every R4
candidate. If further ALU remains costlier than cached continuation, explicitly
retain cache-only control for attribution rather than credit early stop with fetch
savings it cannot produce.
