## Secondary low-risk arithmetic candidate: Complementary prior-weight reuse

Both Reimagined/Unbound r5.9.3 pin the same volume member `d380c3243df73b390433c015fcb5b9182cf98a511b49f7a98d5ccac1313ae8ff`. Their loop computes `currentWeight=F(lastDistance)` and `nextWeight=F(nextDistance)`, where `F(x)=smoothstep1(pow(x/maxDistance,fogCurve))`, then accumulates their difference and assigns `lastDistance=nextDistance`. Neither denominator nor exponent changes inside the loop. Thus the next iteration recomputes exactly the prior nextWeight. A carried scalar initialized with native `F(0)` and updated alongside lastDistance eliminates that repeated expression without changing sample counts, locations, texture operations, shadow eligibility, additive recurrence, native AA or dither.

All loop exits before accumulation terminate the loop; there is no continue. The entity-depth break occurs before both accumulation and tail assignment. These exits therefore do not require another cache-update path. Retain the original initial expression rather than simplifying to zero without a domain proof. For k completed intervals, native weight evaluation count2k becomes k+1 (k−1 fewer pow/smoothstep evaluations); final incomplete iterations and compiler optimization alter actual cost. Default near count10 increases up to15 with scene intensity; already-selected Balanced near count9–14 remains unchanged. Overworld far count is only1 and should not be budgeted further.

This is an explicit pack-specific compiler optimization opportunity, not a promised speedup: the native compiler may already perform loop-carried reuse, register pressure may offset savings, and there is no measured shader/pass fraction. A private candidate should preserve original graph recovery and use the existing generated Balanced route, with runtime enable fallback made explicit before main adoption. A CPU equivalence model can prove its algebra under modeled arithmetic, not GLSL driver bit identity. Parent has the exact scope proposal; no maintained sources were changed in this analysis.

## Why the obvious BSL/Bliss copies are less useful

BSL10.1.8 default AO_METHOD0 performs four angular groups, each with two depth fetches, plus four normal-reconstruction depth fetches. The existing ceil(.875N) policy maps4→4 Balanced: a group-preserving copy of Astra AO saves nothing. Performance maps4→3 but normally selects BSL's native renderer graph, bypassing the adapter. Shrinking individual paired samples, changing normalization/rotation or changing policy would be a new quality choice. The native AO pointiness correction also shares group normalization; a denominator-only copy would be incomplete.

BSL's seven logarithmic light-shaft positions use `exp2(i+dither)-.95`, sum shadow/blocklight and divide by7. Balanced maps7→7; merely changing the upper loop bound truncates distant support. Proper reduction would resample the exponent domain and preserve sum normalization as well as currentDist-dependent blocklight weighting. This has no useful Balanced reduction under current policy and should not consume a port attempt.

BSL default volumetric clouds retain per-step `cloud=mix(cloud,1,noise)`, cloudLighting weight `noise*(1-cloud²)`, multiplicative distanceFade, separate cloudFaded and cloudViewLength first-crossing feedback. Reducing samples and widening step alone changes all these. Even constant-density transmittance requires alpha'=1−(1−alpha)^(oldN/newN); that correction alone does not preserve lighting, distance fade or first-hit feedback. The optional Aurora24→21 transfer is mathematically simpler but AURORA0 defaults mean no default work saving. Existing closed reflected-cloud classification, saturation, early-alpha and renderer no-gain trials remain closed.

Bliss already budgets default VL_SAMPLES in its actual fog consumer before its exponential sampling distribution and differential dd. Native fog/atmosphere/cloud contributions track absorption separately. The active source repeats the identical pow(expFactor,(i+dither.x)/SAMPLECOUNT) expression in d and dd and repeats several extinction exponentials in color/transmittance pairs. Naming each once is straightforward exact-expression reuse, but local common-subexpression elimination is standard compiler territory and cannot be represented as a new GPU saving. A more aggressive recurrence would change floating-point evaluation/accumulation and requires its own error bounds; it is not a necessary concept port. Native cloud march/inner sunlight loops also carry their own physical stride/extinction and temporal reconstruction, so global count substitution is insufficient.

## Removed work, surviving costs and limits

For qualified water, the native 30-iteration maximum/6-refinement path loses its
initialization, repeated project/unproject and depth fetches, hit validation,
terrain-radiance fetch/decode, traced-hit `DoFog`, border/alpha factors and the
hit-only `refDist=dist` assignment. Native preparation survives; the miss starts
with `reflection=vec4(0)` and `refDist=far`. Background composition then supplies
native sky/cloud/background color while retaining the native miss alpha.

The output differs deliberately. `AddBackgroundReflection` includes native sky,
sky-effect cloud work and direct GGX glint. It can execute more often or contribute
more strongly after a trace is removed. Hit fog/radiance work also disappears,
and changed color can affect later temporal/history behavior. Total-frame timing
therefore measures a **coupled contrast**, including this work shift. It does not
isolate the projection ALU, traversal, texture latency or attainable DDA saving.
The added material branch is a cost to account for; a native control variant
without that runtime branch does not measure its removal-mode overhead alone.

A concrete source case is original `reflection.a == 1`: it skips the background
call, while removal leaves alpha 0 and forces native sky/cloud/GGX background
work. The native glint equations are preserved; **visible glint intensity or
coverage is not promised unchanged**. Also, the later normalM assignment is
source-preserved but inactive inside this exact WSR-internal -1 scope.

The material selector is `flat` per primitive, and all original non-water sampler
expressions remain intact. Actual compiler/driver behavior, implicit derivatives,
helper invocations and non-water image equivalence still require runtime checks.
Source preservation alone cannot certify their outputs. PBR, DH, other versions,
other dimensions and Unbound do not gain a support claim from refusal or shared
source ancestry. No new sampler-headroom conclusion is made.

## Remaining scaffolding that must be acknowledged

The five switches own cloud, water, fog, SSR and materials. They do not globally
remove every ShaderLOD expression. Current explicit source still:

- Computes a generic `shaderlod_quality_at` in deferred lighting and passes one
  from translucent shading. With `SHADERLOD_PRESERVE_LIGHTING`, PCF/SSRT/GTAO/SSAO
  select tier zero and original budgets; source-level tier expressions can
  remain before optimization. Do not assume the driver eliminates all of them.
- Retains the deferred debug branch

  flag independently of global enablement. Debug false must be verified from
  config/observations; global OFF is not a substitute for disabling debug.
- Retains uniform declarations and the bridge sentinel. `shaderlod_quality_at`
  returns early when disabled, while enabled can compute generic tiers even
  when no effect changes its final work. This is the specific scaffolding/code
  path difference the proposed control can expose.

`CommonUniformsMixin` registers bridge version 2, enabled, preset, near/far,
transition and debug at `PER_FRAME`. Several getters construct a validated
`ShaderLodConfig.snapshot()`. Only the enabled value changes here; the other
getters and registrations remain present. Supplier execution or intended config
values do not, by themselves, prove a GPU uniform upload or active linked
uniform. Some unused uniforms can be optimized out. If a bounded observer is
added, observe the existing registered integer supplier before returning its
original value; do not reevaluate it at report time or infer linked uniform
state from one registration log. Identify observed versus unobserved suppliers.

The global flag also changes CPU short-circuit paths:
`GeometryLodController` evaluates enabled before terrain-enabled, and
`ShadowCullingRuntime` evaluates enabled before its optimization flag. Keeping
these features false prevents geometry/culling/list-ownership work changes, but an extra config
read on ON is still possible. Commands/runtime-status reporting may log one
flag transition; the settling interval excludes that transition from capture.
Therefore any ON/OFF difference measures the complete live-flag/scaffolding
path, not exclusively the cost of one GLSL branch or `glUniform` call.

"Same workload" here means preserved effect budgets and expected rendering
behavior under these controls. It does not claim byte-identical source to
original Photon, pixel-identical temporal frames, or equal instruction counts.

# Controlled rendering workloads

`scripts/prepare_workloads.py` prepares three independent profiles per scene:

| Profile | Shader archive | Common quality | ShaderLOD |
|---|---|---|---|
| `high` | Original pinned Photon v1.3b | Upstream high, with common Mac compatibility changes | Disabled/inert |
| `lower` | Original pinned Photon v1.3b | Upstream medium, with the same Mac changes | Disabled/inert |
| `adaptive` | Reviewed patched Photon | Same common settings as high | Balanced by default |

The high/adaptive settings preserve upstream default sample counts. This avoids
inflating only the baseline to produce a favorable optimization result. Lower
is a practical simpler preset: it removes entity shadows, screen-space shadows,
water parallax, and shader AO according to upstream medium's intended feature
choices. It retains the same 2,048 shadow map resolution and volumetric fog.
Adaptive retains those high-quality features near the camera and uses the
existing distance policy farther away. Cached-sky approximation is explicitly
off; the rejected aggressive tree-lighting comparison is not the default.

## Preparing

```sh
python3 scripts/build_shaderpack.py
python3 scripts/prepare_workloads.py --config-only --dry-run
# Stop clients using the source world before copying.
python3 scripts/prepare_workloads.py --scene forest
python3 scripts/prepare_workloads.py --scene cloudstorm
# Optional premium cloud quality, applied equally to original high and adaptive.
python3 scripts/prepare_workloads.py --scene cloudstorm --cloud-upscaling 1
```

The source defaults to `run-landscape/lod-on`, with the warmed
`ShaderLOD-Landscape` save. Output is `run-workloads/<scene>/{high,lower,adaptive}`.
All three initial saves, including DH caches, are hash-checked against one
source. Default vanilla distance is 24 chunks, simulation distance 8, DH radius
128 chunks. DH generation is disabled and its processing is limited to two
threads with runtime ratio 0.5. Wait for upload/processing queues to settle.

`--render-distance 16|24|32` changes the matched geometry/submission workload.
`--cloud-upscaling 1|2|3|4` selects a documented Photon cloud resolution option
for high/adaptive; lower retains upstream default 4. Default 4 renders cloud
buffers `colortex9` and `colortex10` at quarter width/height, or 1/16 of full
pixel area. Values 3 and 2 select one-third and half width/height; value 1 uses
full resolution, 16 times default cloud-buffer pixel area. This premium quality
reduces reliance on temporal cloud reconstruction and increases buffer memory
and shading work. It changes resolution equally for high/adaptive, preserves
original sample counts, and introduces no extra texture bindings. Report it as
**premium full-resolution clouds**, not original default high. Source evidence
is the explicit `size.buffer.colortex9/10` branches in pinned
`shaders/shaders.properties`; actual driver performance remains to be measured.
`--camera X Y Z YAW PITCH` supplies a common scene camera. `--source`,
`--source-world`, `--output`, `--pack`, and `--preset` allow explicit overrides.
Each scene needs three save copies; prepare only scenes that will be measured.

`--config-only` writes packs/configuration without reading or copying the source
save, allowing configuration review while the source client is active. It still
refuses to modify an active destination save. These profiles are not launchable
until real saves are copied. `--dry-run` changes nothing. Ordinary preparation
preserves existing saves; `--replace-worlds` first backs them up before making
fresh matched copies. None of these operations launch or stop Minecraft.

## Acceptance evidence

Measure one client at a time, with matched resolution/camera/time/weather and
warmed DH/temporal histories. Run original high, original lower, and adaptive
controls, including repeated/alternating runs to expose variability. Compare
GPU-render time, pass fractions, CPU wall/thread time, FPS, and visual structure
separately. The proof target is roughly 15–20% GPU-render savings in a realistic
workload; an option file is not proof of that gain. Report the measured ceiling
or failed hypothesis if the target is unattainable. A lower-quality original
preset provides a useful quality/performance control against adaptive cuts.

## Spatial and temporal inputs

The fine texture coordinate is `(pos + 0.4*wind)*0.005`; the coarse detail texture
uses `(pos + 0.2*wind)*0.0009`. Each is 64³ and repeats. At scale 10, fine lattice
spacing is `1/(64*0.005*10) = 0.3125` camera/world blocks; coarse lattice spacing
is about 1.736 blocks. Full repeat periods are 20 and 111.111 blocks. These are
source coordinate/lattice scales, not a proof that nonlinear density is strictly
band-limited. Density squares detail, erodes coarse coverage and applies a
rational contrast function, so a texture-cell Nyquist argument alone is unsafe.

`wind = wind_velocity*world_age`; prior `pos` translation plus the fine term gives
1.4 times wind velocity in fine coordinates. Fine lattice motion is
`64*0.005*1.4*|wind_velocity|` texels per world-age second. Actual camera motion
adds relative motion. `world_age=((worldDay%128)*24000+worldTime)/20` can wrap;
frozen benchmark world time does not test normal cloud-wind evolution. Keep
upstream checkerboard phase, jitter, temporal history and reset behavior.

Use the actual cloud viewer `air_viewer_pos` and **current density evaluation
point**, including secondary-ray points, to compute observer distance divided by
`CLOUDS_SCALE`. Do not use fragment terrain depth, planet radius, `length(pos)`,
or distance from the first shell sample. Upstream primary `ray_origin` is already
at the shell entry plus jitter; its `distance_to_sample` omits camera-to-shell
distance and is unsuitable as the LOD metric.

Derive a conservative pixel cone from neighboring unprojected normalized rays,
using the same selected vanilla/DH projection and TAAU scale as the main ray.
For point distance `s` in atmosphere units, transverse footprint is approximately
`s*max(length(dir_x-dir), length(dir_y-dir))`. Multiply by `0.005*64` for fine
texture-cell coverage. Compute directions explicitly before marches; use no
screen derivatives within divergent ray loops. Start with **one final display
pixel**, not the 4×4 checkerboard tile, so retained temporal detail is protected.

Primary linear step length and secondary exponential step lengths are known at
their callers. They are longitudinal integration spacing, not pixel-cone width.
Preserve them; do not enlarge the cone by `max(pixel_width, ray_step)` and assume
the resulting isotropic density average preserves optical depth. Secondary points
use the observer cone at their own position while retaining all light-ray inputs.

replace rather than save the texture fetch, defeating the cost hypothesis.

sampling for its exact Mac profile; it does not validate a new profile/source.
Pinned `.mcmeta` requests blur/repeat, but does not prove actual sampler/mip state.
Recheck bound volume dimensions, base/max levels, filter and anisotropy. No usable
prefiltered mip chain is established. Explicit `textureLod(...,0)` in the new
active density function needs that scoped equivalence check; preserve literal
original implicit samples in the disabled kernel. Do not assume derivatives from
branching density marches are meaningful.

This is a procedural-detail capability, not a ray-count budget: the common
effect policy must not interpret a retained-work ratio as multiplying density.
The adapter owns footprint mapping, calibration and truthful consumed fields.

## Minimal kill test and stopping rule

Before implementing the calibrated path, assign a tiny default-off pinned control
that replaces **only cumulus fine 3D sampling** with a fixed diagnostic value in
all main-pass density calls. Keep coarse noise, all primary/light/ambient counts,
ray extents, seeds, phase functions and reconstruction unchanged. This knowingly
changes quality/occupancy and cannot establish a quality-equivalent speedup or a
strict isolated fetch budget; it only tests whether this source region merits
investment. Use original, disabled and same-source global OFF/ON controls with
verified options; root/runtime operator alone assembles/reloads/measures.

Require an ordinary cloud-visible scene plus forest/coast, GPU frame-only repeated
balanced timings and matched total-frame timing. Reject a flat/regressive result
before calibration. If useful, first freeze source/member/sampler evidence, then
implement interior/full-near filtering and test sun-facing cloud edges, wind and
camera motion, weather, observer elevation inside/above the shell, temporal resets,
water glint through clouds and DH/noDH boundaries. A fast diagnostic is not
acceptance. If edge guards rarely qualify, calibration shifts brightness, or
sampler/transfer work consumes the saving, stop this mechanism. Neither an AO
gain nor this unmeasured candidate is evidence of the 50% throughput target.

# Per-effect work policy

The dependency-free `com.pp.shaderlod.lod` model describes requested work caps for
explicit shader adapters. It does not register Iris uniforms, read NeoForge config,
patch GLSL, or establish shader consumption. The new general LOD goal uses Photon
as its reference consumer; another pack would need an independently reviewed
adapter and its own runtime evidence.

## Immutable model

`EffectPolicy(enabled, preserveSalientLighting, bands, mediumWorkRatio,
farWorkRatio)` snapshots one override. `DistanceBands(nearBlocks, farBlocks,
transitionBlocks)` uses camera-relative Euclidean distance in Minecraft block
units. Transition width is the **full** width centered on each boundary, matching
the existing core contract: 32/96/8 means transitions at 28–36 and 92–100 blocks.
Smoothstep blends retained work from 1 to the medium ratio, then to the far ratio.
Zero width changes tiers exactly at the boundary. Bands cannot overlap or extend
below zero, and endpoint arithmetic must remain finite.

Ratios satisfy `0 <= farWorkRatio <= mediumWorkRatio <= 1`. They cap the fraction
of an adapter's actual upstream work count; they are not universal sample counts,
effect strength, radius, shader quality preset, or screen resolution. Constructor
validation rejects malformed configuration. Runtime decisions preserve original
work for global disable, effect disable, protected lighting, invalid/null effect,
non-finite/negative distance, negative work count, or an invalid retained floor.

The protection flag is part of the immutable policy. With it enabled, shadow
filtering and ambient occlusion keep their upstream budgets even if smaller ratios
were configured. Other effects still need their own quality review: the flag does
not imply that all reflection, water, volumetric or material reductions are safe.

| Effect | Stable uniform key suffix | Default block bands | Protected lighting |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shadow filtering | `ShadowFiltering` | 32 / 96 / 8 | Yes |
| Ambient occlusion | `AmbientOcclusion` | 32 / 96 / 8 | Yes |
| Reflections | `Reflections` | 32 / 96 / 8 | No |
| Volumetrics | `Volumetrics` | 32 / 96 / 8 | No |
| Water surface | `WaterSurface` | 96 / 256 / 32 | No |
| Materials | `Materials` | 32 / 96 / 8 | No |
| Opaque lighting | `OpaqueLighting` | 32 / 96 / 8 | No; spatial guards are adapter-owned |

Do not serialize enum ordinals. These suffixes are stable identifiers; an adapter
must document which operations each broad effect category actually covers.
Volumetrics does not imply every fog/cloud operation shares the same useful bands
or even has a valid surface-distance input.

`defaultsFor(effect)` disables the new override, sets both ratios to 1, and enables
lighting protection. 32/96 are project starting points, not measured optima; water
96/256/32 comes from existing Photon water bands. Unity/off defaults reflect the
current evidence: the recent five-effect pilot regressed, lower shadow/AO budgets
lost salient distant structure, and a far reflection skip produced a visible water
band. No new quality reduction is promoted by this API. See
[STATUS](STATUS.md), [DECISIONS](DECISIONS.md), and the
[Photon glint audit](PHOTON_GLINT_SOURCE_AUDIT.md).

## Explicit adapter use

```java
var policy = new EffectPolicy(true, true, new DistanceBands(32, 96, 8), 0.5, 0.25);
var budget = policy.decide(globalEnabled, Effect.REFLECTIONS,
        cameraRelativeDistanceBlocks, upstreamTraceSteps, minimumLegalTraceSteps);
int requestedTraceSteps = budget.workLimit();
```

This example requests a reduction; it is not a recommended Photon preset. The
adapter supplies the actual upstream count from the selected pack options and
feature path. It also supplies the legal retained floor: zero permits skipping
all work; one preserves at least one iteration. A zero upstream budget remains
zero. Invalid upstream counts are returned unchanged so the caller retains its
original path rather than inventing a valid-looking reduced budget.

Quantization uses `ceil(upstream * retainedRatio)` and clamps to the legal floor
and upstream count. Apart from the declared floor, rounding retains less than one
additional work item above the continuous requested count. A cap cannot increase
the upstream count, including `Integer.MAX_VALUE`. `WorkBudget.retentionRatio`
reports the continuous request; `workLimit` is the integer result after rounding
and the floor. `reason` describes policy eligibility, and `reduced()` reports only
that the requested integer limit shrank. Neither proves fewer physical GPU
operations.

Shader ports must reproduce smoothstep, finite-input guards, non-overlap, protected
lighting, upward integer rounding and bounded caps. Drivers generally evaluate
GLSL floats with lower precision than Java doubles; transport must validate its
float range and use source fixtures plus actual driver/readback checks. This Java
model is an oracle for intended policy, not proof of bit-exact GLSL execution.
An adapter that changes loop counts must also preserve its integration interval,
normalization, upstream early-exit rules and any minimum legal refinement work.
It must not replace semantic work solely because an effect enum exists.

Exact work reuse is a separate capability. Reusing an identical texel/depth fetch
while preserving original iteration positions and evaluation math can remain
eligible when shadow/AO budgets are protected or ratios are 1. The work-cap model
neither enables nor forbids that independent adapter optimization. For example,
duplicate AO taps can share an identical depth fetch but cannot skip horizon math
that still depends on the original fractional ray position.

## Registered additive extension: source state

The integration source now registers a separate NeoForge client config and Iris
uniform extension. `ShaderLod.java` registers `ShaderLodEffectConfig.SPEC` in
`shaderlod-effects-client.toml`. Its seven `effects.<effect>` sections use enum names
in lower snake case: `shadow_filtering`, `ambient_occlusion`, `reflections`,
`volumetrics`, `water_surface`, `materials`, and `opaque_lighting`. Each section exposes `mode`,
`near`, `far`, `transition`, `mediumWorkRatio`, `farWorkRatio`, and
`preserveSalientLighting`. Defaults are INHERIT, the table's block bands, unity
ratios and lighting protection enabled.

The config spec bounds near to 1–4095 and far to 2–4096; snapshot conversion
then raises far to at least near+1. Transition's config range is
0–512; conversion additionally caps it to `min(near*2, far-near)`. Far ratio is
capped to medium ratio. These are deterministic normalization rules in the config
integration, while direct construction of the pure API still rejects malformed
input. The pure API supports finite positive distances beyond those config ranges.
The config spec validates persisted scalar values. Additional normalization
replaces non-finite raw numbers with valid default bands and forces FULL/unity
work; null modes select INHERIT/unity. Repaired cross-fields are flagged in status.
Commands reject invalid ranges/overlap/increasing ratios before changing stored
fields. Reload repair changes effective request/transport values, not the file.

For shadow/AO with protection enabled, the config snapshot publishes both ratios
as 1 while retaining the immutable policy protection flag. Protection is therefore
baked into the transmitted ratios; there is no separate protection uniform. This
protects quality budget counts and does not disable independent exact work reuse.
`Control.requested` retains normalized requested ratios; `Control.policy` holds
protected transport values. Releasing protection restores the stored request.

`EffectUniformsMixin`, listed in `shaderlod.mixins.json`, injects at the tail of
pinned Iris `CommonUniforms.generalCommonUniforms`. It registers 43 PER_FRAME
fields: one integer `shaderlodEffectsVersion` with value 2, plus these six fields
for each `shaderlod<Suffix>` prefix in the effect table above:

| Field suffix | Iris registration | Source value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Mode` | Integer | Explicit mode protocol value 0/1/2 |
| `Near` | Float from double supplier | Validated `nearBlocks` |
| `Far` | Float from double supplier | Validated `farBlocks` |
| `Transition` | Float from double supplier | Validated full `transitionBlocks` width |
| `MediumWorkRatio` | Float from double supplier | Validated/protected medium retained ratio |
| `FarWorkRatio` | Float from double supplier | Validated/protected far retained ratio |

For example, the exact AO names are `shaderlodAmbientOcclusionMode`,
`shaderlodAmbientOcclusionNear`, `shaderlodAmbientOcclusionFar`,
`shaderlodAmbientOcclusionTransition`, `shaderlodAmbientOcclusionMediumWorkRatio`,
and `shaderlodAmbientOcclusionFarWorkRatio`. Enum ordinals are not used for modes.
The existing seven core fields, including `shaderlodBridgeVersion=2` and global
`shaderlodEnabled`, retain their existing registration and semantics.

Version 2 adds OpaqueLighting to version 1's six effects. Older groups retain all
names, modes, units and ratio meanings; an explicit old consumer may accept both
versions for its unchanged group. OpaqueLighting requires version 2.

Mod config loading/reloading events publish one volatile immutable map after
conversion; unloading publishes safe defaults. Commands edit related fields
atomically, publish the map, and save **outside** the policy lock. FML save/reload
owns another lock before posting events, so saving under the policy lock would
invert that order. Only this SPEC is handled; existing core config is unchanged.

One `EffectUniformFrame` is shared by all program registrations using the same
Iris frame notifier, with one listener. At frame start it captures the published
map pointer. Every extension supplier uses that map until the next frame, even
when a command/reload publishes another map meanwhile. Maps allocate on config
conversion/edit, not suppliers or ordinary frames. Weak notifier keys allow
disposed pipeline state to be released. This extension guarantee does not change
the older core's suppliers. Actual notifier ordering and driver reload behavior
still require client acceptance; no measured overhead saving is claimed.

No Photon adapter consumption, driver linking/readback, config reload behavior,
runtime mixin application or performance gain has been established by this source
review. Build acceptance and the GPU/runtime owner must record those checks
separately.

## Requested controls and diagnostics

The command tree adds `/shaderlod effects`, `/shaderlod effects status`, and
`/shaderlod effects <effect> status`, using the seven lower snake case keys.
Per-effect edits are:

```text
/shaderlod effects opaque_lighting mode adaptive
/shaderlod effects opaque_lighting bands 32 96 8
/shaderlod effects opaque_lighting ratios 1 0.25
/shaderlod effects shadow_filtering protection true
```

Modes are `inherit`, `full`, `adaptive`; protection is boolean. Valid edits save
the separate config and reach extension suppliers at the next frame boundary.
Status reports requested bands/ratios/mode, protected transport ratios, repair
state and whether the Iris registration callback was observed. It explicitly
labels shader consumption unverified. Registration, config or an archive name
does not establish a linked consumer; no supported-path guesses are introduced.

OpaqueLighting ratios describe retained shading evaluations, not radiance scaling.
Its first spatial adapter may support K4/K1 only and must declare unsupported
intermediate rates and its geometry/material/light-edge fallback. Existing
shadow/AO sample protection does not certify spatial shadow reconstruction.

| Mode | Intended adapter behavior |
| --- | --- |
| 0: INHERIT | Keep existing adapter/core policy; additive defaults use this mode. |
| 1: FULL | Retain the pack's original work for this effect. |
| 2: ADAPTIVE | Apply the validated custom policy when global enable and protection permit. |

`EffectPolicy.enabled=false` means retain original work at the numerical layer;
it does **not** mean INHERIT. Resolve mode before invoking the custom numerical
model. Global disable selects the original pack work even when a per-effect mode
is INHERIT. Unknown protocol versions/modes, unsupported pinned pack revisions,
absent mod, missing transport, or invalid converted fields must select the
original pack path. A declared effect name is not evidence that any path consumes
its ratios, and missing capability must not silently become a partial override.

Record adapter declarations separately from actual consumption:

| Adapter declaration | Consumption evidence required before acceptance |
| --- | --- |
| Pinned pack revision/source and maintained patch hashes | Selected archive and linked program/source identity |
| Protocol version, supported fields and effect/suboperation mapping | Driver link/readback of those exact fields |
| Distance source/units, upstream count source, legal floor and quantization | Original/off/on in-world behavior and config/reload checks |
| Quality cap versus exact reuse capability, lighting guard behavior | Relevant loop/fetch/work evidence and protected/full-path controls |
| DH paths supported or unsupported | Actual DH-present/absent rendering and boundary checks |

Keep this as an explicit adapter contract; no automatic GLSL rewriting or
capability registry is introduced. The next integration should consume one
measured effect in pinned Photon sources, retain original/mod-absent and disabled
controls, and report compilation, work avoidance, repeated GPU/total-frame timing,
and transition/motion quality separately.

## Checks and ownership boundary

`DistanceBandsTest` and `EffectPolicyTest` cover transition endpoints/centers,
zero-width/touching bands, invalid configuration/runtime inputs, off states,
lighting protection, caller floors, zero work, large integer counts, stable keys,
and bounded monotonic quantization across representative distances.

The isolated implementation adds `ShaderLodEffectConfigTest`,
`EffectUniformFrameTest`, `EffectCommandsTest` and `EffectUniformRegistrationTest`.
They use actual FML sealed config/TOML persistence and reload-event dispatch in
temporary directories; actual Brigadier parsing/ranges; requested/protected
values; frame coherence/shared notifier ownership; and the actual mixin callback
with a fake Iris UniformHolder checking all 43 names/types/defaults. FML config
paths are initialized in temporary directories; no Minecraft registry/bootstrap,
GL context, game client or new testing framework is used. Callback invocation
does not establish that Mixin injection applied in the game.

A minimal build hunk gives tests access to the pinned main API classpath, without
changing production dependencies or JAR packaging. Run `./gradlew test build` in
the interface worktree outside GPU measurement windows. Root must integrate that
hunk while preserving prior main-checkout changes, then check driver fields and
actual consumption in the selected explicit shader adapter. Build/unit checks
are separate from rendering, quality acceptance and performance evidence.

Interface worktree acceptance on 2026-10-05: `./gradlew test build` passed all
60 JUnit tests, zero failures/skips. Production `shaderlod-0.1.0-dev.jar` contains
the effect mixin but no dev-client/JUnit/integration-test classes; Git whitespace
checks passed. Initial runs exposed the existing pure-test classpath restriction
and FML's sealed loaded-config/path setup requirements; the minimal test-only
classpath hunk and real temporary config fixture resolved them. No main-checkout
build, Minecraft client, shader compilation or GPU run was performed by this owner.

## Expected budgets and compatibility inspection

ModernFix targets loading, memory, bugs, world-generation and assorted CPU
costs. FerriteCore primarily reduces memory use. Neither is a shader sampler
optimization, and a large steady-frame improvement in a warmed vanilla scene
is not assumed. Keep ModernFix's experimental dynamic resources at upstream
defaults; enabling a model-loading redesign would be a different experiment.
[ModernFix description](https://modrinth.com/mod/modernfix),
[FerriteCore description](https://modrinth.com/mod/ferrite-core).

ImmediatelyFast batches immediate rendering for entities, particles, text and
HUDs. Its benefit depends on the CPU work visible in the scene. The selected
JAR has explicit Iris compatibility: it accesses `ImmediateState` fields
present in pinned Iris and clears outline buffers at the end of Iris shadow
rendering. Its plugin enables that compatibility only when Iris is installed.
No DH-specific mixin was found in its listed configs. This narrows the static
risk but does not prove the combination renders correctly.
[ImmediatelyFast description/source](https://github.com/RaphiMC/ImmediatelyFast).

The newest README mentions `fix_slow_buffer_upload_on_apple_gpu`; that option
is absent from this 1.21.1 JAR's configuration classes. Its older
`fast_buffer_upload` option exists. Do not attribute Mac measurements to the
newer option or force an unrecognized config field.

ImmediatelyFast also touches GameRenderer and RenderType/buffer flushing.
Its inspected GameRenderer wrappers retain the original render/HUD calls;
they do not cancel ShaderLOD's outer frame-timing methods. However, added
flushes and replacement buffer sources may change the work covered by the
Iris-specific `FullyBufferedMultiBufferSource` profiling hook. Frame timing
remains the comparison metric; do not interpret a disappearing buffered-draw
scope as eliminated cost. Run low-overhead captures with `cpuLayerTiming=false`;
recheck layer scopes before using them for attribution on the optimized stack.

An [open upstream report](https://github.com/RaphiMC/ImmediatelyFast/issues/512)
describes invisible in-world Iris configuration UI on MC 1.21.1 / Iris 1.8.12 /
Sodium 0.6.13 / ImmediatelyFast 1.6.10 with many additional HUD mods. This is
not an established failure of the selected minimal optimizer stack. Check the
in-world shader settings UI; if reproduced, isolate HUD batching and record
the changed configuration. OptiFine/OptiFabric are explicitly unsupported by
ImmediatelyFast and are excluded.

EntityCulling skips hidden entities/block entities using asynchronous visibility
work. Ordinary terrain blocks, clouds, DH terrain and Photon raymarch steps
are not its target. The current forest/cloud scenes suppress mob spawning;
a gain from EntityCulling there cannot be presumed. Use a separate entity-rich
scene with visible and occluded entities. Check shadow casters and block entities
rendering beyond their block bounds. The selected JAR's listed mixins touch
entity/block-entity render dispatch; no explicit Iris/DH-specific class reference
was found in top-level bytecode. Iris behavior still needs a runtime check.
[EntityCulling description](https://modrinth.com/mod/entityculling).

## Benchmark interpretation

Use identical scenes/settings for original, patched-disabled and active packs
within each stack. Keep the mandatory Iris/Sodium versions constant and vary DH
separately. Compare ShaderLOD's incremental gain inside a stack, then report
the stack's independent gain. Keep a manual-radius and simple lower-preset
control, because smaller vanilla detail radius is an existing DH tradeoff.
Balanced run order and repeated complete JVM termination help expose thermal,
cache, background-process and first-launch variance.

The optional stack's loading and visual checks remain unverified at this
research checkpoint. No performance number or general compatibility claim is
established by artifact hashes or advertised project support.

## Durable operation and recovery

`operation.json` records the protocol/operation identity, report and profile
filesystem identities, exact configuration originals/backups and last owned
hashes, mutation intent/acknowledgment, process birth/argv proofs, command sequence,
completed capture hashes, cleanup intents and terminal state. The original
supervisor `session/owner.json` remains authoritative for client/launcher stopping.
The build receipt is retained once as `build-binding.json`; worlds and generated
source trees are not copied into the report.

Normal failure and Ctrl-C enter recovery using the reserved teardown interval.
Expected shutdown writes are acknowledged only when this live controller issues
shutdown from a recorded configuration checkpoint. Full storage checks and the
science deadline do not block recovery commands.

After an interrupted controller has exited, run:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py recover --output dev/logs/my-authorized-run
```

Recovery stops only clients proven by the saved supervisor API, retires only the
proven launcher, waits for the recorded supervisor to exit, then requires an
empty client census, free runtime lane and free save locks. It compares process
birth/argv proofs rather than acting on a reused PID. It refuses a replaced
profile/report root. Configuration restore uses the last recorded owned hash;
it never adopts current bytes after a crash, deletes untracked config files, or
overwrites another owner's changes. Every completed file restore is persisted.

`recover` never reruns a preparation, capture, analysis or completed comparison.
It can be repeated safely. If the controller disappeared during an unacknowledged
mutation, or files changed since their owned checkpoint, uncertain files and
backups remain and `recovery_conflicts` names them. The owner must resolve those
exact files using their recorded backup/provenance. A missing proof is a refusal,
not permission to guess. Terminal recovery is a no-op unless disposal is requested while its profile
identity still matches. A subsequent verified pool reset replaces that identity;
the old report remains historical evidence and cannot authorize changes to the
replacement profile.

## Storage at preparation, run and finalization

Preflight checks 32 GiB plus the declared report/profile allowances on their
actual destination filesystems. Launch uses the existing serialized admission
with a 512 MiB profile-growth forecast, including the 96 GiB workload limit; the
canonical supervisor independently retains its normal admission. No APFS savings
or reduced reserve are assumed.

The operation checks filesystem free bytes and individual console/supervisor/game
log sizes during waits at most once per second. Full metadata checks cover only
its explicit report and selected profile, with a 100,000-entry ceiling. They occur
outside timing windows, never as a broad historical scan. Defaults are 256 MiB per
report, 512 MiB profile growth, 64 MiB per active log and 256 MiB total capture PNGs
in the scoped roots. Generated Iris source export must be Off. A reached limit
stops the attempt and preserves evidence; it never truncates an active log or
silently deletes captures. These are cooperative guard limits, not OS quotas:
one producer burst, the bounded sample interval for full checks, and unrelated
filesystem activity can exceed them. They do not reserve space against other
owners or bound the sum of historical report roots.

| Storage class | Producer and handling |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical scenes, shared packs/mods and other owners' profiles | Protected inputs; no caller deletion or copying into reports. |
| Resettable world-pool slots and world/DH data | Existing pool checkout/reset owns reuse; no hardlinks to writable worlds. Running growth has a declared cap. |
| Generated shader/export fanout | Source export disabled for this protocol; existing exports remain protected and counted. |
| Capture/raw timing evidence | Completed exports hashed and retained. `.storage-keep` pins raw evidence. Missing/invalid exports never pass completion. |
| Text logs | Size checked during waits; retained on success/failure for diagnosis. No active truncation. |
| Preparation/configuration backups | Exact manifested redundant copies retire only after verified terminal restore. Unknown backups remain protected. |
| Shared Gradle/dependency/build caches | Retained reusable inputs; no cache deletion or install by this change. |
| Unknown or historical artifacts | Inventory/preview only; an extension/category or age grants no disposal authority. |

Successful terminal restoration automatically journals and removes only the
operation's exact redundant configuration and supervisor-preparation backup
files. Every original path and backup hash is verified before deletion; unknown
files and pinned trees remain. For a recovered operation, explicitly request the
same narrow finalization with:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py recover --output dev/logs/my-authorized-run \
  --dispose-backups
```

Raw quality/capture evidence is never automatically retired by this caller. The
existing explicit `run_storage.py prune-captures` policy still requires no clients,

It marks retired raw motion evidence as incomplete. Historical maintenance stays
with its authorized owner, and is not run globally at experiment finalization.

Accounting distinguishes logical file length, per-file allocated blocks and
actual destination free bytes. Allocated blocks are not exclusive APFS bytes;

## Request example and path behavior

This 24-second example starts at the existing noDH shoreline player position.
It is an example, not an executed or quality-approved trajectory. Place it in
an ignored prepared runtime directory and use the same request bytes for all
pack arms. The first waypoint must match the prepared `control.json` position
and yaw/pitch within 0.05 blocks/0.1 degrees. Coordinates are **player feet**;
captured `mainCamera` coordinates include the actual interpolated eye height.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "label": "shoreline-motion-r1",
  "warmupSeconds": 30,
  "fps": 10,
  "pngCompressionLevel": 0,
  "waypoints": [
    {"seconds": 0,  "x": 240.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 680.5, "yaw": -180.0, "pitch": 3.0},
    {"seconds": 8,  "x": 244.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 668.5, "yaw": -165.0, "pitch": 5.0},
    {"seconds": 16, "x": 236.5, "y": 69.0, "z": 672.5, "yaw": -195.0, "pitch": 2.0},
    {"seconds": 24, "x": 240.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 680.5, "yaw": -180.0, "pitch": 3.0}
  ]
}
```

Labels accept 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. The source
is parsed to immutable records; exact raw source bytes and their SHA-256 are
retained. The original request is rehashed with bounded reads once each second
and at finalization. Changing it fails the session.

Waypoints number 2–32 and start at time zero. All values must be numeric and
finite. X/Z are within ±29,999,000, Y within ±2048, yaw within ±3600 and pitch
within ±90 degrees. Segment duration is at least 0.25 seconds; total duration is
20–30 seconds and total travel at most 512 blocks. The frame rate is an integer
1–10, and duration must end on a capture slot. Peak eased movement/rotation is
limited to 32 blocks/s and 90 degrees/s. Yaw is unwrapped along the shortest
arc; long intentional rotations need intermediate waypoints.

`pngCompressionLevel` is an optional integer 0 or 1, default **0**. It controls
only the independent Java PNG writer in this explicit quality session. Level 0
uses uncompressed zlib blocks for minimum compression work; level 1 selects
zlib's fast compression. Both preserve exactly the same 8-bit RGBA values.
No frame-rate substitution or global STB compression setting is used. New
requests/labels and loaded capture bytecode distinguish this writer from the
retained legacy `NativeImage.writeToFile` attempts.

The session waits at most 120 seconds for the prepared local singleplayer
spectator and matching first waypoint. It reads server state on the server
thread and requires disabled daylight/weather cycles; it makes no rule, time,
weather, block, entity or shader changes. These controls freeze daylight and
weather, **not** every simulation clock, mob, animation or shader history.
Actual world time/weather and Iris clocks remain in the evidence. Scene
preparation and any decision to freeze additional inputs belong to the runtime
owner.

After acquiring the UUID it holds the first pose for at least 30 seconds and
600 ticks (configurable up to 120 seconds). The owned player's delta movement
is cleared, position and rotation are set at normal Post ticks, and Minecraft's
previous-tick fields provide normal rendered interpolation. The initial snap
uses `setOldPosAndRot()` only before warmup. The moving path uses cubic easing
between waypoints with zero endpoint velocity and deterministic 20 Hz samples.
No OS input, direct mainCamera repositioning or render-frame teleport is used.

Capture scheduling uses path time and the observed render tick delta. Source
wall times are retained separately; slow ticks do not silently become a faster
path. Motion has a 60-second real-time bound. Server scene observations must
complete within five seconds after an owned scene starts. A changed UUID,
dimension, pause/menu, camera entity/type, shader fallback, loaded options,
render radius, framebuffer, control hash or tracked configuration fails the
session. Rain/thunder are required to remain settled during capture. Keep hands
off movement and mouse input during the owned run; source screenshots prove
the actual camera rather than assuming the planned camera was reached.

## Output and bounds

All outputs go to
`<gameDirectory>/camera-quality/<fresh-UUID>/`. Prepared game directories under
`run-workloads/` are already ignored. Do not run against a tracked game
directory or add these generated files to Git. The output root must not be a
symbolic link and resolves directly inside the game directory. Labels and
request content never become paths. Filenames are fixed `request.json`,
`manifest.json` and generated `frame-NNNN.png`; the manifest uses a sibling
temporary file followed by replacement.

The 24-second example requests 241 slots, including start and end; the maximum
is 301. OpenGL readback is on the render thread immediately after the frame's
GUI pass. PNG writing/hashing uses one daemon writer with **one in-flight
image**, no queue of native images. The framebuffer is bounded to 4096×2160
pixels by area (about 34 MiB of RGBA source pixels). The fast writer streams one
`width*4+1` byte scanline plus a 256 KiB compressed chunk and 64 KiB file buffer;
it does not copy the full image into another array. Each PNG is limited to
64 MiB, enforced before writing each chunk. The sequence now has a fixed
**12 GiB PNG budget** with capacity reserved before the next capture, explicitly
approved by root for native lossless quality sequences. The cap is recorded in
the manifest. At 2976×1672, 201 level-0 RGBA frames need about 4.0 GB (3.73 GiB)
plus small PNG/manifest overhead. These bounds do not establish that the
requested 10 FPS capture rate will be achieved. Keep the requested rate; any
missed slots remain explicit rather than being silently reduced.

If a render misses a scheduled slot or the writer is still busy, that slot is
retained as `missed_render_slot` or `writer_backpressure`. The harness never
duplicates a later screenshot to fill missing motion. PNG write completion
returns to the client thread and records hash, size, UTC completion and write
wall time. The final manifest waits for that callback, with a 30-second timeout;
the manifest is also checkpointed after every successful write callback.
An unresolved writer remains explicit in the failed report. A timeout can leave
the daemon writer finishing an owned file, but cannot be called completed
capture evidence.

Each captured checkpoint records actual rendered mainCamera position/yaw/pitch,
local player pose, motion tick/delta, planned/observed path seconds, actual
wall time, session render count, Iris source frame counter and frame-time
sources, the dev GPU frame ID, framebuffer size, world time/weather, actual
loaded pack, capture-boundary archive/options hashes and screenshot completion.
Encoding description, compression level, PNG bit depth/colour type and actual
NativeImage format are recorded for captured frames; skipped slots also record
the selected encoding/level. The manifest records the writer class SHA-256,
native integer byte order and image/disk bounds. File hashes are still computed
from the finished file on disk before callback success, not inferred from the
source image or an encoder's byte count.
GPU frame IDs may stay zero if the existing GPU timer is disabled; they are not
a GPU measurement here. Full loaded shader options, mod versions, initial/start/
end input snapshots, class bytecode identity, exact request/config and advancing
shader temporal inputs are retained in the manifest. Archive hashes are checked
at initial/start/end boundaries; loaded options/config/control are checked each
second. Mid-frame pack reloads are not permitted and need separate coverage.

Statuses distinguish `rejected_request`, `failed`, `incomplete_capture` and
`complete`. A completed sequence requires every requested slot's successful
write callback. Rejected or partial attempts are retained, not erased. Without
`cameraQualityOnly`, the harness restores its acquired player's original pose
when that same UUID remains present. It never stops another process by name.

## Isolated lossless PNG repair: source and standalone checks

`FastPngWriter` writes PNG RGBA8 with filter None and no interlace. It uses a
per-file `java.util.zip.Deflater(level, false)` for PNG's zlib stream, PNG chunk
CRC32 over type+data, big-endian dimensions/lengths, and fixed bounded buffers.
The implementation follows the [W3C PNG specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/png/)
for scanlines, zlib compression and chunk structure. No STB global or GL state
is accessed by the encoder. Existing files are refused with `CREATE_NEW`, and
partial failed outputs are retained.

Exact pinned-source inspection used the cached source archive
`/Users/pippo/.gradle/caches/neoformruntime/intermediate_results/sourcesAndCompiledWithNeoForge_0b59334a24bba2bc8765d4735bf44be048d0ff21_output.jar`:

- `NativeImage.java` source SHA-256:
  `7732dd3894faf6ed0928db8e519132b486cf263bfc0b49e15cb4a28e10027792`.
  The `(width,height,false)` constructor selects `Format.RGBA`;
  `getPixelRGBA(x,y)` reads `MemoryUtil.memGetInt(pixels + (x+y*width)*4)`
  and does not assert the render thread. Public pixel reads are therefore
  available to the owned image writer without reflection/private pointers.
- `Screenshot.java` source SHA-256:

  `takeScreenshot` constructs that RGBA image, calls the existing
  `downloadTexture(0,true)` and `flipY()`. That existing download forces alpha
  opaque. The repair preserves this screenshot/readback behavior exactly and
  does not perform another row flip or alpha transformation.

# Runtime adapter for T3 Code and native agents

The shared assignment/acceptance contract is in [agent operations](AGENT_OPERATIONS.md).
This document maps it to runtime tools; injected current tool contracts take
precedence if names or capabilities change. Check the live catalog before use.

## Delegation and review

Discover T3 provider instances/models with `orchestrator_capabilities`; configured
custom models may be absent from native tool model lists. Select the assigned
model/effort explicitly; preserve user-selected overrides. A provider/model
label does not itself establish a different task authority.

| Operation | Native subagent tools | T3 delegated tasks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Start bounded child work | `spawn_agent` with supported role/model | `delegate_task` with target provider/model; retain returned `taskId` |
| Steer work already executing | `send_message` | Use only currently exposed task-control capabilities; do not message the backing thread as a task continuation |
| Continue a completed worker | `followup_task`; verify acknowledgment | Reuse the supported task continuation; otherwise a new bounded task with current checkpoint/evidence links |
| Independent review round | Fresh reviewer or supported new turn | Only for an unresolved decision-changing objection; distinct request per necessary round, stable on retry |
| Observe / cancel | Native state/events / exact agent interruption | `task_status` / `task_cancel` using `taskId` |

Prefer native same-provider tools when they support the selected model and the
task needs no separate checkout. Use T3 delegation for cross-provider work,
explicitly T3-owned children, unavailable native models, or a separate worktree.
Retain accepted task identities before retrying ambiguous launch responses;
inspect actual state to avoid duplicates. Never use `t3_thread_send` on a delegated
`childThreadId` to start another review round. That thread is backing storage.

Top-level `t3_thread_launch`/`create_threads` create ordinary user conversations.
Use them only when the user explicitly requests separate/new/top-level threads.
They are not the implementation of a request for subagents or parallel work.

## Worktrees and handoff

For a child needing another checkout use T3 `delegate_task` with
`isolation: "worktree"`. It starts from the parent local commit; uncommitted edits
are not copied. The preparation entry point is
`python3 scripts/setup_agent_worktree.py`; inspect its help for options. Do not
commit, copy the dirty checkout, or move an attached thread merely to satisfy an
assumption about isolation. Parent chooses a deliberate snapshot/patch handoff
when the task depends on uncommitted inputs, and verifies those inputs arrived.
Keep runtime worlds, captures and client ownership outside speculative worktrees.

The T3 preparation action invokes the canonical project's read-only setup script
with the new checkout as `--root`. This deliberately bootstraps older committed
bases that lack the new script; it does not copy uncommitted source into a child.
Any source needed beyond that bootstrap still requires an explicit input handoff.
The checkout's STATUS and instructions can also be old commit snapshots. Include
the canonical current STATUS path, current human scope and resource-owner terms
in the child brief; do not treat branch-local historical state as a new authority.

A task cancellation or thread stop does not by itself establish that an external
SSH process, GPU client or local child has exited. Retain exact process identity
and its stop/recovery path, then verify actual state before releasing ownership.
Keep one continuation owner and one stdout reader for each operation.

# Opt-in detailed terrain cap

The geometry prototype caps the **effective** vanilla render radius while DH
keeps its existing long reach. It is disabled by default and requires explicit
confirmation that the current scene's replacement ring has warmed DH terrain.
This is an existing vanilla/DH geometry tradeoff exposed as a reversible policy;
it does not add a mesh renderer or promise a particular speedup.

## Configuration and wiring

```toml
[terrain]
enabled = false
vanillaChunkCap = 16
warmSourceConfirmed = false
warmupSeconds = 30
```

The main ShaderLOD enable flag must also be true. `vanillaChunkCap` accepts
8–32 chunks, and warmup accepts 5–120 seconds. Enable the policy only in a world
whose DH replacement terrain you have inspected and warmed; then set
`warmSourceConfirmed=true`. The acknowledgement binds to that loaded world /
dimension instance. A true value carried to another world does not certify its
cache; clear it and re-confirm after inspecting that scene.

The main constructor registers the client event handler once:

```java
NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.addListener(GeometryLodController::onClientTick);
```

`GeometryLodController.status()` exposes active/requested/effective radius,
configured cap, eligibility reason, API failure detail, and stable/warmup tick
counts for a HUD or diagnostic command. No new shader uniform or sampler is
required. Geometry can use original Photon while ShaderLOD is loaded; that
allows a geometry-only comparison with original shadow/AO quality.

## Behavior

An injection at `Options.getEffectiveRenderDistance()` return applies
`min(originalEffectiveDistance, cap)` only while the cached policy is active.
It never writes the raw `renderDistance` option, `options.txt`, or the client's
broadcast render preference. A manual or server-imposed radius below the cap
remains below it. If the user changes the requested radius while capped, turning
the policy off recovers that **current** value rather than an old snapshot.

Sodium and the pinned DH NeoForge wrapper both read this getter, so DH's vanilla
overdraw boundary sees the same radius as detailed rendering. The policy does
not modify DH128 (or any configured DH distance), its mesh quality, or terrain
generation. It also changes other consumers of the effective radius, including
vanilla fog/entity view scaling; this is a radius policy, not merely a draw-call
cache. Inspect the vanilla/DH seam, water and shadow coverage.

Sodium detects an effective-distance change in `setupTerrain` and rebuilds its
renderer. Use fixed caps and explicit changes; do not tune this value from noisy
per-frame FPS. Initial enable/disable and changing the cap are excluded from
steady-state timings until rebuild/upload and terrain overlap settle.

## Readiness and restoration

At client tick boundaries (nominally 20Hz), the controller requires a loaded
world, an active Iris shader pipeline with a DH terrain program and initialized
DH compatibility instance, and public DH API world/config readiness with DH
rendering enabled. Those checks use the exact pinned Iris seams and cached
reflection handles for the optional public DH API. The hot getter performs no
reflection, config reads, allocations, GL calls, or renderer reloads.

A stable world/pipeline/readiness interval must reach the configured warmup.
Policy/mod disable, DH rendering disable, Iris fallback/failure and unload
recover the original effective radius by the next client tick. World/dimension
identity changes also bypass the cap immediately in the getter, before the next
tick. Null/uninitialized DH API, absent DH, and API linkage failures fail open
with a diagnostic reason. The code never calls Iris `DHCompat.checkFrame()` or
`hasRenderingEnabled()` from an Options getter, because those methods can cause
pipeline reloads.

**Readiness is not a cache-coverage proof.** Initialized renderer resources and
30 seconds elapsed cannot establish that every replacement chunk exists. The
prototype therefore requires the explicit scene acknowledgement and is intended
for inspected, warmed scenes. Disable it before exploring uncached areas; a cold
cache does not become safe merely because DH is installed. Automatic coverage
verification/recovery while traveling is future work and this feature should not
be marketed as an automatic universal geometry LOD solution.

```sh
./gradlew compileJava test --console=plain
```

boundary, server/manual limits, current-preference restoration, safe cap bounds,
and acknowledgement isolation across worlds/dimensions. Build success does not
establish mixin application, actual DH overlap, or performance.

and verify restoration. Inspect cold-cache behavior with confirmation false,
near objects, distant tree silhouettes/shadows, the boundary and moving water.

# Experimental frame-local shadow frustum coherence

Candidate implemented in isolated worktree
`/Users/pippo/.codex/worktrees/frustum-coherence/shaderlod` from `5a06ccd`.
Main checkout is untouched. After the coordinator released a CPU window,
`./gradlew build compileDevClientJava` passed with all 29 JUnit tests, including
nine new coherence fixtures. No game or benchmark was launched by this worker.
This is a default-off independent option, with no performance claim.

## What is avoided

Several Sodium section AABBs can occupy the same small spatial neighborhood
during one frustum traversal. A proven containing coarse box permits its valid
contained children to return visible without repeating all plane FMAs and
rejecting distance-box tests. Partial/outside/unproved coarse boxes still use
the exact original per-child path. No section is dropped, no shader budget or
radius is changed, and every visibility graph traversal still runs.

`ShadowFrustumCoherence` uses 64 fixed direct-mapped slots. The cell key comes
from each child minimum endpoint on a 64-block grid; its containing proof box
extends 96 blocks along each axis. Every call verifies actual float containment
and child finite/ordered endpoints before consulting a proof. Large boxes that
do not fit, NaNs/infinities, inverted endpoints and unknown/malformed planes
fall back. Hash collisions compare all three cell coordinates and never reuse
another cell's proof. Negative proof entries only avoid repeated coarse proof;
they never reject an individual child.

The helper owns three `int[64]` key arrays and one `byte[64]` proof array: 832
raw bytes plus headers/object fields, roughly 1 KiB per initialized frustum,
subject to actual JVM layout. It is lazily allocated on the first enabled
candidate test. There are no per-child allocations, reflection, config reads
or GL calls. New-frustum initialization still allocates this bounded storage,
which can be a material cost if Iris creates frusta every frame.

## Strict proof, rather than trusting Iris's INSIDE code

Pinned Iris's positive acceptance evaluates

`fma(px,x, fma(py,y, pz*z)) >= -pw`

while its negative/fully-inside expression folds `pw` into a third nested FMA.
Those have different rounding near the boundary. Its return value 1 cannot be
used as a general float-safe containment proof.

A concrete counterexample is plane `(1e20f,-1e20f,-1f,-0.5f)`, coarse AABB
`(1,0,0)..(2,1,1)`, and its contained point `(1,1,1)`. The original full
classifier can call the coarse box fully inside while rejecting the point,
under both FMA and separate arithmetic. A written test captures that behavior.

This candidate instead evaluates the **original positive expression** at the
coarse box's sign-selected minimum and maximum vertices, with the original
FMA policy and grouping. It requires finite plane coefficients and finite
results at both extrema, plus minimum result `>= -pw`. Finite contained child
positive vertices are bounded componentwise in the coefficient-selected order.
Float multiplication/addition/FMA with fixed finite coefficients preserve
that weak order; finite extreme evaluations exclude intermediate overflow/NaN
cases that could break the acceptance implication. Signed zero comparisons
remain Java `<0`, not raw sign-bit tests, and tangency remains inclusive.
Thus every accepted cached child satisfies its original positive acceptance
on every plane. Unproved values retain original behavior through fallback.

The coarse box must also lie **fully inside every rejecting distance box**:
each minimum at least `-maxDistance` and each maximum at most `maxDistance`.
Merely calling `BoxCuller.isCulledSodium(coarse)==false` would prove overlap,
not containment. The accessor reads the immutable pinned `maxDistance` field
without reflection. Missing primary cullers use an unbounded constraint;
NaN/negative limits cannot create a fast proof.

For reversed frusta, `distanceCuller` is rejecting, but the inherited primary
box is an **early acceptance**. A plane proof only needs the rejecting distance
constraint. When no proof exists, the original order remains distance reject,
alternate-box accept, then original classifier (or the separately enabled
old math experiment). The new option does not enable that older option.

`ShadowCullingFrustumMixin` retains the pinned testAab fallback and adds a
coherence attempt before it only when the separate cached controller is active.
The base-injected interface exposes that helper to the reversed subclass,
avoiding inherited-shadow declarations in its child mixin.

The pinned `prepare` body first updates its box-culler position, then x/y/z.
The overwrite preserves that exact order and invalidates all slots. The pinned
private `addPlane(float[])` is the sole plane-array insertion/count mutator;
its overwrite preserves assignment/increment and invalidates proofs. Count,
plane-array reference, FMA policy or rejecting-limit changes also reset the
helper's context. Existing plane arrays are only populated during construction

No CallbackInfo/Operation wrapper is introduced by these overwrites. Inactive

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.
