# Projected procedural detail LOD source freeze

2026-10-05. Owner: `procedural_lod`; bounded read-only mathematics advisor:
`procedural_lod/parallax_math`. Source implementation is private, default off,
experimental and **unaccepted for quality or performance**. Neither worker owned
clients, shader reloads or GPU measurement. Root retains runtime ownership.

## Scope and actual interface

General carrier/modulator footprint weighting lives in
`shaderpacks/photon-procedural-lod/shaders/include/shaderlod/procedural_footprint.glsl`.
It accepts caller-supplied procedural coordinate partials in units per raster
pixel, a carrier in cycles per coordinate unit and a modulation gradient bound.
It uses those units directly; camera distance alone does not select an octave.
The explicit Photon consumer retains 1..8 `WATER_WAVE_ITERATIONS` options.
No universal rewriting, other pack support or default preset change is introduced.

Only two upstream members are patched: `shaders/settings.glsl` and
`shaders/program/gbuffers_all_translucent.fsh`. Three private helper files are
added. The original water source, its Belmu Gerstner comment, original Photon
LICENSE (also included in this derivative source directory), all shadow/caustic code and DH entry points remain unchanged. Relevant
entry points are world0/world-1/world1 `gbuffers_water.fsh`, through the common
translucent program, only with `PROGRAM_GBUFFERS_WATER` and `WATER_WAVES`.
Hand-water and other programs do not select the private route.

The sole added pack option is `SHADERLOD_PROCEDURAL_FOOTPRINT`, commented out by
default. The selected route checks existing core `shaderlodBridgeVersion == 2`
and `shaderlodEnabled == 1`. It consumes no extension1 per-effect fields, near/far
mod config or new Java API. Near/far and footprint thresholds below are explicit
private source policy, not a verified mod-config connection. Actual uniform
linkage/readback for this derivative is pending.

## Footprint, work avoidance and fallback

The unchanged Photon normal evaluates **three**, not five, height samples at
`coord`, `coord+(0.1,0)` and `coord+(0,0.1)`. This revision retains those finite
differences, the original normal influence, flow classification, rain/skylight
and grazing suppression. It does not use the prior analytic-gradient approximation.

Full original normal evaluation remains selected through 32 Minecraft blocks.
A smoothstep from 32 to 48 blocks enables footprint filtering. Each octave's
carrier-plus-noise upper phase-frequency bound is evaluated using the actual
raster partials of its procedural coordinate. Squared sine has a second harmonic:
weights fade between 0.125 and 0.25 fundamental cycles per raster pixel (eight to
four pixels per fundamental cycle). The first octave always stays full; full-N
amplitude normalization remains unchanged. Footprint weights are computed once
and shared by the three height evaluations.

Zero-weight octaves skip noise lookup and trigonometry **before** that work.
Each omitted octave contributes its exact uniform-phase mean, 3/8, multiplied
by its original amplitude. Low-frequency height variation remains sampled and
multiplies the entire mean-containing field. This avoids amplifying the coarse
wave through reduced-N normalization or lowering mean height merely by dropping
amplitudes. Retained coarse height/slope amplitudes are preserved.

This is not a calibrated conditional noise mean or a guarantee of equivalent
normal variance/specular energy. High-frequency slope variance is intentionally
removed; no BRDF roughness compensation is applied. The modulation bound is an
upper bound, so it can conservatively overfilter actual resolved detail. Near
identity and phase mean do not establish distant sun-glint parity. The angle
fixture below exposes a material quality risk that runtime review must resolve.

`WATER_PARALLAX=true` is supported. Before any discard, the first `main` block
initializes coordinates in all invocations, reproduces upstream corrected TBN and
flow setup, and evaluates full-quality parallax on water primitives when core
activation is valid. Glass does not run that height march. Returned coordinates
are reused at the original parallax site. After the material branch and adaptive
while have completed, unconditional `dFdx/dFdy` calls capture actual displaced
coordinates before the later material/normal LOD branch. Thus this does not guess
a world-distance ray cone or reuse the unwarped coordinate footprint.

[GLSL 4.10 section 3.8.2](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.4.10.pdf)
says uniform control resumes after divergent substatements complete. Derivatives
at that reconverged point are raster approximations, not exact analytic Jacobians.
All operands are initialized, there is no discard or shader exit before capture,
and material/TBN inputs are flat within a primitive. Derivatives of the validity
flag execute in separate unconditional statements, avoiding short-circuit evaluation.

The full-height/parallax private clone preserves original arithmetic/loop counts
and only qualifies noise samples at explicit LOD0, plus invalid-path guards. Pinned
Photon custom `image/noise.png` is 512²; its mcmeta says blur=true/clamp=false.
Pinned Iris custom-PNG upload bytecode selects LINEAR min/mag and level-zero upload.
Reduced height uses explicit `textureGrad` with captured partials. These paths
introduce no implicit-gradient sample inside new dynamic control. Actual sampler
binding/mip state and driver sampling equivalence still require runtime readback;
upstream texture syntax alone does not prove undefined sampling with a no-mip
texture. Full near normal calls remain literal original; active full parallax is
mathematically preserved but no bit-identical GPU claim is made.

Zero initial height, singular/reversed tangent direction, singular interpolation,
nonfinite coordinates or excessive march count mark the private coordinate invalid.
The original downstream parallax/normal route remains the fallback, including
upstream behavior on those inputs; the private safety guards do not claim to fix
an upstream zero-height interpolation issue. A quad validity boundary also selects
full normal. Large parallax footprint amplification fades filtering out between
2× and 4× the unwarped footprint; at 4× full original normal is selected. This
protects unstable displaced-coordinate regions without a hard normal switch.

Private option off or other programs restore every upstream source byte after
resolving only new guards. Core absent/unknown or global off retains original
parallax and normal work. Enabled-source/global-off can retain small derivative/
control overhead; it is a distinct timing arm from pure original. Singular
persistence >=2.0 also falls back; Photon itself has singular full normalization
at persistence2.0, so this is baseline retention, not a mathematical repair.

## Static and mathematical evidence

Executed `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_photon_procedural_lod.py -v`:
**13 tests passed, no skips**, under approximately one second on this host.

Checks include exact private-off/nonselected upstream source restoration; unchanged
license/water/shadow/DH members; fail-closed source/helper/archive pins and output
scope; original full-height arithmetic restoration after reversing only sample
qualification; scalar full near identity; full-N/coarse amplitude retention;
exact 3/8 phase mean; bounded bilinear noise variation; smooth distance/footprint/
parallax-confidence boundaries; 1..8 octave fetch omission; flow/noise repeat
seams/height-variation/frequency/persistence/ray safeguards.

Actual pinned Iris `OptionAnnotatedSource`, `OptionSet` and `MutableOptionValues`
ran through its real Java lexer. Complete settings/program/stage inputs retain
exact baseline boolean options/references plus the sole private gate. The upstream
shared program already references `PROGRAM_GBUFFERS_WATER`; this test checks no
additional stage leak rather than wrongly asserting baseline absence. Default
false/true and both overrides pass. This is option parsing, not driver compilation.

The independently expressed scalar parallax reference differs by at most
`3.457650183405701e-13` coordinate units in the chosen fixture set. Neighboring
actual mapped coordinates produce up to `249.7361861445753`× footprint expansion,
with five terminal-count switches, supporting the explicit confidence fallback.
Normal fixtures using actual pinned green-channel noise, 1/3/8 octaves, several
flows/times and influence values through 0.38 produce a maximum sampled angular
change of **22.115413607216066 degrees** when fine waves are fully filtered. Near
change is zero in the scalar model. This is a finite fixture envelope, not a
worst-case proof or a perceptual acceptance bound. Distant quality is unaccepted.

No client, Gradle build, GL shader compiler, runtime reload, driver program linkage,
physical texture-count observation or GPU timing ran on this track. No performance
claim follows from skipped source statements or these tests.

# Agent operations

## Choose and bound the operation

[STATUS](STATUS.md) alone owns current scope, authorization, allocation and last
observed state. Use `python3 scripts/project_checkpoint.py show docs/STATUS.md`;
read linked goal sections relevant to the task. Maintenance does not resume a
paused or unobserved runtime campaign.

For an existing-concept port, name the working implementation, missing joins and
actual selected public consumer. Prepare the changed consumer and authentic
caller inputs together, then bind the integrated artifact. For an optimization,
identify active native work and take an early matched original/control/enabled/
return cost and quality observation. An inactive effect is coverage, not a gain.
Use [EVALUATION](EVALUATION.md) for the claim; a manual preview or control increment
does not require every historical performance protocol first.

Put the relevant assignment details in the worker message or existing attempt;
no new form or launch gate is required:

- **Outcome:** family/version/loader/dimension, preset, selected consumer and next
  user-visible result; for work reduction, native → selected active work.
- **Reuse:** working implementation, pinned inputs and valid unchanged evidence.
- **Ownership:** exact files/worktree, dependencies, exclusive resource owner,
  allowed actions and report destination.
- **Acceptance:** authentic input and real entry point, checks and evidence limits.
- **Budget and handback:** review/stopping boundary covering setup, workers,
  repairs and handoffs; changes, actual checks, evidence and exact owned processes.

Rank hypotheses by active removable work, likely total benefit, uncertainty,
effort and visual risk. Batch cheap independent defects with saved inputs and
[preflight](EXPERIMENT_PREFLIGHT.md); stop diagnostic work when the actual consumer
answers the question. The parent targets the next useful result and explains the
main delay across preparation, rendering and evaluation. Repeated same-cause
failure or an overrun of the roughly 15-minute auxiliary review budget calls for
a simplify/justify-extension/switch decision. If uncertainty remains, use one
bounded independent proceed/change/park review, with no execution or allocation
authority; do not add a standing supervisor. Preserve healthy allocated work and
closed negative trials.

## Assignments and integration

Partition by remaining dependencies, not automatically one worker per shader.
Shared API/resource repairs have one owner and one integration. Keep authentic
caller preparation with consumer ownership through handback; do not accumulate
patches awaiting unassigned caller work. Parent accepts actual artifacts/checks,
with independent review for consequential correctness or speed claims.

Repository role briefs under `.codex/agents/` describe domain responsibilities;
use [the runtime adapter](T3_AGENT_RUNTIME.md) for actual availability, dispatch,
review rounds, worktree setup and cancellation. A child handback does not finish
the parent outcome or transfer a client lane.

## Client, build and GPU ownership

Before launch, reconcile actual availability with the last observation. Record
hardware, component pins, scene, command, session, PID/birth/argv, finite deadline
and exact stop procedure. Use existing `scripts/dev_client.py` supervision and
exact-client stop APIs where supported; never kill by broad process name.
Remote hosts and allowed actions come from current STATUS authority.

Quiet measurements exclude source edits, builds, tests, encoders and unrelated
CPU work unless the protocol permits them. An untimed control operation can
release independent source preparation when its owner permits it. Do not change
a live freeze or reinterpret its quiet contract. Verify exact termination and
save/lock release before reporting the lane free. Analysis follows the operation's
executable restore/verify/release path without consuming its recovery allowance.

Build success, startup, in-world rendering, DH terrain, active feature consumption,
quality and speed remain separate evidence. Record hardware/OS; one platform does
not qualify another. Use [benchmark storage](BENCHMARK_STORAGE.md) for capacity/
retention and the [finite speed caller](RENDERER_BRACKET_CONSUMER.md) for supported
tuples. Adoption uses the actual normal producer, compiled resource and caller,
with the current receipt rather than an old staged patch. Keep final freeze/
preflight/deadline stamping/launch in one local operation once callers are ready.
Version-specific builds use their documented executables.

For maintained non-Photon adapters, use the builder's `--sync-resources` preview
and explicit `--apply`; do not hand-copy recipes into ten builds. See
[verified commands and limits](DEVELOPMENT_THROUGHPUT_REVIEW_20261012.md).

## Implementation and source contract

Pinned Sodium 0.6.13 `RenderRegion` owns one persistent mutable
`ChunkRenderList`. Its public constructor takes `RenderRegion`; the getter
returns that original list. Pinned Iris 1.8.12 has separate outer shadow lists,
but collector membership still aliases those region objects. Exact source
revision, local ignored review files and annotated bytecode are recorded in
`VISIBILITY_REUSE_AUDIT.md`.

New production components:

- `ShadowListStorage<T>` holds the original and lazily constructs one alternate
  shadow list. There is no static owner map or saved world/manager reference.
- `ShadowRegionListsMixin` overwrites only Sodium `RenderRegion.getRenderList`.
  Disabled/main paths return the original field. An active shadow getter lazily
  creates owner-local storage and `new ChunkRenderList(thisRegion)`.
- `ShadowVisibilityListsController` caches one active boolean. Per-region
  getters perform no config/Iris pack inspection, GL call or reflection.
- `ShadowVisibilityListsRuntime` reads config and existing Photon names once
  per client tick, requiring global enablement, an in-world shader pack,
  recognized Photon and no Iris fallback.
- `rendering.separateShadowVisibilityLists=false` is the new experimental
  default. NeoForge's client tick listener and both mixins are registered.
  Sodium's pinned artifact is added to main compile-only inputs; its runtime
  remains required by Iris exactly as before.

Lists are owner-local and allocated only on the first eligible shadow visit.
The noncapturing constructor function is initialized once on the transformed
class, not per getter. This adds a storage object, one shadow list and its three
`byte[256]` arrays per shadow-visited region; roughly 0.9–1.1 KiB per region
with typical compressed-reference HotSpot layout, an estimate pending actual
heap inspection. Main/disabled getters retain the original object identity.
Disabling/re-enabling keeps the same alternate storage for that live region;
forced traversals still repopulate it. World/manager replacement constructs
new regions/storage, allowing the old graph to be collected normally.

## Exact existing sprite-consumer behavior

This requirement prevents a superficially correct list split from silently
changing animated-shadow texture activation.

Pinned `RenderSectionManager.tickVisibleRenders` iterates its **main outer
container**, even during shadow setup. In the original shared-list design,
regions visited during that shadow traversal have their inner arrays overwritten
with shadow membership; regions not visited keep their preceding main data.
Regions not in that main outer container are not visited by this sprite tick.

`ShadowSpriteListsMixin` redirects only its
`ChunkRenderList.sectionsWithSpritesIterator()` invocation. In an active shadow
phase, for each existing main-container entry it returns the shadow iterator
only when that owner's alternate list has the current manager
`lastUpdatedFrame`. Otherwise it returns the original main iterator. The caller
continues using the same region and same section/sprite iteration. Main and
disabled paths invoke the original iterator directly. No region is added to
the outer container; no stamp is rewritten; no sprite is ticked by a new hook.

This reproduces the original shared-array selection using existing generation
provenance. It is not a change to "tick all shadow sprites" or broad animation
policy. Frame-wrap equality follows the same original integer-generation
comparison; no elapsed-time or camera-distance substitute is introduced.

The membership fixture models main regions A/B/C and shadow visits B/D, with
an older shadow list for C. Legacy shared arrays and separated sprite selection
both produce `[A sprites, current B shadow sprites, C main sprites]`; D is
excluded because it was not in the original main container. This test passed.
Actual transformed generation/order behavior still
requires runtime evidence.

## Preparing profiles

Stop clients using the source and destination worlds before copying. The script
checks `session.lock` with a POSIX advisory lock and fails if a world is open.
It does not stop or launch games.

```sh
python3 scripts/build_shaderpack.py
python3 scripts/setup_comparison.py --dry-run
python3 scripts/setup_comparison.py
```

Defaults: source `run/saves/ShaderLOD-Smoke`; destination save name
`ShaderLOD-Landscape`; vanilla render distance **24 chunks** (384 blocks),
simulation distance 8, DH radius **128 chunks** (2,048 blocks), two DH processing
threads with a 0.5 runtime ratio, and background DH generation disabled.
The development client chooses the camera after loading. Preparation does not
alter the source save or add artificial geometry.

The source DH database audit found 16,377 detail-0 sections with X/Z positions
-64 through 63, and coarser levels through detail 8. This establishes cached
data exists; visible distant terrain must still be verified in-world. Use a
scenic camera beyond the sparse fixture near the origin.

`--render-distance 16|24|32` select matched settings. `--source`,
`--source-world`, `--output`, and `--pack` override their respective paths.
`--generate` enables `SURFACE_THEN_CHUNKS` for warm-up; disable generation and
wait for processing queues to settle before measuring. A larger radius does

## Important input limitation

Source auditing after these captures found that Photon uses Iris's smoothed
wetness for weather humidity/wind. The reports verify rain level but do not
capture actual wetness. Its pinned rising half-life is effectively 60 seconds;
35 seconds after changing a clear save to rain does not prove convergence.
Reused storm saves can begin already raining on subsequent JVM runs and alter
initialization. This is a plausible mechanism, not a demonstrated explanation
of any particular timing. Treat these results as exploratory and retain them.

Loaded options and camera checks do not prove settled terrain upload work,
unchanging driver clocks, heap state, or every temporal shader input. GPU elapsed
intervals include driver/command gaps, not busy-time utilization. Per-run p95,
range and MAD are in the raw analysis; three repeats provide no significance
claim. Concurrent preview windows are not the source of these serial numbers.

## The important Iris allocation constraint

Inspection of the exact JAR with `javap -p -c` found:

- `gl.sampler.SamplerLimits` reads GL enum 34930 (`GL_MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS`),
  the fragment-stage limit, for `maxTextureUnits`.
- `samplers.IrisSamplers` sets `COMPOSITE_RESERVED_TEXTURE_UNITS` to `{1,2}`.
- `pipeline.CompositeRenderer` passes that set into `ProgramBuilder.begin`.
- `gl.program.ProgramSamplers$Builder` begins with
  `remainingUnits = maxTextureUnits - reservedTextureUnits.size()`.
- Its `addDynamicSampler` checks the linked uniform location and skips `-1`
  uniforms. Several names registered for one sampler supplier share one unit.
  It does not allocate a unit merely because an unused uniform was declared.

Thus a 16-fragment-texture-unit host has **14 dynamically allocatable units in
these deferred/composite programs under this Iris version**, before checking
whether the underlying GL program could physically use 16. The limit is not
simply a count of global GLSL declarations, nor is the final error's sampler
necessarily the feature causing exhaustion. Registration order matters.

These observations refer to exact JAR classes, not an assumed current GitHub

possibly duplicated material reconstruction/visibility sampling; its gain
cannot be assumed on this tile-based GPU. Establish a per-pass live-sampler
table and link it, compare images/motion against the original SSR path on a
host that can run it, then benchmark total frame cost with SSR enabled/disabled.

vanilla distance as shader-ray savings. This would be one explicit pinned

# Sparse visibility-list phase observer

Development diagnostics only. The observer runs after original
`RenderSectionManager.createTerrainRenderList` traversals and never skips,
cancels or changes them. It does not write world/list/sprite state, issue GL work,
read back GPU data or authorize visibility reuse. Keep it out of performance
profiles; its bounded reflection, iterators, hashing and snapshot allocations
are deliberate diagnostic overhead.

## Coordinator wiring

Register dev mixin class `VisibilityListPhaseMixin`.
Set JVM property `shaderlod.dev.visibilityLists=true` for dedicated diagnostic
captures only. Default is false. Property-disabled and unarmed callbacks return
before phase/world/list reads or reflection. Class initialization allocates
empty report storage once. Report serialization allocates outside the callback.
The non-cancellable RETURN mixin itself has ordinary Mixin callback dispatch;
this is not a claim that registering the mixin eliminates all framework overhead.

Use the public API on
`com.pp.shaderlod.dev.timing.VisibilityListPhaseObserver`:

```java
VisibilityListPhaseObserver.beginMeasurement(); // After warmup and actual option/config checks.
VisibilityListPhaseObserver.snapshot();         // Immutable report; does not perform live snapshots.
VisibilityListPhaseObserver.endMeasurement();  // Disarm and release borrowed live references.
```

A property alone does not arm sampling. `beginMeasurement()` resets reports and
arms the next eligible shadow traversal. Capture at most eight attempts/pairs,
at least 30 render frames apart. Failed/unmatched attempts consume the budget;
they are retained as unknown/error information rather than silently retried
until eight successes. A pending sampled shadow may pair with a main traversal
within two game render frames on the same manager/world. Another shadow
traversal first discards the sample, avoiding false attribution of shadow
rebuild changes to the main pass. Manager/world changes, backward frame IDs or
larger gaps similarly discard pending pairs. If main graph traversal does not
occur, report that absence rather than treating a normal draw as a rewrite.

## Bounds and report schema

Each outer scan is capped at 512 region entries. Up to eight inner regions are
selected from shadow outer order. Sprite models are capped at 4,096 section
indices per phase and per compared selection. Region membership arrays are
bounded by pinned Sodium's 256-section region implementation. Reports retain
at most 16 error messages plus total error counts. An incomplete outer scan or
sprite budget overrun is explicitly marked; prefix hashes cannot establish
complete-list preservation.

`Report` contains enable/arm state, bounds, phase calls/attempts/pair count,
unmatched samples/errors, actual Iris field availability, optional ShaderLOD
controller availability, a pending frame and `pairs`.
Each `Pair` contains shadow/main render frame IDs, manager/traversal generation
numbers, manager/world identity tokens, four outer summaries, region rows,
shadow/main sprite models and an explicit diagnostic-only scope.

Outer summaries distinguish:

- Outer object identity and ordered region/list identity hash.
- Ordered region chunk-coordinate hash.
- Ordered source-generation/geometry/sprite/entity count hash.
- Scan completeness and unavailable/truncated status.

For sampled region rows, source/original/shadow membership preserves list
identity token, generation, counts and ordered geometry/sprite/entity index
hashes before/after main traversal. Flags report separate shadow storage,
shadow fingerprint unchanged, original fingerprint changed and borrowed shadow
source fingerprint changed. `mainOuterOverlap` is true/false for a complete
main scan; null means no overlap seen in an incomplete prefix. The first eight
shadow regions are a sample, not proof about every overlapping region.

Java identity tokens/hashes are process-local and may collide; they are
inspection aids, never correctness/permission keys. Coordinate hashes are
portable order descriptors, but generation/count hashes need matching phase
and state context. Do not compare raw identity values across separate clients.
Fingerprints do not establish mesh revisions, GPU draw parity or image quality.

## Sprite-selection model and its limits

The read-only model visits main outer region lists, as pinned
`tickVisibleRenders()` does. It reads public `ShadowVisibilityListsController.isActive()`
when available and optional per-region shadow accessors. In a shadow phase it
models selecting the separate shadow list only when its generation matches
manager `lastUpdatedFrame`; otherwise it uses the original list. With ShaderLOD
absent/inactive, it models shared original-list selection. Lookup failures are
unknown/error evidence, not proof of baseline semantics.

The comparison hypothesis is independently derived from the *actual current
Iris shadow outer traversal*: for a main-container region visited in that
shadow generation, its current shadow outer membership represents what the
original shared array would have received; otherwise use original membership.
Hashes include region chunk coordinates, sprite-section count and ordered local
section indices. The report includes source choice counts, bounded membership
hashes and nullable `matchesCurrentTraversalSharedHypothesis`.

This is a model of section selection, not instrumentation of actual
`SpriteUtil.markSpriteActive` execution, sprite array contents, animated alpha,
texture updates or GPU draws. Different earlier shared-array histories can
also differ from this current-traversal hypothesis. A matching model does not
verify the redirect actually executed or certify visual parity; inspect real
water/animated texture behavior separately.

# Shared diagnostic work trace

2026-10-05. Schema 1 is an explicit, sampler-free diagnostic API in
[work_trace.glsl](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/work_trace.glsl).
The first consumer is the separately owned Photon volume diagnostic reference.
This API does not instrument or rewrite shader sources, register uniforms,
declare a shader option, allocate attachments, or change the work policy.

The [volume audit](SHARED_VOLUME_WORK_AUDIT.md) shows why negotiated counts cannot
stand in for executed work: a coarser march can visit more occupied cells or miss
an early exit. The counters below increment at reached operations independently
of budget metadata. They count instrumented shader source evaluations; they do
not measure hardware texture transactions, GPU time or production speed.

## Storage and calls

The caller supplies the private, default-off `SHADERLOD_WORK_TRACE` shader
option and includes the helper. An enabled shader owns one `ShaderlodWorkTrace`
per fragment invocation, either as a local or an invocation-local GLSL global.
Declare with **no trailing semicolon**; the declaration macro owns it. Other
macros use ordinary statement semicolons:

```glsl
#include "/include/shaderlod/work_trace.glsl"
SHADERLOD_TRACE_DECLARE(adapter_trace)

// Once at fragment entry, before any instrumented operation:
SHADERLOD_TRACE_INIT(adapter_trace);

// When the actual selected path and its budgets are known:
SHADERLOD_TRACE_SELECT(adapter_trace, original_uint, requested_float,
    selected_float, SHADERLOD_TRACE_PATH_ADAPTED, reason_uint);

// Each call must sit at its declared, reached operation:
SHADERLOD_TRACE_PRIMARY(adapter_trace);
SHADERLOD_TRACE_DENSITY(adapter_trace);
SHADERLOD_TRACE_SECONDARY(adapter_trace);
SHADERLOD_TRACE_TEXTURE(adapter_trace);

#ifdef SHADERLOD_WORK_TRACE
counts_out = shaderlod_trace_encode(adapter_trace, 0u);
selection_out = shaderlod_trace_encode(adapter_trace, 1u);
schema_out = shaderlod_trace_encode(adapter_trace, 2u);
#endif
```

`INIT` clears counters and sets valid zero metadata/path NONE. `SELECT` sets
metadata without resetting counters. `PRIMARY`, `DENSITY`, `SECONDARY` and
`TEXTURE` each add exactly one to their independent uint counter. Instrument
the original and adapted paths using the same declared operation scopes. Never
populate counts by multiplying a negotiated budget or by anticipating loop
iterations, density occupancy, early exits or texture branches. Repeated texture
expressions require one marker each, immediately at the expressions; a marker
before a branch containing optional fetches overcounts them.

Each adapter must document primary iteration boundaries, which density
functions and secondary loops are counted, and which source texture-value
evaluations are included. `textureSize` is metadata and is not a texture-value
evaluation. Reaching a density function that immediately returns still counts
one density evaluation; its unreached texture expressions count zero. A
secondary visit and its density call are distinct counters. These scopes can
overlap and must not be added as a universal work total.

`SHADERLOD_TRACE_INVALIDATE(trace)` marks unsupported or incomplete instrumentation
invalid. Metadata failure and count overflow are sticky until `INIT`. Increment
saturates before adding beyond the representable limit, invalidates the whole
record, and never wraps. Encoding rechecks all counters and metadata to reject
corrupted fields too. Signed inputs must be validated before uint conversion;
negative signed values are not valid work counts.

## Schema 1 codec and decoder contract

Emit all three pages through three simultaneous MRT outputs in the **same draw**.
The caller/capture manifest declares the attachment identity and page mapping.
Independent draws cannot establish a same-fragment record even with matching
camera/time labels. Use GL4.1-compatible RGBA32F attachments and raw RGBA float
readback with blending disabled. Preserve values directly: no normalization,
filtering, reconstruction, blending, gamma conversion, tone mapping or
intermediate RGBA16F/RGBA8 storage. Capture must verify actual attachment format,
dimensions, read target, completeness and producer identity, independently of
the option/configuration text.

| Page | R | G | B | A |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | primary_iterations | density_evaluations | secondary_visits | texture_evaluations |
| 1 | original_work | requested_work | selected_work | path_tag |
| 2 | schema = 1 | reason_tag | valid = 1 | reserved = 0 |

All counters, original_work, tags and schema fields are exact integers in the
closed range **0 to 16,777,215**, stored as binary32 float values. All integers
in this range are exactly representable. This deliberately excludes 16,777,216
so every accepted increment remains inside a fixed bounded codec domain.
`requested_work` and `selected_work` are finite, nonnegative binary32 continuous
budgets in the same numeric range, with fractional values preserved. They are
labels, not counters. The general tracer does not enforce requested ≤ original
or selected ≤ requested; detecting an unexpected adapter relationship is part
of the diagnostic. Derive an integer selected cap as `ceil(selected_work)` if
the adapter uses that rule; never call it executed work.

| path_tag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 NONE | No selected march/evaluation path yet; initialized budgets are zero |
| 1 ORIGINAL | Actual original body selected, including full/fallback paths |
| 2 ADAPTED | Actual adapted body selected |
| 3 FULL_TARGET | Explicit diagnostic adapted-body control at original target |

`reason_tag` is an adapter-declared exact uint; its complete mapping belongs in
the capture metadata. It may use existing shared policy reasons but the helper
has no Photon-specific meaning or constants. Unknown paths require a future
schema or an explicit invalid record rather than an invented interpretation.

For any overflow, invalid metadata or page outside 0/1/2, the encoder returns
**(-1, -1, -1, -1)**. An invalid trace emits that sentinel on every page. A
decoder must:

1. Require all three corresponding page pixels from the same draw/coordinates.
   Missing pages, unsupported attachments or failed reads are unknown, not zero.
2. Recognize twelve channels all equal to -1 as an invalid record, excluding it
   from valid work totals. Report invalid pixel counts separately.
3. Reject nonfinite values, partial sentinels, negative values, values above the
   bound and fractional counters/original_work/tags/schema/valid/reserved.
4. Require schema 1, valid 1, reserved 0 and path in 0..3. Budget fractions are
   legal; reason integers need the independently declared adapter mapping.
5. Retain requested/original/selected values separately from counts. Aggregate
   valid integer counts with a wide host integer and report coverage by path and
   reason. Never normalize to an image channel or silently clamp invalid values.

## Disabled baseline, units and quality

When `SHADERLOD_WORK_TRACE` is absent, every declaration/operation macro expands
to nothing, including argument evaluation. Counter storage, constants,
functions and codec do not appear in preprocessed ordinary shaders. Diagnostic
encoding/output declarations also need caller-side guards. This helper never
defines the option itself; it cannot enable diagnostics through a stage leak.
The production adapter and archive remain separately pinned by their owner.

Counts and budgets have work units declared by each adapter. This helper uses
no distance units. The existing shared policy uses radial camera-relative
distances in Minecraft blocks and centered transition widths; the adapter must
preserve those semantics and report its selected/fallback path. Tracing changes
no transition, sampler behavior, fallback, effect strength or quality setting.
Uninstrumented original Photon remains the performance baseline. Instrumented
diagnostics perturb compiler/register/output costs and are untimed evidence;
they cannot establish a production speedup or unchanged visual quality.

## Actionable finding: AO edge check misses tile-member inputs

**Historical quality acceptance blocker; source repair recorded below. Not an
observed driver failure.**
`shaderpacks/photon-lighting-rate/shaders/program/shaderlod_lighting_prepass.fsh`
lines 203–219 read the representative's four AO/depth taps; lines 301–303 reject
only their scalar AO spread. The other three full-resolution tile members do not
necessarily use those same reconstruction taps. Away from screen borders, the
actual union is **3×3**, rather than the representative's 2×2 subset.

With TAAU off, a representative full-resolution pixel center `2N+0.5` maps to
`half_res_pos=N-0.25`, `i=N-1`, `f=0.75`. Its right tile member `2N+1.5` maps to
`N+0.25`, `i=N`, `f=0.25`. Thus the right member reads column `N+1`, absent from
the representative. The upper member similarly adds row `N+1`. Geometry, normal,
material and lightmap continuity can all pass while these AO values change.

A concrete scalar counterexample is equal reconstruction depths, representative
four AO values all 1, and AO 0.2 in the next column. Representative spread is 0
and its reconstructed AO is 1; the right member's original reconstruction is
`0.75*1 + 0.25*0.2 = 0.8`. The current cache can remove that contact darkening.
This is an exact source/arithmetic counterexample, not a captured visual defect.
Near-screen edges, GLSL `ivec2` conversion truncates negative fractional values
toward zero, so a fixed unconditionally offset 3×3 fetch is also insufficiently
specified. Bounds must use actual reconstructed member neighborhoods.

Bounded proposed fix: derive each member's original AO base index using the same
upstream coordinate expression; check the complete union with texture-dimension
guards, finite valid inputs and the conservative spread threshold before shadows.
Preserve original representative AO/depth weighting and diffuse arithmetic. A
scalar regression should cover the formerly missed outer column/row, zero/equal
spread, threshold endpoints, first/last/odd viewport edges and invalid dimensions.
Any extra classifier fetch cost must be included in whole-frame measurements.
Root assigned this repair to the quality worker after this review; old source and
archive hashes must not silently remain qualification pins for a repaired version.

## Five causes and smallest useful corrections

### 1. Source mechanisms and evidence machinery expanded before cheap net-benefit rejection

The October5 spatial integration is the clearest example. `137095d` adds1,160 lines in six files; `967d1f0` adds3,433 lines across40 files. [Structural cost audit](../SPATIAL_COST_AUDIT.md) later identifies an extra full-screen pass, widened cache, duplicated classification and nominal94.9MiB/frame extra attachment output at the held4.98M-pixel resolution. Even full fallback retains enabled graph overhead. [Rejection pilot](../SPATIAL_REJECTION_PILOT.md) reports original15.4881ms/frame, private Off25.1078, and failed FULL113.5953; ADAPTIVE never launched. FULL is failed evidence, not an accepted causal cost comparison, and Off drift prevents precise attribution.

**Inference:** the construction order exposed the project to expensive negative discoveries after broad integration. This is not proof that every earlier line was unnecessary. Counterevidence: reusable policies, actual driver controls and retained negative evidence are useful; the pilot correctly stopped without weakening its sample threshold.

**Minimal correction:** before widening a new mechanism, use its existing original/full-cost/enabled consumer for one bounded net-cost/active-work screen. For today's human priority, port an existing mechanism/control path through one real tuple before adding architecture. Record which user outcome a helper unlocks and stop adding helpers once the consumer is sufficient. Do not revive this closed spatial trial.

### 2. Producer/consumer contract gaps repeatedly emerged only in real launches

[USER_LESSONS](../USER_LESSONS.md) names concrete agent omissions: Java compiled without refreshed dev resources, guessed newer API methods, direct-argv admission dropping NeoForge program argfiles, finite startup deadlines expiring across handoffs, Mixin helpers loaded from a reserved package, partial native option maps, authored GLSL checked instead of Iris serialization, and helper include guards omitted from expected option counts. These are distinct failures sharing a boundary problem: offline success was attached to a different artifact or shape from the actual consumer. Several are corroborated by current source entry points and raw manual-preview startup/results; the report does not independently replay every historical failure.

**Counterevidence:** current `dev_client.py`, saved-plan preflight and focused authentic-producer tests address several exact recurrences. More generic guards are not the default fix.

**Minimal correction:** every changed boundary gets one real saved producer example and the actual consumer invocation before runtime. Batch independent cheap failures. Generate deadline/producer/freeze/preflight/launch in one local operation after readiness, and separate source artifact acceptance from launcher release. Extend the existing checker/runner, preserving original failures; do not duplicate another framework or pretend static checks prove rendering.

### 3. Completion of a patch was confused with adoption by the active operation

The October11 lesson “A staged fix did not reach the active workflow” documents a reviewed rate patch and qualifier left outside the continuing agent's live Java and historical runners. Commits `e355f9a`, `1076f77` and `a31a5ac`, plus [finite caller guidance](../RENDERER_BRACKET_CONSUMER.md), show the repair/adoption chain. A queued or documented handoff was not deployment. **Counterevidence:** current BSL runtime review ties all main origins to an exact delivered JAR, observes DEV correction zero and real main correction progress; that is successful adoption evidence. Untracked files are preserved work, not proof of loss or duplication.

**Minimal correction:** finish each bounded integration with one exact normal-entrypoint receipt: source/resource inputs → produced artifact → selected caller → actual origin. Keep coherent scoped commits when the parent has integrated accepted files; never broadly add the2,396 untracked files or delete them. A workflow improvement counts only after its next real consumer uses it, or is clearly pending while runtime is paused.

### 4. Transferable concepts were sometimes replaced by rediscovery or a borrowed benefit claim

The October7 [active-cost audit](../REUSABLE_ACTIVE_COST_AUDIT_R1.md) had to correct its “new” atmospheric-liveness opportunity: `shaderlod_needs_atmosphere(depth)` already existed in older structural work. ## Current iteration policy — 2026-10-06

The human replaced exact performance qualification with quick sanity comparisons
because laptop thermals and shared resources vary. Record actual loaded pack,
revision, shader/LOD presets, fullscreen viewport, scene and available host/thermal
context. Keep comparisons short, inspect still/motion quality, and repeat only
when useful to a decision. Retain all raw results and identify uncertainty; no
rigid 3% stability, 20% gain or 1.5x throughput gate governs current development.
Do not rewrite historical qualified/failed benchmark results under this policy.

Source/build tests remain distinct from actual driver rendering. Initial pack
support requires successful in-world shader rendering; speed gain per pack can
follow. DH and PBR are required compatibility checks. Local macOS success does
not prove Windows/Linux behavior. Unsupported versions must retain original
behavior rather than infer support from a filename. Preserve selected shader
quality options when preparing adapter copies and when LOD is Off/Quality.

The detailed protocols below are retained methods, not mandatory prerequisites
for every current sanity check.

## Setup evidence

| Check | Required evidence | What it establishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Loader/build integration | Successful build/test command and output artifact | Java and build setup |
| Runtime dependencies | Pinned versions, artifact sources and hashes | Reproducible dependency selection |
| Client startup | Launch command and runtime log | Loader/mod startup |
| Selected pack under Iris | Selected pack, successful compilation and in-world scene | Working shader runtime on recorded hardware |
| DH installed | Mod loaded and actual distant terrain in a scene | DH render integration |
| DH absent | Iris/selected-pack client renders without DH | Optional dependency behavior |
| Initial LOD | Disabled/enabled comparison plus near/far/transition inspection | Observable first distance LOD behavior |
| Agent setup | Parse profiles/config, execute hook, validate local skill | Local infrastructure correctness |

A shader parser or lint pass is useful but does not substitute for shader
compilation on the Minecraft OpenGL driver. Report partial checks explicitly.
A setup pass need not prove the entire later optimization hypothesis.

## Performance proof

Use a repeatable scene with a fixed seed/save, coordinates, camera direction,
time/weather, resolution, render distance, resource pack, and selected-pack preset.
Record Minecraft/loader/Iris/Sodium/DH versions, selected-pack revision and patch,
GPU, driver, OS, Java, mod config, and every relevant shader option.

Warm up chunk loading, shader compilation, temporal effects, and GPU clocks.
Compare the same patched pack with LOD disabled versus enabled so unrelated
upstream changes do not enter the result. Keep DH absent for the first normal
terrain optimization proof; test DH as a separate compatibility/extension run.
Use repeated windows or interleaved runs to expose noise and drift.

Measure GPU frame time when tooling on that hardware permits it, with per-pass
or capture evidence for the modified effect. Record median and tail behavior,
measurement method, sample duration, and variability. FPS may diagnose total
frame behavior but is insufficient to attribute a GPU optimization. CPU/chunk
loading bottlenecks can hide the result.

Before the first performance decision, record the acceptance criterion with the
user in `docs/DECISIONS.md`. The illustrative 8 ms to 6 ms example in the idea
outline is a motivating example, not a frozen requirement. If gains are within
noise, investigate whether branching or changed samples actually reduce work
before adding more packaging.

## Visual and compatibility checks

Inspect near objects, transition bands, distant geometry, thin geometry,
reflections, water, moving camera, temporal accumulation, and hard material
boundaries for the effect changed. Capture the baseline and LOD view from the
same camera. Include debug LOD colors when useful; a debug overlay itself does
not prove that an expensive effect changes its workload.

For the current multi-pack scope, expand to DH terrain/water and the vanilla/DH depth boundary,
shader reloads, config reloads, unsupported selected-pack versions, Iris absence,
DH absence, and renderer version mismatches. Only promote a component set to
supported after its runtime behavior has been checked.

Keep raw logs/captures/worlds outside Git and link reproducible local paths or
summarized reports from the active goal. Never label a planned check as passed.

## Current experiment admission

Use the active goal's multi-pack/Fabric+NeoForge scope, not the older Photon-only
setup examples. No rigid 1.5x gate governs current sanity checks. Define the
current decision before spending runtime: source premise, exact candidate,
expected consuming observation, acceptable still/motion boundary and the early
original/control/enabled/original-return comparison. Charge intrinsic setup,
classification, sampling, reconstruction, binding and driver overhead. A faster
candidate than an artificially slow control does not establish original-relative
benefit. Preserve drift and failed/contaminated captures without causal precision.

probe; its passing result establishes only the listed static predicates. Use
actual `ControlCaptureReceipt` output separately for loaded pack/options and

or executed work. Consuming source/runtime evidence, avoided work, ordinary
still/motion quality, total-render benefit and compatibility require their own
observations. Historical plans/receipts can exercise checker regressions without
becoming admission for a new launch. Reuse qualified unchanged checks; do not

# Benchmark guide

For the local Asahi machine without a desktop, see [headless development](HEADLESS.md).
The maintained Linux ARM64 launcher selects its installed GPU-backed virtual
display when no display is explicitly selected; the native 2560×1600 viewport
and all normal benchmark guards remain required.

For the prepared RTX 2080 Ti Windows host, see [Windows benchmarking](WINDOWS_BENCHMARK.md).

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py baseline --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --output FRESH_BASELINE
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`baseline` renders the original pack with the main mod absent in the backed-up
authored save. After 120 seconds conditioning it captures three unchanged
20-second native windows, with the standard ownership, readiness, sample and
restoration checks. The report gives frame sample variance/SD (ms²/ms), and
separately variance/SD of the three window means and first-to-last drift.
These describe frame jitter and within-process variation, respectively; neither
is a confidence interval. Repeat in fresh processes to measure between-run
variation. Keep absent-mod baselines separate from the matched Master-Off
controls in optimization comparisons. Startup failure supplies no frame-time
measurement. `native-startup` remains a short original-only startup diagnostic.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

C02 is an explicitly labeled 2×2 bloom quality tradeoff, with Master-On native
controls; its scoped exception is documented in the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md#c02-experimental-bloom-shading-rate).

## Choose the check for the question

| Question | Maintained route | What it does not establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What inputs and candidates exist? | `discover`, then `plan` with selected inputs | Runtime compatibility or ownership |
| Does this change activate and recover? | `check` | Performance or visual equivalence |
| Is the idea worth more investigation? | `test`, then `report` | Broad workload/machine qualification |
| What does native do without ShaderLOD? | `baseline` | Installed-Off overhead by itself |
| Does it preserve motion or work across packs/hardware? | Candidate-specific protocols in the reference | Coverage of untested scenes, transitions or machines |

Before designing a new study, establish the user's intended decision: deep
workload performance, compatibility breadth, quality, or a quick screen. Reuse
the supported commands above. Put the chosen claim, comparator, coverage, useful
metrics, controls and budget in the existing experiment record. Record exclusions
and fallback separately; do not impose a universal repetition count or payback
horizon. Performance requires actual-window execution and valid output evidence,
not merely enabling a setting. Source changes do not inherit earlier timings.

## Records and milestone cleanup

Keep current work in STATUS, durable attempts/decisions in EXPERIMENTS, supported
procedures here and specialized routes in BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES. Extend the existing
candidate entry when adding a route; retire superseded wrappers only after checking
imports, tests and historical reproduction dependencies. Keep active experiments in
`dev/experiments`, reusable inputs/clients in `dependencies` and `run-workloads`,
and retained historical evidence in `experiment-evidence`. Do not move a pinned

After an investigation, preserve compact raw measurements, configuration/source

## Request example and path behavior

This 24-second example starts at the existing noDH shoreline player position.
It is an example, not an executed or quality-approved trajectory. Place it in
an ignored prepared runtime directory and use the same request bytes for all
pack arms. The first waypoint must match the prepared `control.json` position
and yaw/pitch within 0.05 blocks/0.1 degrees. Coordinates are **player feet**;
captured `mainCamera` coordinates include the actual interpolated eye height.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "label": "shoreline-motion-r1",
  "warmupSeconds": 30,
  "fps": 10,
  "pngCompressionLevel": 0,
  "waypoints": [
    {"seconds": 0,  "x": 240.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 680.5, "yaw": -180.0, "pitch": 3.0},
    {"seconds": 8,  "x": 244.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 668.5, "yaw": -165.0, "pitch": 5.0},
    {"seconds": 16, "x": 236.5, "y": 69.0, "z": 672.5, "yaw": -195.0, "pitch": 2.0},
    {"seconds": 24, "x": 240.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 680.5, "yaw": -180.0, "pitch": 3.0}
  ]
}
```

Labels accept 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. The source
is parsed to immutable records; exact raw source bytes and their SHA-256 are
retained. The original request is rehashed with bounded reads once each second
and at finalization. Changing it fails the session.

Waypoints number 2–32 and start at time zero. All values must be numeric and
finite. X/Z are within ±29,999,000, Y within ±2048, yaw within ±3600 and pitch
within ±90 degrees. Segment duration is at least 0.25 seconds; total duration is
20–30 seconds and total travel at most 512 blocks. The frame rate is an integer
1–10, and duration must end on a capture slot. Peak eased movement/rotation is
limited to 32 blocks/s and 90 degrees/s. Yaw is unwrapped along the shortest
arc; long intentional rotations need intermediate waypoints.

`pngCompressionLevel` is an optional integer 0 or 1, default **0**. It controls
only the independent Java PNG writer in this explicit quality session. Level 0
uses uncompressed zlib blocks for minimum compression work; level 1 selects
zlib's fast compression. Both preserve exactly the same 8-bit RGBA values.
No frame-rate substitution or global STB compression setting is used. New
requests/labels and loaded capture bytecode distinguish this writer from the
retained legacy `NativeImage.writeToFile` attempts.

## Output and bounds

All outputs go to
`<gameDirectory>/camera-quality/<fresh-UUID>/`. Prepared game directories under
`run-workloads/` are already ignored. Do not run against a tracked game
directory or add these generated files to Git. The output root must not be a
symbolic link and resolves directly inside the game directory. Labels and
request content never become paths. Filenames are fixed `request.json`,
`manifest.json` and generated `frame-NNNN.png`; the manifest uses a sibling
temporary file followed by replacement.

The 24-second example requests 241 slots, including start and end; the maximum
is 301. OpenGL readback is on the render thread immediately after the frame's
GUI pass. PNG writing/hashing uses one daemon writer with **one in-flight
image by default**, or two only when explicitly requested. Its executor queue
has a fixed capacity of one; image/callback leases enforce the separate 1–2
producer bound. The framebuffer is bounded to 4096×2160
pixels by area (about 34 MiB of RGBA source pixels). The fast writer streams one
`width*4+1` byte scanline plus a 256 KiB compressed chunk and 64 KiB file buffer;
it does not copy the full image into another array. Each PNG is limited to
64 MiB, enforced before writing each chunk. The sequence now has a fixed
**12 GiB PNG budget** with capacity reserved before the next capture, explicitly
approved by root for native lossless quality sequences. The cap is recorded in
the manifest. At 2976×1672, 201 level-0 RGBA frames need about 4.0 GB (3.73 GiB)
plus small PNG/manifest overhead. These bounds do not establish that the
requested 10 FPS capture rate will be achieved. Keep the requested rate; any
missed slots remain explicit rather than being silently reduced.

If a render misses a scheduled slot or the writer is still busy, that slot is
retained as `missed_render_slot` or `writer_backpressure`. The harness never
duplicates a later screenshot to fill missing motion. PNG write completion
returns to the client thread and records hash, size, UTC completion and write
wall time. The final manifest waits for every pending slot's own callback. At
30 seconds of draining, an unresolved callback records a timeout failure;
the manifest is also checkpointed after every successful write callback.
An unresolved writer remains explicit as `failed_waiting_for_png_callbacks`.
The session continues draining instead of finalizing/closing while a queued or
active image could still be owned. Root must inspect a genuine stuck writer;
timeout is not completed capture evidence. Normal finalization and owned-client
shutdown require zero pending leases, including images already closed whose
client callbacks are delayed.

Each captured checkpoint records actual rendered mainCamera position/yaw/pitch,
local player pose, motion tick/delta, planned/observed path seconds, actual
wall time, session render count, Iris source frame counter and frame-time
sources, the dev GPU frame ID, framebuffer size, world time/weather, actual
loaded pack, capture-boundary archive/options hashes and screenshot completion.
Encoding description, compression level, PNG bit depth/colour type and actual
NativeImage format are recorded for captured frames; skipped slots also record
the selected encoding/level. The manifest records the writer class SHA-256,
native integer byte order and image/disk bounds. File hashes are still computed
from the finished file on disk before callback success, not inferred from the
source image or an encoder's byte count.
GPU frame IDs may stay zero if the existing GPU timer is disabled; they are not
a GPU measurement here. Full loaded shader options, mod versions, initial/start/
end input snapshots, class bytecode identity, exact request/config and advancing
shader temporal inputs are retained in the manifest. Archive hashes are checked
at initial/start/end boundaries; loaded options/config/control are checked each
second. Mid-frame pack reloads are not permitted and need separate coverage.

Statuses distinguish `rejected_request`, `failed`, `incomplete_capture` and
`complete`. A completed sequence requires every requested slot's successful
write callback. Rejected or partial attempts are retained, not erased. Without
`cameraQualityOnly`, the harness restores its acquired player's original pose
when that same UUID remains present. It never stops another process by name.

## Isolated lossless PNG repair: source and standalone checks

`FastPngWriter` writes PNG RGBA8 with filter None and no interlace. It uses a
per-file `java.util.zip.Deflater(level, false)` for PNG's zlib stream, PNG chunk
CRC32 over type+data, big-endian dimensions/lengths, and fixed bounded buffers.
The implementation follows the [W3C PNG specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/png/)
for scanlines, zlib compression and chunk structure. No STB global or GL state
is accessed by the encoder. Existing files are refused with `CREATE_NEW`, and
partial failed outputs are retained.

Exact pinned-source inspection used the cached source archive
`/Users/pippo/.gradle/caches/neoformruntime/intermediate_results/sourcesAndCompiledWithNeoForge_0b59334a24bba2bc8765d4735bf44be048d0ff21_output.jar`:

- `NativeImage.java` source SHA-256:
  `7732dd3894faf6ed0928db8e519132b486cf263bfc0b49e15cb4a28e10027792`.
  The `(width,height,false)` constructor selects `Format.RGBA`;
  `getPixelRGBA(x,y)` reads `MemoryUtil.memGetInt(pixels + (x+y*width)*4)`
  and does not assert the render thread. Public pixel reads are therefore
  available to the owned image writer without reflection/private pointers.
- `Screenshot.java` source SHA-256:
  `5ec5a5ee36fb49977454a61ad552666d2b837a488352b83d4e5747843fb5ab43`.
  `takeScreenshot` constructs that RGBA image, calls the existing
  `downloadTexture(0,true)` and `flipY()`. That existing download forces alpha
  opaque. The repair preserves this screenshot/readback behavior exactly and
  does not perform another row flip or alpha transformation.

Native RGBA bytes on the little-endian M3 are returned as the integer
`0xAABBGGRR`, not ARGB. The writer emits its low-to-high bytes as R,G,B,A.
For a big-endian native integer, the session reverses the integer's bytes first;
that platform path is source reasoning, not tested host coverage. A non-RGBA
NativeImage is rejected explicitly. The retained legacy screenshot's IHDR also
confirms 2976×1672, 8-bit colour type 6 (RGBA), so no RGB-only assumption is used.

The optional immutable request field `maximumInFlightImages` now accepts integer

`CaptureWriteTracker` is pure synchronized lifecycle bookkeeping, independent
of Minecraft/GL. At most two monotonically identified slot leases exist. Each
advances through reserved readback, waiting writer, active write and awaiting
callback. The source image closes in the worker resource block before callback
delivery; only that slot's callback releases its pending capacity. Readback and
submission failures close any returned image and reject their own unsubmitted
lease. Submission succeeds before later metadata collection, so a metadata
failure cannot close an image already owned by the worker.

The executor has exactly one daemon thread and a physical queue of capacity 1.
No unbounded producer queue is used. A successful queue offer records its peak
even if the worker dequeues before the next client sample. Tracker snapshots
record pending/reserved-image/active/waiting/callback counts and peaks, slot IDs
and stages, accepted/rejected/settled counts and physical queue peak. Waiting
writer stage counts can include the first task starting its thread as well as
the queue; they are not substituted for physical queue size. Native pixel slots
are bounded by 2×4096×2160×4 = **70,778,880 bytes** (about 67.5 MiB), plus the
existing readback scratch row and one fixed encoder-buffer set. Reservation
counts conservatively cover readback; images closed before callback no longer
count as image slots, but still count as pending leases.

The manifest records the selected limit, maximum image-slot bytes, one-thread/
capacity-one policy, tracker class SHA-256 and current tracker/queue state.
Frames retain slot identity/hash/error plus state before readback, after
submission, after callback and at skipped slots. Added wall-clock diagnostics
separate `readback_wall_seconds`, `writer_queue_wait_seconds`,
`write_wall_seconds`, `writer_callback_delay_seconds` and
`image_lease_wall_seconds`. These are quality-harness diagnostics, not GPU
timings or a causal proof. Conservative 64 MiB disk reservation per pending slot
prevents two concurrent leases from overcommitting the fixed sequence cap.

Every failure drains all already submitted slots. A 30-second drain timeout
retains failed-waiting status and pending IDs instead of prematurely finalizing
or stopping the owned client. No new readback occurs while draining. Final
manifest and owned shutdown require every lease to settle, including closed
images awaiting callbacks. A genuine stuck I/O/callback requires root attention;
the harness does not free an image while a worker might still read it.
