# Development CPU and GPU timings

The development harness measures real OpenGL timer queries. FPS and CPU clocks
are not used to calculate GPU milliseconds. It is compiled only in `devClient`,
and the released ShaderLOD jar does not contain its mixins or query code.

## Scopes and backend

`game-render` begins at `GameRenderer.render` entry and ends at its return, while
a world is present. It includes world geometry, Iris rendering, DH rendering
inside that call, shader passes, and HUD drawing. It excludes buffer swap,
Minecraft's frame limiter, simulation, and rendering submitted outside that
method. This is GPU timeline elapsed time for completion of the marked command
sequence, not an isolated shader ALU occupancy or hardware utilization counter.
Driver scheduling and CPU command-starvation gaps can affect it.

Extended attribution adds the following pinned entrypoints. These are command
intervals, not mutually exclusive busy-time fractions:

| Scope | Actual boundary and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| `render-and-blit` | `Minecraft.runTick`: before `RenderSystem.clear` through just before `Window.updateDisplay`; includes render setup, GameRenderer, HUD and main-target screen blit; excludes swap, events and limiter. |
| `terrain/world/opaque+cutout` | Sodium 0.6.13 `drawChunkLayer(RenderType.solid(),...)` draws both SOLID and CUTOUT. The separate cutout/cutout-mipped calls are no-ops in this pinned implementation and are not measured. |
| `terrain/world/translucent` | Actual Sodium `drawChunkLayer(RenderType.translucent(),...)`; includes vanilla water and other translucent terrain. |
| `terrain-setup/world` | Sodium `setupTerrain`: visibility/culling, section preparation and any upload commands within the method. GPU elapsed includes command-starvation time during CPU preparation; this is not geometry draw busy time. |
| `terrain/shadow/...`, `terrain-setup/shadow` | Same entrypoints while the real `ShadowRenderer.ACTIVE` flag is set; separated from world terrain. |
| `dh/world/opaque`, `dh/world/translucent` | DH 3.3.3 inner `LodRenderer.renderTerrain(IDhTerrainRenderer, RenderBufferHandler, RenderParams, boolean, IProfilerWrapper)`: boolean true means opaque, false means transparent. Measures buffer lookup and real renderer delegation when buffers exist. This is the inner opaque flag, not the outer deferred flag. Transparent includes water and other DH transparency. |
| `dh-total/world/main`, `dh-total/world/deferred` | Entire DH `render` / `renderDeferred`, including render-list construction, setup, events, terrain calls and cleanup. These overlap DH draw scopes and must not be added to them. |
| `dh/shadow/...`, `dh-total/shadow/...` | DH calls while the same Iris shadow flag is active, if that workload invokes them. |
| `buffered-draws/world/opaque`, `.../general_transparent`, etc. | Real Iris `FullyBufferedMultiBufferSource.endBatchWithType(TransparencyType)` draws. Includes entity and block-entity batches, not exclusively individual entities. `remaining` measures its actual `endBatch()` flush. Shadow versions use the Iris shadow flag. |

Individual `EntityRenderDispatcher.render` callbacks mainly build buffered
vertices and are measured as CPU `entity-build/world` or `entity-build/shadow`.
They are not labeled as GPU entity draws. The corresponding GPU batch submission
is measured at the actual Iris flush entrypoints above. Empty enabled scopes can
legitimately yield zero or tiny query intervals; raw samples preserve this.

The pinned Iris 1.8.12 `CompositeRenderer.renderAll` debug groups identify actual
programs: `iris/deferred`, `iris/deferred1`, `iris/composite`, etc. Individual
passes include their compute work (if present), mipmap generation, bindings,
uniform updates, and fullscreen draw, up to the debug group's end. They measure
the real enabled passes, rather than assuming a numeric index always names the
same effect. `iris/shadow-map` measures `ShadowRenderer.renderShadows`; it is
shadow-map generation, separate from Photon shadow filtering. `iris/final`
measures `FinalPassRenderer.renderFinalPass`, including its copies/swaps.

The timer probes `GL_QUERY_COUNTER_BITS` for both `GL_TIMESTAMP` and
`GL_TIME_ELAPSED`; OpenGL 4.1 alone does not establish useful counter support.
The [Khronos specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_timer_query.txt)
allows zero counter bits, in which case no useful measurement exists. Runtime
logs record both values, GL version, renderer, and selected backend.

- With useful timestamps, pairs of `glQueryCounter` marks time frame, stage,
  and pass intervals in nanoseconds. Nested stages and passes are valid;
  `iris-stage/deferred`, etc. overlap their contained passes and must not be
  summed with them.
- With useful elapsed queries and zero useful timestamps, the fallback uses
  `GL_TIME_ELAPSED`. These queries cannot nest. Extended attribution rotates
  seven frame categories: `FRAME`, `IRIS`, `TERRAIN`, `DH_DRAW`, `DH_TOTAL`,
  `BUFFER_DRAWS`, `RENDER_AND_BLIT`. Only the selected category emits queries
  in that frame. For example, a DH-total query is active in a different frame
  from its nested opaque/transparent query. Each category gets one of every
  seven sampled render frames; statistics are interleaved estimates over a stable
  workload and cannot be added as a measured decomposition of one frame.
  `GpuTimers.samplingPolicy()` and the snapshot record the exact policy and
  selected category. Query stack collisions still skip a sample explicitly.
- Optional sparse cadence schedules GPU query work once every N runTick frames.
  N defaults to 1, preserving the original schedule. Categories advance by
  sampled-frame ordinal, so N=7 or N=16 cannot accidentally measure only one
  category. Unsampled frames issue no timer queries, query-result polls,
  capability probes, current-query state reads or timer error checks. Existing
  pending results are polled only when the next sampled frame arrives. CPU
  wall/thread clocks keep recording every frame independently.
- If neither target has useful bits, the overlay reports `GPU: unavailable`.
  Errors or 16 consecutive zero world-frame results disable timing with an
  explicit diagnostic. A GL error observed at frame end may originate from the
  renderer; the timer conservatively stops rather than displaying questionable
  results. Results still pending after 600 render frames also stop timing.

Nanosecond **units do not imply nanosecond precision**. ARB_timer_query issue 2
says granularity is implementation-dependent; issue 10 warns that tile-based
implementations can assign timings when the frame completes, nonlinearly and
depending on placement. These caveats matter on the Apple Metal/OpenGL driver.
A positive whole-render measurement establishes a useful aggregate GPU timeline
measurement, not that every tiny pass is individually resolved. A pass with
median zero is not proven free, cached, skipped or unimportant. In particular,
Photon's sky-map deferred program executes every frame in the pinned source;
a zero median does not establish that it was cached away.

Scope statistics export exact-zero count and minimum positive result (nullable
when none) as resolution diagnostics. The minimum positive result is not a
calibration of the driver's clock precision. Use whole-render and
render-and-blit deltas across matched real workloads as primary evidence;
per-pass/terrain/DH intervals are attribution clues with these limits. Do not
label `game-render minus sum(pass means)` as driver overhead or GPU busy time.
No synthetic workload was added to either comparison baseline, and no isolated
FBO calibration is claimed as executed.

## CPU wall and render-thread CPU

`CpuTimers` exports a separate stream using `System.nanoTime` for wall duration
and `ThreadMXBean.getCurrentThreadCpuTime` for the current Minecraft render
thread's consumed CPU time. The latter is enabled only when supported, and
unsupported values are null, not zero. These clocks are explicitly CPU data;
they are never substituted for GPU query results.

| CPU scope | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `run-tick` | Whole `Minecraft.runTick` entry/return: scheduled tasks, simulation, render, blit, swap/events, frame limiter, yield and post-frame bookkeeping. Excludes other work in Minecraft's outer run loop. |
| `game-render` | Same GameRenderer boundary as the GPU scope; includes development query maintenance and CPU marker overhead within that call. |
| `render-and-blit` | Render setup/clear through immediately before `Window.updateDisplay`. |
| `swap-and-events` | `Window.updateDisplay`, which includes buffer swap and event processing in the pinned runtime. A large wall/thread difference can reflect waiting or scheduling, without by itself proving a GPU bottleneck. |
| `frame-limiter` | `RenderSystem.limitDisplayFPS` when called. At the uncapped 260 setting Minecraft does not call this method, so the scope may be absent. |
| Terrain, terrain setup, DH draw/total, buffered-draw and Iris names | CPU submission/preparation intervals at the corresponding GPU boundaries, recorded every frame when layer CPU timing is enabled. |
| `dh-render-list/world`, `.../shadow` | Actual DH `RenderBufferHandler.buildRenderList`: CPU visibility/list preparation, nested inside DH-total. |
| `entity-build/world`, `.../shadow` | Actual `EntityRenderDispatcher.render`: vertex construction and related entity renderer work, possibly multiple invocations per frame. |
| `block-entity-build/world`, `.../shadow` | Actual Sodium public `renderBlockEntities` entrypoint, CPU only. |
| `sodium-command-fill/world`, `.../shadow` | Pinned private static `DefaultChunkRenderer.fillCommandBuffer` per region/pass: section iteration, visible-face decisions and native-memory writes assembling multi-draw arguments. No GPU query or new command caching. |
| `sodium-execute-batch/world`, `.../shadow` | Pinned private static `DefaultChunkRenderer.executeDrawBatch`: tessellation/VAO bind, actual multi-draw submission, and unbind/close. |
| `sodium-draw-submit/world`, `.../shadow` | Actual `GLRenderDevice.ImmediateDrawCommandList.multiDrawElementsBaseVertex`: reads current primitive/index/batch arguments and invokes `GL32C.nglMultiDrawElementsBaseVertex`. CPU wall/thread around the native submission, not completed GPU draw time. |

CPU parent and child intervals overlap. Do not sum `run-tick`, `game-render`,
terrain and DH-total. Likewise, an individual entity's invocation mean is not
the per-frame entity total: aggregate repeated samples by `frameId` before
computing a workload fraction. Current-thread CPU omits DH workers, integrated
server threads, driver worker threads and the GPU. Wall minus thread CPU is
unaccounted off-thread/wait/scheduling time, not proven GPU waiting. Marker
syscalls and instrumentation overhead are included where they occur; quantify
them with matched enabled/disabled instrumentation runs before small claims.

Sodium fill/execute/submit scopes run once per region and render pass; aggregate
their raw invocations by `frameId`. World versions include all world terrain
passes, not exclusively opaque terrain. `sodium-execute-batch` contains
`sodium-draw-submit`; compare them, but do not sum them. Both and command-fill
are nested inside the parent terrain CPU interval. Fill measures assembly;
native submission includes Java/native transition, GL driver work and any wait
inside the call. Wall minus thread CPU cannot distinguish a GPU fence wait from
other scheduling. These fine scopes add more clock calls and allocations than
coarse terrain timing, so run the documented `cpuLayerTiming=false` control
before claiming small assembly or submission improvements. No shader or mesh
work is skipped by this instrumentation.

Pinned bytecode acceptance: `DefaultChunkRenderer.render` invokes
`fillCommandBuffer` at bytecode offset 133 and `executeDrawBatch` at offset 211;
the immediate draw wrapper invokes the real native GL32C function at offset 37.
Strict mixins target those existing methods, whose names/signatures were
inspected from the locked Sodium jar. Compilation alone does not establish
that these new narrow hooks ran; verify positive invocation records in the owned
client before drawing an assembly-versus-driver conclusion.

## Asynchronous samples and statistics

Each scope owns twelve query slots. Results are first polled at least two render
frames after issuance, and fetched as unsigned 64-bit nanoseconds only when
`GL_QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE` is true. There is no `glFinish`, wait loop, immediate
query-result read, or synchronous timestamp read. A full query ring drops the
new sample instead of overwriting a pending result or stalling the renderer.
Elapsed queries already owned by another tool are respected by skipping the
colliding sample. Query names are deleted before Minecraft closes its GL window.
With sparse cadence, the next poll may be N frames later; availability still
gates result retrieval, never a wait. The existing 600-render-frame pending
timeout remains measured in real frames, and the interval is bounded at 1–60.

The HUD API `GpuTimers.summary()` describes `game-render` rolling arithmetic
mean, median, and nearest-rank p95 in milliseconds. Each scope retains up to
240 completed samples. `snapshot()` also reports sample count, lifetime count
since reset, ring drops, pending count, backend, and useful counter bits. No
samples produce NaN statistics and should be shown as warming rather than
serialized as normal JSON numbers.

`drainSamples()` returns completed `Sample(scope, milliseconds, frameId, epoch)`
records without touching OpenGL or waiting. A bounded queue keeps at most 8192
unconsumed results. Call it regularly during benchmark runs. `resetSamples()`
starts a new measurement epoch, clears statistics and completed results, and
discards pending query results issued under older epochs. This prevents baseline
GPU commands from entering the LOD measurement after a quality switch. All
methods are intended for the Minecraft render thread.

`GpuTimers.resetSamples()` also resets CPU history and measurement epoch.
`CpuTimers.drainSamples()` returns
`Sample(scope, wallMilliseconds, threadMilliseconds, frameId, epoch)`, separately
from GPU samples. The CPU queue retains at most 16384 unconsumed records and
reports queue drops. Open CPU scopes issued before a reset are discarded on
return without disturbing nested stack order. `CpuTimers.snapshot()` reports
per-scope wall mean/median/p95 and nullable thread CPU equivalents;
`CpuTimers.summary()` displays whole run-tick wall/thread means. CPU and GPU
frame IDs share the runTick index. Clock timing, ring behavior, rotation and
export shape have static/unit verification; real rendering hook application
still needs runtime validation for each added seam.

## Controls and evidence

Comparison clients enable timing by default. Other dev runs opt in with JVM
property `-Dshaderlod.dev.gpuTiming=true`. Set
`-Dshaderlod.dev.gpuPassTiming=false` for the lowest-overhead whole-render
benchmark: elapsed queries then measure every sampled world frame, with pass timing
disabled. Timestamp mode similarly disables pass marks. Use identical timing
settings for baseline and LOD phases. Timer queries themselves carry overhead;
serial A/B measurements should report the backend and pass-timing setting.

The default `-Dshaderlod.dev.gpuAttribution=true` selects the seven-category
schedule. `false` restores the earlier two-category FRAME/IRIS alternation.
`-Dshaderlod.dev.cpuTiming=false` disables all CPU marks;
`-Dshaderlod.dev.cpuLayerTiming=false` retains whole CPU frame/render/swap/limiter
clocks while disabling detailed CPU layers. For an instrumentation-off overhead
check disable both GPU and CPU timing. Keep overhead checks separate from actual
quality savings.

`-Dshaderlod.dev.gpuSampleInterval=16` schedules one GPU-query frame out of every
16; the default remains 1 for historical comparisons. The accepted range is
1–60 (out-of-range integers are clamped and malformed values fall back to 1,
with a log message). `samplingPolicy` includes cadence and polling policy;
snapshot adds `sampleInterval`, `scheduledSampledFrames`, and an `UNSAMPLED`
category on other frames. Scheduled frame count describes slots, not successful
results; use actual exported scope counts and ring drops to assess evidence.
At N=16 with seven-category attribution, each category is observed once every
112 frames. Consider frame-only sampling when collecting short sparse runs.

Query instrumentation itself may affect driver scheduling, tile flushes and
frame latency. A preliminary cloud/lower frame-only query run differed sharply
from a CPU-only run; that discrepancy is not yet established as a causal timer
effect without matched repetitions. The appropriate control is the same
scene/profile/resolution with CPU-only clocks, full-frequency queries and sparse
queries, repeated in alternating order. Sparse sampling reduces how often query
work occurs, but an individual query-bearing frame can still be perturbed by
its markers. Keep measured GPU values labeled as instrumented timeline durations;
do not turn CPU/FPS improvements from disabling queries into GPU milliseconds.
The exported absolute frame IDs allow CPU records to be compared between
query-bearing and other frames. Report cadence, counts and repeat variability.

Two concurrently rendering windows share the GPU, memory bandwidth, and driver
queues. Their numbers serve the visual preview and cannot establish a standalone
speedup. Benchmark a single warmed client with matched camera, render distance,
shader settings, resolution, DH cache, time, weather, and alternating quality
phases. Record raw samples, counts, median, mean, p95, and percent change. Keep
DH world generation and initial terrain uploads out of timed phases.

Static evidence: the pinned Iris bytecode has two `pushGroup` and three
`popGroup` call sites in `renderAll`, verified by `javap -p -c`. The strict
development mixin hooks these existing calls and preserves their behavior.
`./gradlew compileDevClientJava` verifies Java integration, not successful mixin
application, timer support, shader rendering, or GPU measurement. Runtime
validation belongs to the coordinator's owned client and is recorded with the

HUD statistics are refreshed four times a second to avoid sorting every pass's
history twice per rendered frame. The original-Photon baseline runs this harness

### Stronger no-op finding: MakeUp reflection budget uses the wrong denominator for opportunity

Current manifest budgets post-crossing refinements from **RAYMARCH_STEPS**, not from actual remaining refinements. Native `config.glsl` sets10. `water.glsl` starts `searchFlag=false`, iterates i=0..9, and sets searchFlag only after the current iteration's sampling. Therefore at least one iteration is coarse, leaving at most9 refinements. Balanced's minimum possible limit is ceil(10*.875)=9: it cannot stop any work, even in the far band. Near/intermediate limits only increase it. Generated Performance's minimum limit8 can save at most one iteration, and only if the first coarse iteration already finds the crossing; a crossing on iteration1 or later leaves≤8 refinements and saves none. The native loop can still run10 total iterations in those cases.

This is a static conclusion at native10, independent of unknown scene coverage. It does not imply lowering the guard/minimum is safe, nor authorize a new reflection algorithm or a retry of the closed trial. The newer cloud10→9/8 join is a distinct, more direct work opportunity.

## Family-specific source results

**Photon.** [Height/normal/parallax](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/photon/shaders/include/surface/water_normal.glsl:50)
uses three heights for the forward-difference normal. Source defaults are
`WATER_WAVE_ITERATIONS=3`, strength/frequency/persistence/lacunarity/speeds `1.00`,
waves/height variation/parallax enabled, caustics disabled. The normal therefore
spells 12 noise lookups before parallax: three heights times three phase noises
plus one envelope lookup. This is source call counting, not driver instruction
or cost evidence. Parallax has depth increment `1/4`, **not a hard four-iteration
cap**: its `while` tests the height and enabled height variation can exceed one.
Profiles Low/Medium disable parallax and caustics; High enables parallax; Ultra
also enables caustics. Native profile declarations do not establish loaded
options. Settings allow carrier frequency and lacunarity changes, including
non-increasing carrier sequences; a monotonic tail cannot be assumed globally.

Main water computes parallax then normal at
[translucent:466](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/photon/shaders/program/gbuffers_all_translucent.fsh:466).
Normal reaches direct lighting, GGX highlight, reflected rays and packed
refraction output (`:563`, `:647`, `:694`). Native water base roughness is `0.002`
in [material:24](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/photon/shaders/include/surface/material.glsl:24);
water texture highlights can increase it. Critically,
[specular:317](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/photon/shaders/include/lighting/specular_lighting.glsl:317)
excludes water from the stochastic rough-reflection branch: adding roughness to
the direct highlight alone would leave mirror-direction water SSR/sky behavior
unfiltered. Caustics in
[shadow:106](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/photon/shaders/program/shadow.fsh:106)
use the normal to refract light and compute derivative area ratios. A slope
variance substitution is not that spatial focusing calculation.

DH's raster water program writes the water classification and returns;
including the wave helper there is not a wave evaluation. Actual distant water
shading is [blend:374](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/photon/shaders/program/c1_blend_layers.fsh:374)
calling [distant_water:73](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/photon/shaders/include/misc/distant_water.glsl:73),
which evaluates the normal, direct highlight and reflected rays without the
main-water parallax call. Native asymmetries must be preserved, not replaced
with an invented requirement that every pass use identical normals. Existing
grazing attenuation is credited; it is not a screen-frequency or glint bound.

**Solas.** [Water normals](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/solas-shader/shaders/lib/water/waterNormals.glsl:1)

three and High/Ultra inherit that. Modes 1/2/3 use different channels,
frequencies, squaring and anisotropic coordinates. The normal offsets are added
in texture coordinates after division by 256, including for the different
noise-B scale; treating them as one ordinary world-height gradient is incorrect.
The computed Fresnel `normalStrength` has no effect on the final assignment:
the next line overwrites `newNormal` using `normalMap`. Do not credit the dead
assignment as a native grazing attenuation or new opportunity.

Both [main:231](../../dev/logs/mechanism-evaluation-r3/water-spectrum/sources/solas-shader/shaders/programs/gbuffers_water.glsl:231)

## New witnesses versus the carried foundation

The carried [water helper](../../shaderpacks/photon/shaders/include/shaderlod/water_lod.glsl)
already selects smaller literal iteration counts, distance tiers and optional
analytic gradients. Its prior loop specialization is credited. This handback
does not rename it A9 or repeat its runtime pilot.

1. Photon has carrier cycles `0.7`, `0.793333`, `0.899111` at default settings:
   wavelength grows by `1.5` while the coordinate multiplier grows by `1.7`.
   Squared sine expands to `3/8 + sin(p)/2 - cos(2p)/8`, adding second harmonics.
   Independent phase-noise UVs grow by `2.5`. There is no single iteration-number
   Nyquist cutoff; even a correct carrier cutoff must handle harmonics, warp,
   anisotropic pixel footprint and time. Reducing N=3 to N=2 using the carried
   normalization also scales **all kept amplitudes by 7/6**.
2. For height `H(x)=E(x) sum A_i g(phi_i(x))`, the derivative includes both
   `grad(E) sum A_i g` and the noise part of `grad(phi_i)`. The carried analytic
   helper omits both, and native normals use finite differences, not the
   infinitesimal derivative. A synthetic smooth noise witness gives full chain
   derivative `-6.146957` versus frozen-noise `-2.199115`. Central differencing
   independently checks the chain result. This is **not a sample of the native
   PNG, a measured slope error, or a rendered quality result**.
3. Equal first/second slope moments do not uniquely define a distribution or
   deterministic phase. Two synthetic distributions with mean zero and second
   moment `0.0001` differ by `450.616x` in mean upward Photon GGX **NDF only** at
   roughness `0.002`. This excludes finite sun integration, Fresnel, geometry
   terms and clamps; it is not a pixel-energy prediction. It refutes an exact
   moment-only equivalence claim while leaving approximate, workload-validated
   lobe models eligible. Reflection directions, normal-height correlation,
   refraction and caustic focusing need their own transfer checks.

[LEAN Mapping](https://userpages.cs.umbc.edu/olano/papers/lean/) supplies a useful
normal-distribution filtering precedent but its stated Ward/Blinn-Phong mapping
does not certify these pack-specific GGX, mirror and caustic paths. The author
page was opened during this audit; no paper performance number is transferred.
[GLSL 4.10, sections 8.9 and 8.10](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/specs/gl/GLSLangSpec.4.10.pdf)
also requires care with derivative availability in divergent flow. A future
footprint branch cannot freely keep implicit texture derivatives inside only
some lanes. Any explicit sampling normalization affects the control arm too.

`neoforge-1211-benchmark-v1`: the existing MC 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.253
benchmark-control harness, pinned Iris/Sodium from `dev/runtime.lock.json`,

adapt another loader, shader family or Minecraft version.

NeoForge 21.1.253 and the pinned Iris/Sodium JARs: three complete valid windows,
verified exact configuration restore, canonical world reset and zero remaining
owned processes. An earlier native version-gate failure also restored/released
automatically. A separate real Python process fixture covers interruption after
a completed capture and repeated recovery. Native DH/PBR compatibility, visual
equivalence, native crash recovery and Windows/WSL runtime remain unqualified.
The smoke is lifecycle evidence; it establishes no optimization benefit.

## Entry and preparation

First choose the existing loader/version/scene slot. If the authorized experiment
requires a canonical reset, use the existing [checkout](BENCHMARK_STORAGE.md)
command before this entry. Its eight-slot policy, staged recovery, APFS independent
copies, world fingerprints, 32 GiB reserve and 96 GiB workload limit still apply.
This caller reuses the selected slot; it creates no profile or world copies.
Reports must be outside the disposable slot. Do not reset a slot while a client or
an interrupted operation still owns it.

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py \
  --profile run-workloads/world-pool/neoforge-1211-coast/client \
  --pack /absolute/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /absolute/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --output dev/logs/my-authorized-run --suite smoke
```

The default is static preflight. It writes no report/profile, creates no client,
starts no build, and downloads nothing. It briefly uses and removes a tiny
control-file fixture required by the existing plan builder. It batches independent
input, pool receipt, source/compiled hook, runtime archive pin, literal mod metadata version, current build,
Gradle command, shader/options, mod and destination-capacity defects. The original
`check_experiment_plan.check_plan` remains the command/schema checker.

After fixing the actual inputs, the runtime owner uses the same command with
`--run`. This flag explicitly selects this **foreground** native timing protocol,
including focus and a 1920×1200 fullscreen viewport. It is not a background
launcher. Existing lane authority, quiet-window procedures and finite supervision
are still required; static preflight grants none of them. The protocol requires
a validated existing source/classes/resources receipt and always skips compile
and resource processing; `--already-built` remains accepted for old command lines.
A stale build must be repaired by its owner before this caller can run. The
authorized build owner can run the existing offline compile/resource producer
and establish a source-consistent, producer-backed build receipt; the caller
does not invent one. The native validation retained the prior receipt, required
unchanged sources across a successful offline producer, then replaced the shared
receipt only after checking its prior hash. The launch uses `--no-daemon` to avoid
leaving a newly created persistent Gradle process; reusable cache files remain.

The caller rechecks build/input identities immediately before launch, then uses
the existing `dev_client` supervisor and exact-client stop APIs. The small wrapper
records preparation inside the supervisor's actual runtime lock. A startup
handoff prevents the controller and preparation wrapper from racing on their
manifest. There is no scheduler, daemon or automatic retry.

Before expensive windows, live control acknowledgments must identify the owned
client, game directory, selected pack/pipeline, loaded version tuple (derived from the hashed JAR metadata, not distribution
release labels), requested
Iris option overrides, ready world/meshes and focused viewport. The installed ZIP
must still match the frozen input. A completed window requires matching request,
label and output directory; result/guard/before/after files; positive completed
frames; and valid positive timing samples when recording. Its runtime identities
and options must match the acknowledged binding. These joins do not prove GLSL
uniform consumption or visual equivalence. Existing scientific evaluation remains
separate; `smoke` never becomes an optimization performance claim.

## Durable operation and recovery

`operation.json` records the protocol/operation identity, report and profile
filesystem identities, exact configuration originals/backups and last owned
hashes, mutation intent/acknowledgment, process birth/argv proofs, command sequence,
completed capture hashes, cleanup intents and terminal state. The original
supervisor `session/owner.json` remains authoritative for client/launcher stopping.
The build receipt is retained once as `build-binding.json`; worlds and generated
source trees are not copied into the report.

Normal failure and Ctrl-C enter recovery using the reserved teardown interval.
Expected shutdown writes are acknowledged only when this live controller issues
shutdown from a recorded configuration checkpoint. Full storage checks and the
science deadline do not block recovery commands.

After an interrupted controller has exited, run:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py recover --output dev/logs/my-authorized-run
```

Recovery stops only clients proven by the saved supervisor API, retires only the
proven launcher, waits for the recorded supervisor to exit, then requires an
empty client census, free runtime lane and free save locks. It compares process
birth/argv proofs rather than acting on a reused PID. It refuses a replaced
profile/report root. Configuration restore uses the last recorded owned hash;
it never adopts current bytes after a crash, deletes untracked config files, or
overwrites another owner's changes. Every completed file restore is persisted.

`recover` never reruns a preparation, capture, analysis or completed comparison.
It can be repeated safely. If the controller disappeared during an unacknowledged
mutation, or files changed since their owned checkpoint, uncertain files and
backups remain and `recovery_conflicts` names them. The owner must resolve those
exact files using their recorded backup/provenance. A missing proof is a refusal,
not permission to guess. Terminal recovery is a no-op unless disposal is requested while its profile
identity still matches. A subsequent verified pool reset replaces that identity;
the old report remains historical evidence and cannot authorize changes to the
replacement profile.

## Storage at preparation, run and finalization

Preflight checks 32 GiB plus the declared report/profile allowances on their
actual destination filesystems. Launch uses the existing serialized admission
with a 512 MiB profile-growth forecast, including the 96 GiB workload limit; the
canonical supervisor independently retains its normal admission. No APFS savings
or reduced reserve are assumed.

The operation checks filesystem free bytes and individual console/supervisor/game
log sizes during waits at most once per second. Full metadata checks cover only
its explicit report and selected profile, with a 100,000-entry ceiling. They occur
outside timing windows, never as a broad historical scan. Defaults are 256 MiB per
report, 512 MiB profile growth, 64 MiB per active log and 256 MiB total capture PNGs
in the scoped roots. Generated Iris source export must be Off. A reached limit
stops the attempt and preserves evidence; it never truncates an active log or
silently deletes captures. These are cooperative guard limits, not OS quotas:
one producer burst, the bounded sample interval for full checks, and unrelated
filesystem activity can exceed them. They do not reserve space against other
owners or bound the sum of historical report roots.

| Storage class | Producer and handling |
| --- | --- |
| Canonical scenes, shared packs/mods and other owners' profiles | Protected inputs; no caller deletion or copying into reports. |
| Resettable world-pool slots and world/DH data | Existing pool checkout/reset owns reuse; no hardlinks to writable worlds. Running growth has a declared cap. |
| Generated shader/export fanout | Source export disabled for this protocol; existing exports remain protected and counted. |
| Capture/raw timing evidence | Completed exports hashed and retained. `.storage-keep` pins raw evidence. Missing/invalid exports never pass completion. |
| Text logs | Size checked during waits; retained on success/failure for diagnosis. No active truncation. |
| Preparation/configuration backups | Exact manifested redundant copies retire only after verified terminal restore. Unknown backups remain protected. |
| Shared Gradle/dependency/build caches | Retained reusable inputs; no cache deletion or install by this change. |
| Unknown or historical artifacts | Inventory/preview only; an extension/category or age grants no disposal authority. |

Successful terminal restoration automatically journals and removes only the
operation's exact redundant configuration and supervisor-preparation backup
files. Every original path and backup hash is verified before deletion; unknown
files and pinned trees remain. For a recovered operation, explicitly request the
same narrow finalization with:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py recover --output dev/logs/my-authorized-run \
  --dispose-backups
```

Raw quality/capture evidence is never automatically retired by this caller. The
existing explicit `run_storage.py prune-captures` policy still requires no clients,
14-day age, `.storage-keep` exclusions, a journal and first/middle/last samples.
It marks retired raw motion evidence as incomplete. Historical maintenance stays
with its authorized owner, and is not run globally at experiment finalization.

Accounting distinguishes logical file length, per-file allocated blocks and
actual destination free bytes. Allocated blocks are not exclusive APFS bytes;
clones/snapshots can share them. WSL filesystem free space does not establish
Windows VHDX host-volume reclamation; that host backing is explicitly unmeasured.
Terminal backup-disposal receipts include before/after actual free bytes and a
concurrency caveat, not a claimed APFS reclaim amount.

Focused fixtures exercise unknown-file preservation, changed/replaced roots,
backup and process identity refusals, request/capture completion, cooperative

## Minimal common policy, if the screen earns it

Keep projection and march implementation in small explicit pack hooks. The
common input is **projected full-relief displacement in current terrain raster
pixels**, a dimensionless screen-size quantity; distance remains radial

existing band's units. Near protection must fit inside the selected POM range:
the general 32/96-block example would protect all default Photon POM.

For a proposed hook, define local-tile displacement over normalized depth [0,1]

each component by tile scale. With that matrix `G`, estimate

range as a conservative local displacement estimate, not an unmeasured
per-material min/max. Reject nonfinite values, degenerate/ill-conditioned G,
back/grazing directions and unsafe atlas/tile data to stock work. The tangent
plane/local derivative assumption can fail on perspective discontinuities;
the guard is not a global geometric error proof. Existing lower-resolution
rendering needs a corresponding stricter raster-pixel threshold to bound

# ShaderLOD project overview

ShaderLOD targets general-purpose, configurable distance quality control across
shader packs. Photon is the first implementation and performance proof. The first platform is NeoForge with Iris required. Photon is the
explicit compatibility target, and DH is optional for the mod while included
in the development runtime for compatibility checks.

The initial distance proposal is full quality through 32 blocks, medium quality
through 96 blocks, and low quality beyond that. These are starting defaults,
not a measured optimum. Define distance in camera-relative block units and
use transition bands or stable dithering to avoid a visible moving ring.

## Development sequence

1. Establish a reproducible NeoForge client skeleton and compatible Iris,
   Sodium, Photon, and DH runtime. Add durable goal/team infrastructure and a
   small LOD foundation that can be inspected and tested.
2. Prove one distance-sensitive Photon effect works under Iris with DH absent.
   Compare the same scene with the change disabled and enabled; inspect both
   visual transitions and GPU execution time before expanding infrastructure.
3. Build the Photon MVP around several measured effects. Candidate effects are
   POM/material work, shadow filtering, and SSR. Add validated configuration
   transport and useful quality presets as evidence supports them.
4. Extend LOD to DH terrain/water/shadows and validate the vanilla/DH boundary.
   Keep DH optional and test both installed and absent configurations.

## Architecture boundaries

The NeoForge client mod owns config, loader/runtime detection, and integration
lifecycle. Photon owns explicit GLSL LOD logic through a pinned, maintained
patch or derivative. Iris provides the shader runtime. DH extends terrain
rendering and eventually needs dedicated integration checks.

A Java config file does not automatically become an Iris custom uniform.
Document and test the actual bridge before claiming the mod controls shader
quality live. Shader-pack options can support the first proof independently.
Do not expand into automatic rewriting of arbitrary shader packs during setup.

## Product direction clarified by the user

The intended product eventually supports many shaders through a common Iris LOD
protocol, per-effect configuration and explicit pack adapters. Configuration can
map options, units, budgets, compatibility and defaults. Each shader still needs
reviewed code that avoids effect work with distance; names or preset changes alone
do not establish that connection. Pin and verify adapters independently.

Renderer-specific CPU experiments remain secondary, optional components. They
must not become the product's main abstraction or change sunlight cadence to
manufacture results. No sunlight updates or shadow-map refreshes have been changed;
source cadence investigation only informs possible visibility reuse. Keep Photon
performance proof first and preserve the user's existing expansion gate.

## Initial risks

Distance branches may save little GPU work when neighboring pixels diverge.
Some effects cannot safely change samples or ray-march steps without changing
appearance or temporal stability. Loader and renderer versions must be
compatible as a set. Photon may require hardware/driver features unavailable
on the development Mac; record this as a runtime limit rather than calling
static source inspection a rendering pass.

The setup goal establishes an environment and evidence base. It does not
promise an FPS gain, freeze the product's final quality thresholds, or complete
the later Photon/DH MVP.

## Shared contracts, with pack-owned semantics

The common policy should consume a small set of facts an adapter can actually certify: projected support/footprint; current visible coverage; material frequency/roughness; effect contribution or remaining-integral bound; history validity/confidence; and pass/resource liveness. It returns a bounded work decision, not a global visual preset. Thresholds remain private policy controls and native choices remain available.

1. **Coordinate contract:** units, projection and jitter, viewport origin/size, exact sample centers, texture extents and depth encoding. Vanilla, DH, hand and translucent depth must be explicitly identified; do not compare raw depths from different projections.
2. **Surface contract:** material ID, geometric and shading normals, roughness, PBR channels, alpha/cutout coverage, motion/deformation provenance and whether a low-frequency component can be separated from specular/emission/transmission.
3. **Validity contract:** full producer epochs and resource identity; camera/viewport/projection changes; world/chunk uploads; resource-pack/material changes; sun/time/weather/light changes; animation and screen-space disocclusion. Conservative uncertainty executes the native path.
4. **Resource contract:** producer/consumer program names, actual texture identity and flip generation, storage format/range, sampler state, filter support and write/read lifetime. Reuse by texture ID alone is insufficient for ping-pong and DH.
5. **Error contract:** preserve low-frequency energy and important high-frequency cues. A contribution bound is distinct from an empirical confidence heuristic; only the former can certify a bounded skip. Unknown HDR/emissive radiance invalidates a claimed luminance bound.

Screen-space histories generally cannot prove correctness for waving foliage, animated water, emissive changes or moving shadows from camera matrices alone. A stable history is evidence of past agreement, not proof of unchanged current inputs. TAA/reconstruction must not be applied twice blindly: effect history, effect resolve, native TAA and motion rejection interact. [TAA survey](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/rtr/publication/yang2020survey/) explains accumulation/history validation; [SVGF](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/rtr/publication/schied2017spatiotemporal/) supplies a variance-aware reconstruction precedent, not a performance claim for these packs.

## Cost accounting and ranking method

Rank investment value using whole-frame opportunity, ordinary gameplay coverage, retained quality, transferability and integration burden. Evidence confidence is a separate axis; a cheap exact test may precede a larger speculative investment. All new cost shares are **unknown** unless explicitly backed below. Shader source tap counts are not executed instruction counts; reduced work area is not end-to-end gain.

For a single affected component, let `f` be its original fraction of frame time, `r` its residual cost ratio after optimization and `o` added cost as a fraction of original frame time. Under a fixed non-overlapping cost model, throughput factor is `1 / (1 - f(1-r) + o)`. A 20% throughput improvement requires at least one-sixth of original frame time removed net. For illustration only, cutting a 40% component in half with 3% overhead gives `1/(1-.20+.03)=1.205`; none of those input values is measured here. A perfectly removed 5% component gives only `1/.95≈1.053`.

CPU/GPU overlap and presentation make even that additive model conditional. After raster reduction, per-pixel work shares and hierarchy/resolve overhead change. Two methods removing the same shadow taps, rays or shaded pixels cannot have their claimed savings added. Measure each next mechanism against the accepted combined baseline while retaining faithful original-Off for the product denominator.

### A1. Native-TAAU fixed/dynamic resolution

**Algorithm and removed work.** Use a pack's existing integrated temporal upscaler to reduce actual opaque/translucent raster and explicitly scaled effect producers, while keeping output presentation and the native AA algorithm. This is **global per-frame fixed/dynamic internal resolution**, not local distance LOD. Start with one fixed rate; later frame-level error/footprint statistics can choose a global rate only with a complete scale-transition history contract. Local coarse shading or hardware VRS are different entries. CPU traversal, shadows, mesh work and full-size final/history passes do not automatically shrink. Source TAAU existence and actual GPU viewport/work reduction are separate proofs.

**Evidence/native baseline.** Photon already remaps vertices/clips raster under TAA+TAAU (`program/gbuffers_all_solid.vsh:159–169`, solid fragment `:228–234`, `c4_taa_exposure.fsh:313–360`, `dh_terrain.fsh:58–82`). Its historical gain is already in the project and cannot be counted as a new contribution. Bliss has explicit native TAAU (`lib/res_params.glsl:1–11`, `dimensions/all_solid.vsh:369–374`, `DH_solid.vsh:58–63`, `dimensions/composite5.fsh:317–360`). Actual Bliss `world0/composite5` includes **composite4** for min/max preparation, and `world0/composite6` includes **composite5** for TAA. Filename resemblance is not a program identity. Source ledger R1–R3 below.

**Contracts, costs and risks.** Current/output extents, all opaque/translucent/hand/DH projections, jitter units, texture bias, sample centers, history extents/age and native clipping all belong to the adapter. Retain full native work for AA-off or an unverified path; Bliss explicitly undefines upscaling without TAA and its AA-off output reads unscaled coordinates. Do not silently turn on TAA, replace FXAA, change stored native quality choices, or treat ordinary TAA as an upscaler. The product must expose the effective sampling change honestly through ShaderLOD policy. Resizing or scale changes need native-equivalent history reset/remap and bounded transition behavior. Foliage thin features, PBR relief, moving water, refraction, hand edges and DH transitions are the decisive risks. Preparation/reconstruction reads and full-size allocations can consume the saved work. Mac fragment/FBO paths suffice; cross-pack adapter burden remains substantial.

**Changed premise and falsifier.** This removes work across a larger native raster chain than the closed isolated AO/VL pilots and can reuse existing reconstruction rather than add a second resolver. It is still an approximation with unknown eligible cost share. At linear scale 0.85 the *eligible pixel count* falls 27.75%, not the total frame cost. Under the illustrative 2% total overhead assumption, a 20% throughput target would require that work to be at least about 67.3% of original frame time. First falsifier: one exact Bliss full-chain source/viewport/resource join, with native-AA-off refusal. If any consumer remains in incompatible coordinates, do not time it. If qualified, one fixed-rate original/candidate/return and a short disocclusion/foliage/water motion check decides continuation; no scale rescue search.

### A2. Replace repeated view-space reflection projection with projective traversal

**Algorithm/work.** Spend reflection work according to conservative or explicitly approximate contribution/footprint estimates, then use perspective-correct projected traversal where it reduces work. Inputs include Fresnel/specular weight, roughness, projected ray length and confidence; an uncertain bright reflected source prevents claiming a strict energy bound. A 2D DDA with depth intervals can avoid redundant pixel visits and repeated matrix projection/unprojection, but saving ALU alone may be weak if fetch latency dominates. Neither bottleneck is measured here. The first future candidate should change one mechanism at a time—e.g. bounded DDA at unchanged contribution policy—so a ray-budget cut and traversal rewrite are not conflated. Existing depth textures suffice; no new hierarchy/history/target/resolve is intrinsic. Keep native material gating, border/sky fallback and composition. [McGuire–Mara](https://jcgt.org/published/0003/04/04/paper.pdf) supplies the traversal method, not a ShaderLOD forecast.

**Evidence/native work.** BSL `lib/reflections/raytrace.glsl:31–104`, Complementary `materialMethods/reflections.glsl:34–133`, Solas `lib/pbr/raytracer.glsl:31–87`, and AstraLex `simpleReflections.glsl:1–77` contain repeated project/unproject loops. Photon `include/misc/raytracer.glsl:8–110` and Sildur water `:206–237` already step in projected space, weakening that transfer. Complementary WSR and some DH/Voxy paths bypass the target loop. BSL rough reflections retain a 5×5 post-hit radiance/alpha gather (`roughReflections.glsl:17–68`); traversal optimization cannot claim that cost. R4–R7 record checked sites.

**Contracts and quality.** Name the ray and depth spaces, interval/thickness/refinement rule, jitter, viewport and output position/radiance semantics. MC and DH inverse projections differ: use separate traversal layers or a proved common comparison space; raw nonlinear depth minima are invalid. New hit ordering and spacing change pixels even if geometric hit accuracy improves, so this is **approximate relative to native output**. Thin reflected foliage, grazing water, disocclusion, screen exits and PBR metal/rough lobes are the acceptance cases. Keep full native fallback where conventions or material support are unknown.

**Cost and decisive test.** Added clipping, reciprocal interpolation, interval tests and divergent loops may cost more. One-pixel traversal can visit more locations than the native cap of 30 iterations; a fixed maximum plus a justified stride/refinement policy is essential. Native active ray coverage/iteration distribution and total share are unknown. This has a materially better overhead premise than an added half-rate producer/resolve, but no measured win. Cheapest falsifier: actual loaded source/options show the retained scene bypasses SSR or rays end almost immediately. A single source-qualified bounded adapter would then compare hit masks/quality and total frame cost without a new hierarchy. A bad hit/energy change rejects it even if faster; a flat screen closes it without scene search.

### A3. Spend POM work by projected relief and material error

**Algorithm/work.** Allocate primary height-ray steps/refinement from atlas-local projected relief footprint and a declared error budget, keeping full work near, at grazing angles, near discontinuities and when inputs are ill-conditioned. Height-map samples and loop ALU disappear *before* the material producer evaluates them. Self-shadow or slope work is a separate live output, not automatically removable because the primary ray is coarse.

**Existing foundation/native gates.** Photon already distance-gates/fades POM and uses explicit gradients (`surface/parallax.glsl:12–93`, solid producer `:239–280`); BSL and Solas also fade, reject unsuitable normals/materials and stop at hits. Complementary `pomEffects.glsl:7–120` returns UV/depth used for slope normals and self-shadow; custom-material caller `:20–43` supplies native eligibility. The project's [private projected-POM candidate](../PROJECTED_MATERIAL_CANDIDATE.md) already implements a Jacobian-based primary-count policy while preserving selected quality, gradients and native equations. This report does not reinvent it or claim it rendered successfully. Its 0.25 output-pixel/0.5 texel nominal spacing bounds do **not** certify the same first intersection or bound specular/shadow error. Historical POM On/Off snapshots are prioritization only. R8–R10.

**Contracts and added costs.** Preserve height convention, atlas tile boundaries/animation, gradient provenance outside divergence, tangent view/light directions, native relief/fade and material normal/roughness/emission/SSS semantics. Shared policy should return a supported count/error decision; each adapter owns stepping and previous-hit/refinement semantics. Reject unknown PBR encoding, invalid Jacobian, large slope or alpha-cutout case to native work. Scalar projection/classification and divergence cost remain; a height min/max/cone structure is a different mechanism with update/memory costs (B17). Default-POM-off profiles have zero saving. DH coarse terrain has different representation and must keep native behavior rather than invent displaced DH surfaces.

**Quality/falsifier.** Tiny height displacement can still move a sharp metal glint or self-shadow. Require close/grazing brick and wood, camera translation, changing light, mip transitions and relevant material groups; full PBR coverage is broader than one relief screenshot. Mac GLSL and existing explicit gradients suffice. The cheapest falsifier is insufficient active multi-step material coverage under retained native options. If it is live, audit/reuse the existing private source candidate before writing another; one fixed candidate versus original decides useful quality and total cost. No POM-distance preset reduction is called LOD research progress.

### A4. Allocate receiver PCF/SSS samples without deleting shadow cues

**Algorithm/work.** Select a few coherent native sampling tiers according to projected penumbra/filter width, normal/material variation and allowed temporal uncertainty. Save receiver PCF or SSS taps while retaining full shadow generation, caster range, a visibility estimate, colored transmission and every native lighting consumer. Far distance may influence a budget; it never certifies “unshadowed” or “no SSS.” This is approximate.

**Source and native headroom.** BSL fixed nine-tap PCF (`shadows.glsl:103–132`) and conditional twelve-step SSS (`:225–260`) supply explicit seams; SSS is gated by ADVANCED_MATERIALS, enabled SSS and positive material in `forwardLighting.glsl:60–73`. Sildur `deferred.fsh:565–577` and AstraLex `shadows.glsl:200–258` supply other loops. Photon already adapts count by penumbra and exits after four uniform probes (`pcss.glsl:108–161`); Complementary already varies near-SSS samples (`mainLighting.glsl:264–277`); MakeUp/Solas already use small kernels. Those are credited native work, not new gains. R11–R13 and [adaptive-PCF primary chapter](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems2/part-ii-shading-lighting-and-shadows/chapter-17-efficient-soft-edged-shadows-using).

**Contract/cost.** Preserve kernel distribution/normalization, hardware comparison support, bias, color/depth-layer distinctions, SSS thickness and native TAA jitter. Evaluate derivatives before divergent decisions; native-AA-off gets a separately conservative policy or full fallback. No new target is intrinsically needed, which avoids the closed pilots' extra resolver, but classifier ALU, dynamic-loop specialization loss and incoherent lanes still cost. Actual active coverage and frame share are unknown, particularly for optional SSS. DH receivers can have different fallback lighting; keep them native until their exact seam is certified.

**Quality/falsifier.** Foliage backlight, fences, glass, caustics, moving sun and material highlights can expose unstable sample tiers. Prefer stable footprint-based transitions and preserve all low-frequency shadow energy; temporal averaging cannot excuse popping. First falsifier is the actual preprocessed option path showing only an already-cheap kernel or inactive SSS. Then a one-loop fixed-budget candidate must preserve still/motion cues and improve total cost. The native `2/-1/2` family result is not a cost estimate for this receiver subset.

### A5. Spend new AO/indirect rays only after effect-history validation

**Algorithm/work.** Move history eligibility before expensive AO/GI evaluation; confident pixels reuse an effect-specific estimate or request fewer fresh samples, while uncertain pixels run full native work and a bounded refresh schedule limits accumulated error. This changes executed horizon/ray searches, unlike blending a fully computed new result more heavily with history. It is approximate: identical receiver depth/normal does not prove unchanged off-pixel occluders or incident light.

**Evidence and scope.** Photon `d3_ao.fsh:154–175` computes AO first, then `:177–238` reprojects and blends history; native scale is already 0.5 and history age up to ten frames. Preserve its AO, ambient SSS and bent-normal XY channels and native reconstruction in `d4_deferred_shading.fsh:315–333,412–450`. Bliss optional SSRT at `indirect_lighting_effects.glsl:372–426` is gated at `dimensions/composite1.fsh:1203–1205`; source defaults select SSAO, not that GI path. R14–R15. The general policy can cover reflection/cloud histories only through separate effect contracts; final TAA color history is not interchangeable.

**Inputs/overhead.** Need named current/previous depth, geometry/shading normals, material/SSS identity, projections/jitter, motion or deformation provenance, history age/confidence and contributing-light/geometry change handling. Camera cut, new surface, world/dimension/resource/extent changes invalidate. Waving leaves, water, emissive animation and moving lights cannot use camera-only reprojection. More complete metadata/moments may require extra full-frame reads, targets and scarce DH/PBR sampler bindings. Fragment branches can still cost whole quads; global epoch invalidation may leave few useful hits during gameplay. Native effect resolve plus native TAA remains, so do not add another denoiser without accounting for it.

**Falsifier/acceptance.** First use existing source/history state to identify what *can* be validated without a new pass; missing normal/material/provenance makes a proposal a heuristic and must be labeled. The smallest useful future diagnostic is stable eligible fraction and complete added-resource budget, not a new general profiler. A single moving-occluder/torch/disocclusion case can reject the policy; periodic refresh alone does not repair persistent lag. Only a useful net total-frame result with native-AA-on and AA-off fallback earns broader adaptation. This is distinct from and does not reopen the BSL half-rate AO pilot.

### A6. Delete whole passes whose remaining operation is a certified identity

**Concrete algorithm/source.** At native `WORLD_BLUR=0`, Complementary R/U `program/composite3.glsl:127–161` reads colortex0 RGB by integer texel fetch and writes it unchanged. All blur/depth/DH/bloom-fog work and its mip request are within `WORLD_BLUR>0`. The three dimension wrappers remain active and properties contain no corresponding disable gate. Native bloom-fog placement moves to composite1 when blur is zero (`common.glsl:624–629`); no effect should be lost. Both original variants have identical inspected program/wrappers, but remain two pins. R16–R17.

**Why alpha is not a source refutation.** The fragment writes alpha=1, so this is not a generic RGBA identity. The pinned `pipelineSettings.glsl:2` declares **R11F_G11F_B10F**, which stores no alpha; finite representable RGB read/rewrite is the proposed identity. Actual attachment format, blend state and exceptional/NaN behavior are still acceptance gates. `colortex0Clear=true` supplies initialized current color. The following composite4 asks for its own colortex0 mips, which must stay attached to the correct logical current image.

**Graph contract/cost.** Disable the pass through an explicit option-and-pin-qualified enabled-pass graph, preserving Iris's normal subsequent alias/flip construction. Merely suppressing its draw while retaining the old flip would read stale storage. No compute companion or shader-side storage write exists for this zero branch. Trace physical main/alternate textures, first-frame/reload/resize clears, history consumers and later mip generation. Exact Iris constructor bytecode tests source validity before constructing a graphics pass (R18); this supports feasibility, not runtime parity. Source helper/default option off restores original behavior. No new pass, target, classifier or resolver is needed.

At 1920×1200, a 32-bit RGB read plus write is nominally **18,432,000 bytes per frame**, plus one fullscreen draw/setup. This is logical traffic, not measured DRAM traffic or a speedup. It likely has a smaller ceiling than A1–A5, but all rendered pixels participate and adapter cost is low. It does not establish a 20% strategy alone.

**Cheapest falsifier.** Effective native blur must already be zero. Verify original executes this draw; candidate removes it with no replacement blit/resolve, correct actual format/aliases and unchanged downstream logical contents. Under truly matched deterministic time, frame/jitter and history inputs, identity must persist every frame; temporal divergence is not acceptable proof of exactness. Separate-JVM screenshots with merely equal day/weather do not establish those inputs. Any unexplained mismatch rejects correctness. This is now a **correctness rider**, not the first cost experiment. A noisy flat instant-FPS screen cannot disprove a small saving: record “no detectable gain under this screen; magnitude unresolved,” without promoting it as progress toward the substantial target. The original copy-first proposal remains frozen in pre-review evidence.

### A7. Skip certified empty cloud regions while preserving native samples

**Algorithm/work.** Build conservative density-support bounds and skip runs of native sample indices whose density must be zero. This avoids repeated coverage/altitude calculations and possibly density reads; it does not reduce native nonzero sample count or move surviving samples. Exactness requires the bound to cover every native filter support, shape parameter and numerical threshold. A heuristic coarse noise probe with a large step is a different, approximate algorithm and cannot inherit this claim.

**Native baseline and evidence.** Photon cumulus `:36–107` already returns zero before expensive Worley erosion; `:274–344` skips lighting rays for empty samples and terminates low-transmittance rays. Its cloud producer/history already uses checkerboarding and reprojection. Bliss has coverage rejection and lower-detail lighting density (`volumetricClouds.glsl:182–222,343–395`). Thus the new opportunity is avoiding repeated *coarse* empty probes, not counting native skipped light rays again. Photon local-coverage mapping is radially warped, camera-relative and animated (`coverage_map.glsl:9–78`): a straight UV-grid walk is invalid. R19–R21.

**Resources/risks.** A fragment/FBO max hierarchy is Mac-feasible, but requires explicit non-averaging reduction, a buffer/sampler, pass ordering and a cheap conservative curved-map/altitude bound. Unknown cells stay occupied. Per-frame weather/wind/map-origin changes invalidate bounds; a static procedural-noise hierarchy requires conservative composition of all transformed octaves. Keep the native sample lattice, jitter and surviving accumulation order, native cloud depth/history and DH foreground termination. Include derivative/sampler semantics when introducing divergent skips. For a 2D R32F pyramid including base, storage is about `4WH×4/3` bytes per independent copy; extra ping-pong is additional.

**Decision.** The earlier altered-density result of about 0.408 ms against 15.372 ms is qualified negative prioritization evidence, not a bound on this different algorithm ([density decision](../DENSITY_DETAIL_COST_DECISION.md)). Sparse regions have cheap native rejection, dense regions terminate early, and checkerboard production already reduces invocation count. Bound construction/divergence may erase savings. First falsifier is an offline, source-faithful bound/tightness check over fixed representative inputs: if there are few long provably empty native-index runs or the bound is too expensive, stop. No fog/weather/scene search to rescue it. Retain as a consequential conditional investigation, not an implementation-ready promise; the feasibility reviewer preferred Tier B for precisely these unresolved premises.

### A8. Share one conservative depth hierarchy among genuinely expensive rays

**Algorithm/work.** Build explicit min/max depth levels once after relevant depth producers; each compatible consumer skips provably empty screen intervals and descends near overlap. Preserving native tested sample positions and hit predicates can certify skipped samples; changing traversal/horizon estimates is approximate. Driver is visibility plus projected ray support. Potential consumers are SSR, long contact rays and optional indirect rays, not every effect carrying a depth sampler.

**Evidence/native optimization.** A2 sites expose long SSR loops. Photon shadow SSRT `:20–98,128–164` already shortens/exits rays and chooses combined versus LOD depth; Sildur contact steps are sixteen; Bliss already samples quarter-resolution depth. Ordinary averaged mipmaps are not a conservative hierarchy. [Scalable Ambient Obscurance](https://research.nvidia.com/publication/2012-06_scalable-ambient-obscurance) is a depth-preprocessing precedent. AMD [SSSR](https://gpuopen.com/manuals/fidelityfx_sdk/techniques/stochastic-screen-space-reflections/) illustrates hierarchy/classification reuse, but its shipped compute/subgroup/DX12/Vulkan implementation is not a native Mac/Iris drop-in. R4–R7, R15 and R22.

**Contracts/cost.** Actual MC/DH projection, clear/far sentinels, depth precision/thickness, opaque/translucent/hand ownership and producer time must be compatible. A pre-water opaque hierarchy cannot automatically service later refractive depths. Current-frame rebuild avoids stale-history assumptions but costs raster passes/FBO traffic. RG32F full pyramid storage including base is about `8WH×4/3`, or 24.576 MB at 1920×1200 per independent copy; multiple domains/copies cost more. New texture reads/branch refinement, scratch allocation and sampler pressure must be paid once and assigned to every real consumer. A sole short four-/nine-/sixteen-sample kernel is a weak amortization premise.

**Falsifier and disposition.** Before allocating anything, identify two active substantial compatible consumers and an exact fragment-pass/resource layout. Reject if no common depth domain or native loops usually exit early; one especially expensive consumer could still justify it but requires actual cost evidence. Thin geometry, grazing rays and DH boundaries must survive. Benchmark full build plus all changed consumers only after that gate. This overlaps A2 and A5 rather than adding independent savings. Retained as deep reserve; both cost and feasibility reviews downgraded immediate priority.

### A9. Filter procedural water frequencies while preserving their appearance

**Algorithm/work.** Use projected derivatives and wave spectrum to omit unresolved high-frequency height/normal evaluations, transferring their slope variance into an adapter-specific filtered normal/specular model. Preserve resolved wave phase, large shape, flow and native water composition. This saves repeated procedural noise/Gerstner evaluations and optional water-parallax work, not generic PBR material samples. Approximate appearance preservation must be proved against the native BRDF.

**Evidence/native constraints.** Photon `water_normal.glsl:50–165` evaluates three heights for a normal, each with noise/Gerstner loops; consumers include main translucent water `:476`, shadow caustics `shadow.fsh:121` and distant water `:77`. Solas `waterNormals.glsl:1–64` has water-POM plus repeated heights; Bliss `waterBump.glsl:31–88` uses three multi-layer heights and already grows finite-difference span with distance. Photon also attenuates grazing detail. Credit this native filtering. R23–R25. [LEAN Mapping](https://userpages.cs.umbc.edu/olano/papers/lean/) motivates normal-distribution filtering; its particular models do not validate these packs' GGX/artistic highlights.

**Contract/cost/quality.** Small wave height does not imply small slope or glint error. Need octave amplitude/frequency/phase, screen footprint, covariance or a validated cheaper surrogate, native roughness/normal convention, wind/time and coherent main/shadow/DH consumers. Keep alpha/refraction/absorption and PBR reflection energy intact; shadow caustics may need separate native fallback. Added variance math, branch specialization, BRDF changes and shader size can erase a low native octave count's savings. No new history is intrinsic; optional lookup tables need their own memory/update budget. GL4.1 math/sampling is feasible, but cross-pack semantics are high burden.

**Falsifier.** Evaluate one fixed set of grazing water/glint and moving-camera conditions before speed: if residual variance cannot retain highlight energy/shape, reject without tuning away the cue. Then prove actual expensive procedural calls removed, with all remaining variance/reconstruction costs included. Prior distance-only octave/SSR cuts and bad glint controls cannot be relabeled as this new mechanism. Total water coverage/share remains unknown; no default all-pack gain promised.

### A10. Reuse cloud lighting within the same frame through an optical-depth field

**Algorithm/work.** Evaluate a light-space or volume field of density-integrated transmittance once, then sample it at many occupied primary cloud samples instead of launching nested sun/sky density rays. This targets a different cost from A7, which skips empty primary samples. Driver is spatial/light coherence and projected field resolution. Same-frame production avoids stale weather/history but spatial interpolation and changed quadrature are approximate.

**Evidence.** Photon cumulus `:314–325` traces separate sun and upward sky rays per occupied sample, with origin-dependent hash/jitter and nonlinear scattering downstream; Bliss cloud `:365–373` performs three lower-detail sun samples and other layer terms. Solas already uses cheaper lighting density, weakening transfer. R19–R21. The official [2015 real-time rendering course](https://advances.realtimerendering.com/s2015/) establishes volumetric-field precedent; the team did not treat an inaccessible large Nubis PDF as inspected algorithm evidence.

**Design obligations.** A single 2D sun column loses altitude-dependent optical depth; a 3D field or layered atlas costs more and still needs directional/phase and cross-layer semantics. Preserve separate sun/sky/ground contributions, native light motion, cloud coverage/weather, shell geometry and shadow/foreground/DH composition. Define a bounded field resolution and interpolation error; retain native sampling for uncertain edges/layers. Mac implementation would use raster-written 2D atlas/layer passes, not unavailable image stores/compute. Additional field writes/integration/texture reads, sampler slots, padding and update cost are substantial. At current checkerboard cloud rate, a whole volume can cost more than native visible rays.

**Falsifier/rank.** First count source-qualified occupied-sample nested work and compare with a concrete field update/sample budget at representative retained inputs. If preserving altitude/native terms makes the field larger than the actual queried domain, stop. Still/motion acceptance must retain silver linings, cross-layer shading and wind-driven edge behavior. This was added after independent Round 1 as a missing potentially high-impact mechanism; it remains a high-burden reserve, not a first prototype or an assumed 20% source.

A future diagnostic that changes only a generation subset while holding receiver **source** fixed remains coupled because receiver inputs/branches change. Preserve that limit instead of promising isolated timing. This reserve is source-backed as an integration question, not promoted on the reviewer’s inferred performance ceiling.

### Rejected or low-value formulations

- **Calculate both full and cheap results, then blend by distance.** Removes no expensive producer work. A blend is useful only when selection occurs before the saved operation or producer allocation actually changes.
- **Disable shadows/SSS/GI, lower native quality, or shorten distance and call it LOD.** A deliberately degraded cost diagnostic can identify a family; it is not a retained-quality product algorithm.
- **Repeat the closed half-AO or half-VL candidates with another scene/threshold/resolver tune.** The two actual null screens remain closed. A changed algorithm must name a different work/overhead premise.
- **Optimize inactive or compiler-dead features.** POM/SSS/GI/colored-light presence in source is not activation; a helper or a static sample-count expression is not a issued-instruction count. Hoisting code the compiler already hoists can extend live ranges and lose performance.
- **Camera/sun-only cache keys, old visible lists, unconditional cadence, or history confidence called exactness.** They omit geometry/task/resource/animation/light/off-pixel changes. Fast stale rendering fails acceptance.
- **Treat ordinary TAA, averaged mipmaps or a full-resolution discard mask as TAAU, conservative Hi-Z or hardware VRS.** The relevant data/work contracts differ.
- **Automatically narrow every target or deduplicate samplers by texture ID.** Pack phases, ping-pong suppliers, comparison samplers, HDR range and DH/PBR consumers can diverge. No blanket safe rewrite exists.
- **Claim a whole-frame percentage from taps, pixel area, bytes or a local microbenchmark.** Net work, active coverage, bottleneck and reconstruction change the denominator. A technically correct small saving may still miss the user’s objective.

### Cost discriminators and maintenance burden

No strict effect ceiling has been measured. Degraded feature/work-removal diagnostics may cheaply prioritize a family, but altered output can change fallback, later branching, temporal inputs and CPU/GPU overlap. Label that coupled scope; do not convert it into an isolated hard upper bound. A small result on one water-heavy scene does not establish a universal ceiling for other PBR/indoor/material workloads. A fixed universal 4–5% per-layer threshold is not justified by the evidence or the current flexible pack goal. Declare the useful decision signal relative to the retained controls/protocol before a test, then preserve inconclusive outcomes.

For A1, fixed global internal resolution is an explicit approximation even when AA selection is preserved.
